*** APB COMMUNITY ***   Very long review, but if you have the time, read it.        Some play this game for the design factor, social status and overall attention, to play while disregarding the Terms and Conditions, alot play to troll other players, many play for skill and respect from others in the community, some just play for fun in their free time, others may play none stop to accomplish a personal goal of theirs. I personally have been playing this game for many years, for countless hours, I've always been for skill based playing and personal goals rather than grasping for a dead communities attention. This game has more cons then pros, cons being such as cheaters, or people trolling constantly, bugs, ddosing, server failures, and technichal difficulites this game has always had since start, bad gms and a very debatable slacking company, constantly biting off more then they can chew. The pros of this game are very simple, it has potential, and the way to make players keep coming back even after they've completely lost hope in enjoying the game again. Over the years this game has improved adding many patches and more recently FairFight. A system to remove (ban) players accounts once found hard evidence of using methods against the Terms and Conditions. Although in the past years, cheaters most definitely made many quit the game because of unfair gaming, FairFight has given APB:R a small amount of hope again for a game that has no cheaters. Which will in definitely never happen, all games of all generes have cheaters, so for a free to play game to never have cheaters is very unrealistic and this community needs to realize that. To add to players wanting social status and attention, many players of this game want to feel wanted by people of a dead community, that most likely will never interact with in real life. This  game is full of emotinal dissasters with real life problems that take it out on the game and players. Such as having a large ego, or constantly begging for attention in awful ways sometimes hurting themselfs even more. In recent events, some go over the top and ban themselfs on purpose to get comments and likes on the FFBan list creating some type of "social status" and it screams attention ♥♥♥♥♥, FairFights list of cheaters they have caught and banned. Some simply get banned to not feel the need to play this game anymore. If you're emotionally unstable person, I personally would say don't play this game in general because over time you will be affected one way or another. This game is very easy to troll and make other players in the community rage, my advice is to play patentiantly and calmly and know when to quit because after all, it is just a game. Raging and playing APB:R is a setup for failure, resulting in even worse emotional state. Don't take anything serious and just have fun. If you're grinding towards personal goals, such as maxing out a weapon role, maxing out your characters level, or even grinding money for a legendary you really want. It will come over time, not over night. To the people who are maxing a weapon role, set short term goals, example, 100 pointman kills aday, adding up over time. Don't force yourself to play more then you should. Don't just quit grinding simply because of a player cheating, or someone better then you is constantly killing you, or even if someone is trolling you, DON'T QUIT. I'f you're in for the long run, time flys, you'll regret not grinding towards something greater, I know I have. In ending discussion, I recommend this game over all the cons. This game is unique and like no other, with plently of potential and a ton of things to grind towards in-game. You dont have to buy anything and can still grind and get everything they put out in-game. I will never quit liking this game, and will never regret playing this game. So to you user, try this game out, maybe you'll enjoy, maybe you won't. You'll never know until you try it.

Back when I was in middle school I had two close online friends who I played games with every night. We played the usual thing middle schoolers played like Call of Duty and some free to play games. There are mods for Modern Warfare (Not the COD game, but a conflict between China and U.S.A) with it's own campaign, mods that expand upon existing units and vastly expand the possibilities of the game, mods that feature the Eastern front (USSR vs. Germany), mods that feature the war in Africa, Italy, and Japan, and many, many, many more. This game is a thing of beauty.

The HECU soldiers in the original mod had deadly accuracy and split-second reaction times, causing firefights with them to feel extremely unfair. This has been fixed for the Steam release. Unfortunately, the soldiers are now too dumb, instead of being too smart. Sometimes they charge blindy at you with no sense of self-preservation, and other times they just stand there without even bothering to shoot back. This issue is even more noticeable with the Vortigaunts. I would like to see the AI tweaked a bit further.

I went into this game with a wary mindset. Hearing terrible things can do this. Yet, when I began to play I found myself immersed in an MMO quite unlike the handful I had played before. While some MMOs require grinding in many skill areas (i.e. runescape) this is not what i have experienced with The Elder Scrolls Online. While you do grind quests, I do not find myself running around killing every enemy in sight for the experience, nor do I find myself performing the same task over and over for hours on end to gain a few levels. The gameplay is quite enjoyable and different from previous Elder Scrolls games, using an ability-based skill sytem instead of the tiring combat I found in Skyrim (though I did enjoy getting creative in TES:V).
As far as the graphics go I am amazed at the awe-inspiring graphics for a game this size. Though I suspect the large download size has much to do with it, it is nonetheless a positive aspect of the game.
Performance wise the game has crashed several times due to what I assume to be connection issues (I live on a college campus so this is not unexpected), but they do not take away from the game. It runs smoothly, the framerate staying within a range of 10-15 fps away from 60 on high and ultra setting graphics (Though your experience may vary). I have not spent nearly as much time on this game as I plan to and only recently purchased it but I am highly satisifed with what I have experienced. For $60 this game offers hours of enthralling gameplay and what I hope to be a high replay value.

The story itself is quite good, assuming you get all the way to the "true" ending, although the barely concealed anti-war preachiness made me angry, like it always does.
The bottom line is that, if you're as obsessed with end-of-civilization stories like I am, you're likely to find this a treat. And besides, it's free! It's hard to go wrong with free.

I'm going to keep this short and sweet, and this game contains only one of those qualities: short. But this depends on how you play. Play it smart, you'll be playing for a while. Play it without thinking, and you're going to get bombed like I did Try #1. I didn't use the word "sweet" because you are trying to survive a soon-to-be harsh environment, and even if you do nothing wrong it can still blow up in your face (pun partially intended).
The game is very simple, but also very complex. Simple: survive. Complex: Rich story writing that lures you in first-hand to just what is happening, gritty black and white art that sometimes contains red highlights (I could just sit here and look at the art for hours), and finally: the story itself is molded completely by what perks you choose, and what you say and do.
What would I add? Gameplay is flawless and perfect, I just wish there was a gallery for seen art, as well as maybe a tracker/log of endings?

“I wonder if I've been changed in the night. Let me think. Was I the same when I got up this morning? I almost think I can remember feeling a little different. But if I'm not the same, the next question is 'Who in the world am I?' Ah, that's the great puzzle!”
― Lewis Carroll, Alice in Wonderland
The game is presented as a dialogue between the main heroine, Alice, and her friend, M. Hatter. Alice is presented as a narrator of the story(stories), while M. Hatter comments on some particular events which happen to Alice in her lucid, life-like dreams. In each dream Alice is different. She is shaped by the statistics you are able to customize (and by the decisions you make during your walkthrough). The game presents you with an opportunity to choose a preset Alice (default or "dark Alice",which even has her own art). The dialogue and the beginning of the game differ depending on the stats you choose.
At first you might think that the game is about plain survival, That's definitely not the case here. Of course, you are able to play this way, making choices according to your outlook. However, the "true" ending is hidden accurately, and it will take you a few playthroughs to get to the main idea of the game. And even then there will be unanswered questions left, the answers to which you will have to come up with yourself.
I would definitely recommend giving this game a try.
So many options! I'm greatly enjoying this game so far. and it's free!

A surprisingly replayable VN despite its short length, this game is atmospheric and very tense. You play as Alice in an apocalyptic dream, and although the basic narrative will stay the same, multiple playthroughs are encouraged in order to gain all the different endings and achievements. These playthroughs didn't feel like a chore, however, since I was naturally curious as to what the different choices would lead to, and how the stats affected your decisions (the fact that there's a stat barrier definitely helps, imo).
The narrative, however, isn't all that fleshed out. Although one could argue that mystery and intrigue is best developed through ambiguity and imagination, I would say that in this case, the sole redeeming factor is that it's inspired by Alice in Wonderland - a similarly open-ended story - because the plot doesn't really ... go anywhere.
Overall, a surprisingly entertaining game that will take up a bit of your time if you're a completionist, but worth at least a few playthroughs.

I've spent a good number of hours playing this game now and can safely say it is the best alien game released since the pant wetting experience the original AvP game arrived.
While a little slow at times, you really get a good feel of stalked constantly by the alien. The non scripted movement patterns keep you on your toes and the inability to kill it keeps you nervous at all times. Story is a little lacking, but that is understandable due to the fact the majority of the game is you wandering alone.
Save points are nicely placed throughout the game. If they were as close together as they are here on other games, you might ask why there wasn't just a save option built in - You would be wrong to ask that. Points might be 15 meters apart, but the TIME it takes to move between them is substantially longer than that of your average game. Several times I have been pinned down by the alien in the same area because it kept hearing noise and investigating. Truely pant wetting moments can be had, stuffed inside a locker, praying that the alien doenst open it and rip you out.
The crafting system is nicely done, universal parts placed in devices to build tools and weapons - though i must ask why a molotov cocktail requires a sensor module. The important thing to note is that you should never leave materials behind if you can avoid it - better to craft something and have it than leave things behind and wish you hadn't.
Start of the game is a little slow - its fairly obvious that you are safe from the alien until it pops out for the first time in predictable game fashion, though it does allow you the opportunity to get to grips with some of the other aspects first.
Pro's
+Good scare factor and tense moments - lets you really feel its a survival game
+Good range of items that can be cobbled together
+Graphics are stunning
+Sound is fantastically done - the thuds and bumps from the alien keep you tense
+The alien
Cons
-Sometimes feels a little slow, especially when being trapped by the alien
-Androids are just generally irritating.
-Backpack for some components could be larger
Overall, a fantastic addition to the alien franchise that really delivers the experience that ridley scott envisioned and gave us with the first alien film. You truely feel like you are alone and your character knows this too. Creative Assembly deserve a round of applause.

So another Call of Duty, I was very hesitant after Ghosts disappointed me so much. However after finishing the Singleplayer and playing a few hours in Multiplayer I find myself being pleasantly surprised. I found the Single player to be much more engaging than Ghosts and it was a bit longer too. I don’t know if it’s just me but I also found the game to be a little more difficult which is good. That could just be me though. The reviews I’ve seen seem to be a little harsh I think, If you take the time to try and fix it a little (It’s not that hard) then you will enjoy this game. Let me list a few Pros and Cons.

Pros:
-Nicer, new graphics (as expected)
-Still has the swift and fluid feel that COD always has.
-A little longer Single player than the last COD.
-Great pre-rendered scenes.
-More engaging story and characters you care about a bit more.
-New technology and a new world to see.
-Jet pack is a nice change.
-Good maps.
-Nice new weapons.
-New and different types of attachments and grenades etc.
-New kill streak rewards.
-Finally the pricing of a COD game isn’t insane for a long period and is already going on special.
Cons:
-Like all new COD games, it could still be longer. (Not as disappointing as Ghosts but still.)
-Of course no dedicated servers which once again sucks, I blame consoles for introducing that. COD Multiplayer was a lot better when dedicated servers existed.
-Lag, lag everywhere unless you can fix it. Without Vsync my game ran smooth but at certain parts it got incredibly choppy, I would still be getting between 70-90 frames a second and some severe vertical tearing. With Vsync on the game ran smooth and had no vertical tearing but there was input lag (The mouse wouldn’t be fast and precise, it would feel drifty). To fix this I used a program called Nvidia Inspector, with it you can select an option that sets the frame rate and fixes the input lag. After that it ran smoothly. It sets the frame rate to 58 rather than 60 which Vsync restricts it to.
-I don’t know if it’s just my imagination but I swear the choppiness seemed to precede some scripted scenes that have the first person animations. Then slowly disappeared as I got further away from them. Rather odd and because of it I always knew a scene like that was coming up.
-There are two graphics settings Cache sun shadow maps & Cache spot shadow maps. You would think that considering that these two settings take more RAM to use that they would do something. Nope, as far as I can tell they do absolutely nothing except take RAM and make it lag. So turn them both off.
-The Supersampling graphics setting seems to just be a lag switch too. (Perhaps intended for people running higher resolutions?)
-Sliding only works with ‘crouch’ not ‘toggle ‘crouch’. As I only use toggle crouch, a very important scene when you had to slide under a closing door got ruined because it told me to press ‘unbound’ to slide. (I must admit that one is a little bit of nitpicking)
-Unless I’m mistaking there is no throwing knife in Multiplayer which sucks because I love the throwing knife.
-Loading screens in the Single player can be rather long. They seem to have to load half way then finish when the pre-rendered scene is finished. (A setting the graphics is the main cause but having it on reduces the chance of hitching during the game.)
-Changing most graphics settings, with a few exceptions, requires the game to reload and with the long load screen time can be quite infuriating, especially with all the new options.
-The AutoDetect graphics seemed to think my computer had the power of a single potato.
There you have it, I might have missed a thing here and there but that’s all I can remember at the moment. So essentially what I’m saying is, the game is good. If you don’t have any problems with lag consider yourself lucky but if you do, try and fix it (google helps) before you complain.

Such an adorable and chill game, one of the best I've played. The $20 is totally worth it, and even if you wait till the game's finished, it'll stay the same price. So if you'd rather wait, there's no issue there!
The gameplay concept is super simple: Make corrals for slimes on your ranch, make gardens and Hen Hen coops to supply food for them, use the slime plorts to earn money. And when you have enough, you can unlock the lab to make devices to obtain resources for making cool stuff!
The world is amazing, and so beautiful. You start out in the Dry Reef, which is nice and perfect for getting the starting slimes and food. It won't be too long before you get Slime Keys from the Gordos scattered around the world to unlock the doors to the bigger and greater parts of the world, giving you access to new resources and slimes! It doesn't hurt to take the time to explore every inch of the world too, you never know where you might find a treasure pod!
There's very few dangers to the game, so if you're not a fan of super-stressful things, then this is a good game. All you have to worry about are Tarrs(slimes that ate one plort too many and turn hostile), feral slimes in certain areas(feed them or just run past them), and the Slime Sea, which is an instant KO if you fall into it. Just be careful around certain slimes too, they can hurt.
TLDR; If you'd like a simple game where you can chill out as a farmer on a weird, alien planet with the cutest creatures and beautiful scenery, then this is a great game for you!

First of all, it's not skyrim with multiplayer.
The textures are on par with if not worse than Skyrim's.
But hey, it's an MMO remember.
Don' get me wrong though I love how the game looks and it's similar to Skyrim.
It has first person combat, skyrim-like hud,  huge open world and voice acted quests.
As an ex-wow player i'll give you a little comparison:
-Graphic wise ESO is better than WoW, especially compared to the old zones like Elwynn forest etc.
-Quests are less boring in ESO because of nice voice acting and dialogue instead of just a small quest description.
-ESO's combat is great fun, especially in first person. It's less complex than WoW's high-level combat because there are just 6 ability slots you can use instead of dozens.
this isn't necessarily a bad thing though, it makes it easier to learn your attacks and takes less space on your screen which adds to immersion.
I haven't played very long yet so I can't say much about the PVP or PVE side of the game.
But I've heard wow's endgame PVE is better.
One thing I dislike about ESO this far is the fact that you'll have to save for quite some time to get a mount if you are not willing to buy one with real money, and also the lack of flying mounts in-game.
If you like wow, but wish it was a bit more immersive, simple, visually appealing or simply subscription free,
and/or if you are a fan of the elder scrolls' lore, this is your game.
WoW certainly has things that are better than in ESO right now, like some anim./emotes, diversity in armor, garrisons & raids..
(Do keep in mind that ESO is rather new compared to WoW, so i think it's kinda forgivable.)
I suggest you try both if you haven't already.
Both are good, But hey, I prefer to keep my €13 each month.

I went into this game with a wary mindset. Hearing terrible things can do this. Yet, when I began to play I found myself immersed in an MMO quite unlike the handful I had played before. While some MMOs require grinding in many skill areas (i.e. runescape) this is not what i have experienced with The Elder Scrolls Online. While you do grind quests, I do not find myself running around killing every enemy in sight for the experience, nor do I find myself performing the same task over and over for hours on end to gain a few levels. The gameplay is quite enjoyable and different from previous Elder Scrolls games, using an ability-based skill sytem instead of the tiring combat I found in Skyrim (though I did enjoy getting creative in TES:V).
As far as the graphics go I am amazed at the awe-inspiring graphics for a game this size. Though I suspect the large download size has much to do with it, it is nonetheless a positive aspect of the game.
Performance wise the game has crashed several times due to what I assume to be connection issues (I live on a college campus so this is not unexpected), but they do not take away from the game. It runs smoothly, the framerate staying within a range of 10-15 fps away from 60 on high and ultra setting graphics (Though your experience may vary). I have not spent nearly as much time on this game as I plan to and only recently purchased it but I am highly satisifed with what I have experienced. For $60 this game offers hours of enthralling gameplay and what I hope to be a high replay value.

Single Player:
Story spoiler:
It's Half-Life 1 how do you not know the story? Seriously? Fine. The story takes place at the Black Mesa Research Facility in New Mexico. You play as a theoretical physicist named "Gordon Freeman". You are heading off to your normal day of work and to nobody's surprise everything goes to hell. You are then sent throughout the Black Mesa Research Facility against both the U.S. Military and aliens alike, starting your adventure in the Sector C research labs, making your way through the offices of Black Mesa, the railway transits, hell that is known as the surface, and then the lambda complex. (To be Continued: Xen.) The game is basically one long "Get from Point A to Point B" with a bunch of puzzles, confusing level design (To new players), and some small boss battles along the way. But with the twist of the design forcing you to plot how you will play the game through, make you conserve your ammunition, and at some points question your mental sanity and wonder how the hell you're supposed to get through that room with 3 health and no armour left at all.
Level Design:
Can you really count "Level Design" since it's a remake? Damn straight you can. A lot of small and large changes were made to the game's levels. Even adding some new areas to the game. Some of the more noticeable changes are the scenery during the introductory tram ride, sector C laboratories, and the surface areas. It's just enough of a difference to keep the game going without making it feel like you're playing something that isn't Half-Life 1.
Downside in the level design: The "Vent maze" and the "Tram maze" were cut from the Steam version of the game as the developers said they don't feel they were made to their standards. A user has re-uploaded them from the mod version to work compatibly with the game on the Steam Workshop.(On a Rail Link) (We've got Hostiles Link)
Cutscenes:
The game has been given a much more dramatic feel with more voice actors, facial generation, and quite a few added little cutscenes and dialogue. For example in Half-Life 1: "What the hell are you still doing here? Get topside I hear troops are coming to rescue us." Almost every guard or hiding scientist has their little story to share when you find them. All the existing cutscenes in the game have been overhauled amazingly well, one of my favourite being the "Tentacle Scene" in the rocket firing chamber. which has seen some rather nice improvement in visuals and sounds from the mod version. Also the new voices for the HECU soldiers in the Steam version are a ton better than the original mod version's in my opinion.
Gameplay:
The game itself plays relatively similar to Half-Life 1 with added physics, but controls and moves as if it were Half-Life 2. You have the option in the "Black Mesa" section of the options menu to make your character always run, more like Half-Life 1 was. Holding sprint in either mode will make the player run significantly faster and play an animation on all weapons other than the crossbow and the satchel charge. The weapons all function the same. Satchels explode on command, grenades have their same insane movement influence in gravity.
Soundtrack:
Joel Nielson did an amazing job. Damn near perfect. (My personal favourite song being the first On a Rail segment) The soundtrack seems to fit amazing with the ambiance and progression of the game and it's story. The combat music is some of the better sides (Questionable Ethics #1 being an exceptional example) and fits very well into the Half-Life feel of the game. I truly imagine this mod would not have made it as far without his works added to the game.
Other:
The visuals, sound, and AI for the game have been extremely improved upon. (AKA HECU and scientists no longer run into grenades.) The visuals to the game are extreme. Quality you'd expect from an actual game studio. Albeit limited due to the source engine. The sound design is superb, meant for modern systems with surround sound providing an extremely immersive experience.
A few smaller new features were added to Black Mesa, such as an auto-crouch jump (This can be turned off from the "Black Mesa" section of the options menu). Which I can only feel was added solely because of DSP.
Multiplayer:
Note: The multiplayer is incomplete as of the current time this review was written and has some changes planned to be made. I will keep this section bound to core elements only.
Gameplay:
The game in multiplayer plays near parallel to Half-Life: Deathmatch's. And yes, crossbow bolts explode again. The multiplayer maps are being remade and modified to Black Mesa's play style and completely overhauled in visuals. It feels essentially like Half-Life Deathmatch but with an HD remake overlayed over it, but with changes in all the right places.
Levels: (?)
The multiplayer maps have to be downloaded from the Steam Workshop. If I have to guess this is so the developers can easily update a map without having to release an update for the entire game. As of the current time there are the following maps available from play officially from the BMS team: "dm_rocketfire, dm_tension, dm_office, dm_rail, dm_shipping, dm_boom, and dm_power". Adding up to seven maps currently.
A list of the good, and the bad:
Good:
- Complete Overhaul. Not much more needs to be said there.
- Balanced and fun to play multiplayer which will have more features in future updates
- Just holy hell that soundtrack.
- Plenty of little Easter eggs, inside jokes, and references to find everywhere.
- More improvements than the free mod version
Bad:
- The AI can still show it's typical for the source engine at times (Several times I've walked up to HECU Soldiers and they did not do anything but stare at me with their gun practically in my throat.)
- Being on Source, you can expect both good physics, but at the same time physics that will break at a moments notice and likely injure or damage the player.
- Just holy hell, the human assassins will swarm the player and just spray away with their guns, making it extremely difficult to kill them without explosives or wild gunfire before dying. (You have about 5-10 seconds on the medium difficulty before they kill you.)
My "Overall" rating would be ultimately a  9.4 out of 10.

I'm gonna be honest, I Like Dark Souls 1 a lot more than 2, that in no way means its a bad game. However when you have an established franchise at this point with Dark Souls 1 and Demons Souls, there are some things fans should expect and rely on.
Despite the flaws I have with this game, its still contending to be game of the year at this point for me (compared to whats being released). What you get in this game is a great set of customization through the usual armour/weapons the soul games provide and a slew of new items/spells to try out. The game also features the most bosses ever in any of the souls games. If you're still butt hurt about the PC port of Dark souls 1, then you'll be (fairly) happy to know they actually took more time on this port (60 FPS, Steam support, MUCH easier to summon/invade).
Now for the bad, the biggest gripe from the community is soul memory now playing a factor in connecting with others, while this sounds good on paper by preventing low levels invading low levels, it ultimately screws over people who co-op/are in covenants/pvp builds. As you reach higher soul memory at a low level, expect to meet people MUCH higher level or have no luck summoning.
PVP also needs to looked at better, invading as either blue or red covenants is a disaster due to having to duel in the arena for items to invade, put into perspective you have to win these fights AND hopefully the person you invade doesn’t disconnect/run into the boss door/is a hacker. Also have fun doing an extra step and waiting forever if you’re a blue sentinel. Since the arena also doesn’t have any range for soul memory or level, be prepared to be one shot quite often.
PVE for the most part in this game is not bad, however the imagination that was in Demons Souls and Dark souls 1 seems to be gone after you notice fighting a huge guy in Armour with (insert big weapon) for the 100th time. This game heavily relies too much on multiple enemies in a room  for bosses and in the game generally, this seems to lead to just annoying areas in the game rather than fun. Attack patterns in for enemies also seem wonky, especially getting hit when you see yourself roll away from an attack, this however could be contributed to the ADAP skill (which should have never been put in anyways).
Maybe I expected too much of this game, but it just seems that this was more of a cash grab and rode on  the popularity Dark Souls 1 accumulated. If you enjoyed Dark Souls 1, you'll still enjoy Dark souls 2, but expect to see some drastic changes that can change your previous Soul play styles due to frustration in the design and game play that should not be there.

Short but interesting, Bottom of the Well is an apocalyptic choose-your-own-adventure style visual novel told through the medium of an IM conversation. You are able to customize your version of Alice and the choices you make influence your starting items and chance of success in various scenarios. There are also minor (in some cases major!) story differences depending on the personality you give Alice which is a nice touch.
Don't expect to play through the game once and get the real ending. The game is meant to be played multiple times (think 10 or even more) to unveil it's secrets.
The story is well written and worth replaying, although there are negatives. You are often presented with an illusion of choice. Many options lead back into others while others are mearly fluff. There are also too few locations in my opinion. I suppose the developer wanted to keep the experience somewhat compact but once you get the hang of progression, the lack of choice becomes more evident.
But as a free visual novel, Bottom of the Well is definitely worth reading/playing as it is a unique experience with real moments of intrigue. I'd recommend it.

Overall rating: 7/10
Positive:
Very scary game. The scenery is amazing, good graphics and very detailed. Together with the high guality soundtrack and creepy sound effects it creates a very deep atmosphere. Reminded me alot of the first Dead Space game (but even more scary  - I quess mainly because its first person).
The low-fi sci-fi / retro look is a gift for every fan of the alien movie(s) and done very well, very nice design.
So if you don't have the computer to play on ultra settings, I recommend getting it for consoles. During the cutscenes it felt like watching an ALIEN movie.
When combining stealth and action tactics, its very intense. For example I used stealth to bypass an human patrol and reach an generator. Once I pushed the button, I ran away from the androids and the alien and then sneaked up to the human patrol blocking the pass to the exit. My motion tracker told me the alien was coming up behind me (because I was sprinting/running away from it) so I decided to use my gun to shoot some crew members (patrol) while the alien would deal with the rest of them as I just ran through guns blazing to get to the exit before the alien catches me - very close but it worked :)
Since they added androids and hostile crew members, the gameplay brings some changes as it would be pretty repetitive with just the alien. (Altho if you want that, I quess you can play the Nostromo DLC)
Negative:
The AI isn't good at all. Human enemies are pretty stupid. I walked up to two guys and hit one with the hammer (loud melee fight) and the other guy standing right in front of that fight (facing the other way) didn't notice anything.
Standing inside of >OPEN< vents, enemies passing by never noticed me so far.
The alien AI seemed pretty random, but not intelligent at all. Like: yes, you don't know what it's gonna do next - BUT not like it will actually do something, that makes sense. More like scripted random, not intelligent random :D
The alien will always be in the area around you. Yes they said that it could smell you and so be on the hunt for you, but that's not true. It's just SCRIPTED to be nearby. Like, even if it's just heading into the opposite direction of yours and you move on, it will suddenly be teleported into an vent exit nearby. So it's not hunting, just being teleported nearby by scripts. It would also often double and triple check a room instead of checking the other surrounding rooms.
So at those parts it turns from being scary to just being annoying - unless you have the flamethrower ;-)
But atleast it's random, so if you can forgive the very basic AI and live with the scripted stuff, it's still a damn good alien game.

Old school stealth game through and through. Think more along the lines of Thief rather than Hitman or Dishonored. It's got lovely lighting and shadow effects and the models and environments look nice considering it's age. I'm a sucker for stealth game which don't hold your hand.
I found this game overly frustrating and medicore. It's frustrating because its shadow system, which reminded me heavily of the early Thief games at first, doesn't work half the time. You think you are sitting in darkness but the bar to the bottom right thinks otherwise, and everyone nearby opens fire on you. You fire back, and then realise too late that any deaths or more than one alert fails the mission. Your handler makes damn sure you know about it too. So insta-fail missions are in there too. Considering this was Ubisoft, why am I not surprised; they still employ it today in Assassins Creed.
The game's worst sins are the terrible controls for jumping (a mixture of movement keys and left-shift) and the level design. Trying to grab onto a ledge from above is trial and error gameplay at its worst. Double jumping correctly requires you to face the higher ledge you want to reach so the guy can pull himself up onto it. I found myself quicksaving not just when I was in a tight spot surrounding patrolling guards, but everytime I needed to make a jump or grab a ledge below. Jumping from a pipe to a balcony for instance, is just as bad, if not worse. It really does feel like the game is punishing you for trying to move forwards.
Moving forwards is ALL you do in this game. I thought older games had massive levels that you could easily get lost in? Not this one. Every level is a corridor or a courtyard. No grand palaces/agency complexes with multiple covert entrances or opportunities to enter. Nope, always one, every time. And there are plenty of scripted moments too. Really, it feels far more like Call of Duty: Stealth Edition than any other stealth game I know.
The story? Bleugh. It's about as bland as they get. The Russians, the Chinese and some nuclear weapons. Nothing interesting comes out of those things unless you add James Bond. And Splinter Cell guy certainly doesn't feel like a James Bond game, especially when you mistakenly double jump to your demise in the last mission because the movement is so damn arbritary.
All in all, I'd say it's not worth playing. There are better stealth games out there than Splinter Cell, much less frustrating yet no less challenging or rewarding. Try Styx: Master of Shadows, or Dishonored on V.Hard using no powers and with the HUD off. Linearity is better suited for fast paced action gaming like shooters or puzzle-based platformers, not patient and meticulous stealth gameplay. In the Splinter Cell series alone, there are also better games - Chaos Theory I've heard is everyone's favourite entry and one of its strengths is the variety of ways in approaching missions and carrying out objectives.

Short:
While I enjoyed the first few hours, this game slowly becomes tedious, and has it's place now as the most theme-park oriented survival game I have ever played.
Long:
I bought this game on the advertised premise of "explore and exploit" and "A game of aerospace industry and interplanetary exploration", in short, this game really only lives up to the bare minimum of that description. While yes, you do explore, it feels more like "exploring" a grocery store, where I get a shopping list and go find what aisle it is in; Yes I "explored", but as in a store, it is predictable where everything will be and plentiful.
This game feels gauged in difficulty and complexity for a 10 year old and offers absolutely no challenge for any experienced gamer. Construction leaves -very- little room for any creativity, while the digging tool, and only tool you will get, seems to have recieved all the love by the devs, which makes this game feel more like an art and roleplay sim than an "aerospace industry game", as the only purpose for editing a terrain is almost entirely superficial. Building roads to resources is entirely pointless as all resource are depleted within 30 seconds, and roads take 20+ minutes.
Construction, is entirely node based and with vehicles, that makes them very limiting, especially with how few of modules you recieve. There is really only 3 variations of rover you can make, and only 2 variations on the ships that are actually useful.
What really was dissapointing is the overall lack of threat and survival in this game. If you die, you are carted comfortably straight back to your base via orbital drop, you are then given a massive beacon to your body were you can just walk back and grab your stuff and pick up where you left off. The biggest hurdle on survival was surviving a 30 second occassional storm, which required me sitting in a vehicle for 30 seconds. All other "hazards" were, don't go near the gas (which somehow kills me in an enviromental suit), dont fall off cliffs, don't go near the bad plants..
Graphics are excellent and inviting, but the interface is sloppy and uninformative. The text does not scale properly with the screen size and results in becoming pixelated and unreadable. No item has a description, and while I don't like hand holding in a game, it is helpful to know what exactly a "narrow mod" is in the description, which probably works out for the devs as blatantly putting that you will have to spend hours to unlock the dig tool attatchments that allw you to make pretty squiggles in the dirt, may prompt people to refund. These attatchments for your tool make up around 25% of all available research and addons, which, may be nice for an artsy sim, but is a mind-boggling decision for a game that advertises itself as a aerospace engineer game. Do you think Elon Musk will fly to mars to study how to effictively shovel dirt in a decorative manner? (actually, he may.)
The devs seemed to have put in more time building ship wreckage models than actual usable ships. You will get excited seeing some of the ship debris you can scavenge, huge chunks of ships and space stations, only to find out that you will not be able to use or unlock these at any time, and there seems to be no planned features for implementing bigger ships than the current dinky little shuttles.
The biggest, and final straw for me in this game where I just turned it off and dont plan to return until content triples is, I spent hours constructing a ship, and probably 20 minutes fueling it, only to find that I could have popped in one tank of gas and been good, cause apparently in a tiny little ship, a full tank can skip around the universe, planet to planet, without even putting a dent in the fuel reserves. Fuel could have been the key that made it entertaining, instead they punched the "easy mode" till it broke.
Pros -
Graphics are great, inviting
Awesome kids game
Cons -
Missing the giant "For children 8-14" sticker on the storepage (absolutely no challenge)
Dissappointing progression
Bad interface scaling and description
No reason to travel to other worlds
Very theme-park construction, flying setup
Little replayability
- Final -
This isn't a bad game, but it's setup like a childrens game. Apart from the blurry UI, which can be easily overlooked, this game had no bugs or issues that I could find in 10+ hours of gameplay. I do recommend that if you are looking for a challenging, space exploration game, that you completely avoid this. This game is basically a node-based construction game, where you can change map (planet). Resources are not challenging to get, no advanced logistic concerns, no serious enviromental hazards, the only survival resources are power and oxygen (oxygen is given in an unlimited supply in all vehicles and bases without any need to mine/extract it).

UPDATE: Nominated this game for the "Most Deserving of a Second Chance" award
I'm going to do my part in giving this game a thumbs up since it breaks my heart that two of my favorite recent stealth games have been given mixed reviews on Steam.
Dishonored 2 is a FANTASTIC game. We all know the problems with the performance and I certainly don't approve of how they handled the game's PC launch; however, now that I've installed the beta patch and begun playing it runs buttery smooth on my GTX 970, and the gameplay is absolutely sublime.
The biggest drawback of the game in my opinion is the story, honestly. Perhaps I just haven't gotten far enough in it yet, but there doesn't seem to be as much of a sense of revenge building up in the player throughout the game like in Dishonored 1. In the first game, you initially want revenge on Daud and the Lord Regent, but then you're betrayed and your lust for revenge gets even stronger. In this game, other than wanting revenge on Delilah, there isn't much that drives me.
However, what DOES drive me is the gameplay and level design. Both are expertly crafted, with power usage responsive and allowing for even more creative ways to deal with your opponents than was possible in Dishonored 1, which was already an enormous number. Add that on top of Emily's powers, and this game has a lot of replayability.
If it didn't have the initial performance issues, it would be a 10/10 from me. But alas, I'll have to knock one point off.
9/10 - DO BUY if you're into stealth games or anything like them

After the much hyped lead-up to the Isolation release, I remained somewhat sceptical until I first played it....on Hard. Within minutes, I was fully immersed in the Alien world, and it didn't let up.  Hands down one of the best games I have played in a long time. There has never been a game in which I was downright sweating as much as I was in Isolation. The music, in-game effects, level design and npc's all make for what is an intense survival horror experence.
Pros- Musical score and sound effects. Brilliant. Absolutely perfect for the experience while you play. The noise above, below and to the side of you as the alien hunts you is exhilarating.
Graphics - Ran on ultra settings on avg pc and no problems at all. Environment perfect and great
representation of the original  Alien movie.
Atmosphere - Hard pressed to find another game that makes me pause before of every corner, and listen to every noise and subtle effect the game produces. Outstanding
Achievement - Finally a game that makes you work damn hard for every save point! I realise this can be a negative for some people, but I found it to be a huge postiive.
Cons - Really only one negative, and that is maybe it leads you on too much,and gives you false hope, as you tend to run back and forth in the same areas rebooting systems etc.
Overall - The best game I have played this year...........10/10!

Overall rating: 7/10
Positive:
Very scary game. The scenery is amazing, good graphics and very detailed. Together with the high guality soundtrack and creepy sound effects it creates a very deep atmosphere. Reminded me alot of the first Dead Space game (but even more scary  - I quess mainly because its first person).
The low-fi sci-fi / retro look is a gift for every fan of the alien movie(s) and done very well, very nice design.
So if you don't have the computer to play on ultra settings, I recommend getting it for consoles. During the cutscenes it felt like watching an ALIEN movie.
When combining stealth and action tactics, its very intense. For example I used stealth to bypass an human patrol and reach an generator. Once I pushed the button, I ran away from the androids and the alien and then sneaked up to the human patrol blocking the pass to the exit. My motion tracker told me the alien was coming up behind me (because I was sprinting/running away from it) so I decided to use my gun to shoot some crew members (patrol) while the alien would deal with the rest of them as I just ran through guns blazing to get to the exit before the alien catches me - very close but it worked :)
Since they added androids and hostile crew members, the gameplay brings some changes as it would be pretty repetitive with just the alien. (Altho if you want that, I quess you can play the Nostromo DLC)
Negative:
The AI isn't good at all. Human enemies are pretty stupid. I walked up to two guys and hit one with the hammer (loud melee fight) and the other guy standing right in front of that fight (facing the other way) didn't notice anything.
Standing inside of >OPEN< vents, enemies passing by never noticed me so far.
The alien AI seemed pretty random, but not intelligent at all. Like: yes, you don't know what it's gonna do next - BUT not like it will actually do something, that makes sense. More like scripted random, not intelligent random :D
The alien will always be in the area around you. Yes they said that it could smell you and so be on the hunt for you, but that's not true. It's just SCRIPTED to be nearby. Like, even if it's just heading into the opposite direction of yours and you move on, it will suddenly be teleported into an vent exit nearby. So it's not hunting, just being teleported nearby by scripts. It would also often double and triple check a room instead of checking the other surrounding rooms.
So at those parts it turns from being scary to just being annoying - unless you have the flamethrower ;-)
But atleast it's random, so if you can forgive the very basic AI and live with the scripted stuff, it's still a damn good alien game.

I write this review as a massive RL fan and RLL fan, having put hundreds of hours into RLL 1 and 2.
RLL 1 and 2 were not perfect games and had a lot of bugs which were very frustrating. The biggest in my opinion, being the inevitable intercept if you attempted a cut out ball in RLL2 (I'm sure fans of the series know of what I speak). However they were very playable and very fun. The career mode in RLL2 was clearly modelled of FIFA and that is a good thing. The graphics weren't groundbreaking, but for the most part you could recognise the faces of the players.
Now, to RLL3. It is essentially a reskinned version of RLL2, with the intercept bug fixed. Unfortunately, a series of new, increasingly frustrating bugs emerged. All of the players have the same, unrecognisable beat up looking face (I think they resemble Sam Burgess), and the game is either frustratingly difficult or way too easy, depending on difficulty setting.
Defending: If you play it on pro or veteran, a high ball is undefendable, Your opponent will score almost every time. It has the illusion of you being able to compete for the ball, but you will almost never win.
If you are engaged in a one on one strip. You will lose. Nothing stops it.
You can not select your fullback to stop a line break. It will stick with the winger or whoever was initially in pursuit, despite your best button mashing efforts and yelling at the screen. If you do manage to use your fullback as a last resort, it's 50/50 as to whether he will make the tackle, or be stepped or run over the top of. There is no combatting this, despite attempting new strategies.
Your markers will appear to be on an onside position, however will occasionally suddenly become offside when you attempt a tackle, giving away a penalty. This happens too often.
Attacking: Rarely will you be able to produce a decent linebreak, and even rarer will you have anyone in support if you do.
The forwards do not go forward and are tackled imiediately when contact is made.
There is no longer an option to run with the dummy half as he is immediately tackled, so it's pointless.
Offloads? Negative. You'll pull one off as often as a rocking horse takes a dump. The controls are unresponsive. You can attempt a pass just before taking a hit up, but nothing will happen and you will be tackled with the ball. This allows almost no second phase play.
If you attempt to pass from the ground after winning the scrum, you will either throw it on the ground or it will be a forward pass to someone in the scrum. You have to physically carry the ball away from the scrum before risking a pass. By then, any chance of a decent backline play is gone.
The only way I can get field position is to attempt 40/20s. They are only possible during one half of the game when the wind is on your side, or don't try it. Even then, you will often over kick it and it will go out on the full, because the controls are very hit and miss.
Player management: You cannot select a goal kicker! It will choose one for you. Usually the playmaker, even if their kick stats are poor.
Career mode: Coaching. The FIFA model used so fluidly by RLL2 is gone. There's little in the way of choice and it seems way too "locked in" with your choices.
Career mode. Rookie superstar.  You can only control one player in this mode. His stats will only improve if he has his hands on the ball. So, you either spend the whole game trying to get into a position to receive the ball (and then get tackled immediately as I already described), or your player just won't improve. He also gets subbed real quick if he doesn't touch the ball. That is out of your control.
Rookie/Novie mode etc. Give the ball to any player and they will run the length of the field and score everytime. It becomes a borefest. There's no satisfying middle ground between too easy and impossibly hard.
In summary, I could put on RLL 2 and play all day (spent many a hungover Saturday doing just that). This game, I struggle to finish more than 2 games, and that's after several rage quits. I keep coming back to it every month or so hoping for a different experience, but I get frustrated and bored just as quickly.
Give this game a try simply because there's no other Rugby League video game franchises, but prepare to be frustrated.

Anyway --- top game, been a year and still loving it -- 61 hours now. If anyone still reads this hit me up and let's get some online going.

It's free, and that's the first thing you need to know, but the second is that this is a genuine bit of writing-driven hypnotic cleverness. The music and art are both on point, and the story is so profoundly aware of itself that all its gameified elements backfeed into the plot, get shout-outs in the text, and and genuinely lift this kind of storytelling above the static, linear progression you'd see in a really good novel.
Bottom of the Well is a choose-your-own-adventure in the old Joe Denver's Lone Wolf sense, with stats and equipment and companions all tracked. It's also one in which decision-making is guided primarily by your stats, and secondarily by common sense. I built a hulking musclebeast of an Alice and sent it rampaging through the nuclear wasteland, tanking incredible amounts of radiation and going head-on with every encounter it met. It survived, but learned nothing about the circular dream it was trapped in, and eventually it comitted suicide of its own will to reset the scenario.
By the way: this game is chilling. It's not exceptionally dark, but every little bit of inhumanity in it is very nuanced by the characters and tone, and all of them *hurt* just a little to read. If you're looking for something happy to play, this is not that. If you're looking for the kind of story that you routinely survive, this is not that either.
There's a hidden ending in this game, by the way. A final rabbithole to descend, although I haven't found it in my hour-and-change of getting bombed and then dying. I haven't seen any walkthroughs of it online, so for the time being it is still a special thing; a hidden thing. A bit of narrative that you could find that few other people have seen.
Anyway Red Nettle, the studio that produced this, has created something fey and unsettling. Here's hoping that they can follow it up with something just as clever.

The Bottom of the Well was created with the game engine, Unity by Red Nettle
.
First off, let me give you a slight description of the game, without giving spoilers(as I likely can't). In The Bottom of the Well, you play as Alice who has just had an unsettingly life-like dream about the end of the world. You can kind of call it Alice in Wonderland, but there's endless possibilities for the paths she can take. Even though it's multiple choice, and a visual novel, you are allowed to customize your 'Alice', if you so like, but RedNettle does recommend you to use the 'Default Alice' in your first try. But I've played RPG's before, so I headed straight for the customization, because that's the best part of RPG's!(well for me at least).
You'll immediately start talking to your friend online, called "Mad H.", quite the punny guy in my opinion. With that, you won't be able to choose what Alice types, it's much like the game 'Emily is Away', but you are allowed to choose how Alice answers, just maybe not in your preferred words.
There was however some minor Syntax, Grammar, Spelling of words and use of words issues, but it wouldn't bother most. It's a good game if you're into some visual novel games, and even though it may only take you 20 minutes to finish, if even that long, I say for a Free-To-Play game on steam, I'd definitely play this again(to see how it ends with a different 'Alice') and pay for it!
What makes this game even more brilliant, is the fact that it's so small, 60Mb for a game is very rare to find in our modern era, and the graphics isn't bad either. I would've liked some extra visuals when the scene changes, just a little beauty for the eye.
All-in-all it's a great game, with excellent qualities and minor flaws that can be fixed.

The Bottom of the Well is a text based story telling game, it recaps the dream of a young girl through her conversation with a friend on a messaging site. The girl explains that she had a very lucid dream about an apocalypse and begins to recap what she did in the dream.The story that the girl tells changes based on your decisions, sort of like a choose your own adventure book, you also get to choose what items you want to take with you on your adventure that could help you later on. The game uses the player influenced decision well and has very descriptive actions that the girl takes based on them, they also make sense and always provide the player with another interesting peice of information about this girls dream. The game offers a variety of ways to direct the story and you can spend ages picking combos of decisions until you get a ending that you are happy with, this is great as it allows replayablity and always tuants the player to do better or try a different approach. This is a great game to pick up if you enjoy choose your own adventure type books and is a fun little thing to do to pass some time.

You might think that a game where all you can do is drive around in a virtual truck can't possibly be fun or engaging whatsoever - but that's where you're wrong, kiddo!
This is not only a game with a creative community, the developers are also churning out new updates that enrich the game's experience and they actually listen to their player base.
You can choose a more relaxed playing style with mouse and keyboard or go for the hardcore simulation experience with steering wheel, shifter, pedals and IR tracking, because the game supports many types of controllers.
The visuals are stunning, nothing I've ever seen in a sim, and the map is constantly expanding. The AI sometimes lacks common sense, but more often than not it anticipates your behavior and acts accordingly.
I would recommend this game to anyone, be it someone who just wants a relaxed trucking experience driving through Europe's ever changing scenery while listening to his favourite songs on the radio or someone who craves the challenge of a realistic trucking sim.
I nominated this game for the "The world is grim enough lets just all get along" award, notwithstanding occasional road rage, for its peaceful and non-violent atmosphere.
Simply addictive at first, i always come back for a relaxed drive from time to time. Ever present in my library.

Wonderfully recreation of Half-Life.
Think Half-Life with the engine of Half-Life 2. It's HL better than you remember; I felt like I was playing HL1 for the first time again.
It has the same story as HL1 but beyond that everything has been updated. New textures on EVERYTHING, new voice acting, new scripted events, new ENGINE.
The new textures make gameplay more immersive and the people look more like, well, people. The bullsquid is incredibly terrifying now. The voice acting has been redone and some new dialogue can be heard, especially from the new female scientists (I guess the EO complaints finally caught up with Lambda.)
There are new scripted events for enemy intros that really show off all the work the Crowbar Collective has put into this game. Most levels have been modified in small ways to use puzzle mechanics from 2HL2. Anyone who is a fan of the HL series will enjoy playing game as we wait for the next installmant in the HL franchise.
Pros:
-New Engine!
-HL2 mechanics-set enemies on fire, throw back grenades, crawling zombies
-New textures for EVERYTHING
-Voice acting redone and more dialogue from NPCs, female scientists.
-New enemy intros, attack styles, and sounds
-Most levels updated to feature puzzle mechanics from HL2
-Amazing gameplay!
Cons:
-As of writing this the entire game has not been completed yet; Xen levels not released.
-Some of the levels have ledges big enough to walk around/skip fights i.e. Surface Tension
-On the level "Surface Tension" if you travel to the sublevel 'Ordnance Exterior', leave and return you can be stuck in a loop of gameover explosions. Can set you back if you don't save.
-Enemy AI seems more like NPCs always know where you are even-through walls. i.e. Tanks and Helicopters are always aimed and shooting at you even inside buildings.
Even if there is no xen campaign it's a great remake,20€ it's the right price for this game,if you enjoyed half life 1 you shuold buy this

Early Access/Pre Zen Update
11hrs for £15 (so far).
Gameplay wise it hasn't changed too much from Half Life 1. So if you liked the original, chances are you'll like this.
There's been a few changes in level designs and I think the weapons have been slightly rebalanced, so don't expect a complete carbon copy of the original. Saying that, I liked most of the changes. Personally, I found some of the platforming sections annoying (as I did in the original - something I would have been happy if they had skipped recreating) and the bloody assassins are real pains, but getting past them gives the same sense of achievement. In that sense I enjoyed the game.
However, the big selling point, and the original point (from what I remember) of the mod, was to recreate Half Life with better graphics. And this is where the developers both succeed and fail. If this had been released a couple of years after Half Life 2, then I wouldn't have any reservations about recommending it. Unfortunately, the engine has aged (not as badly as some mind you), but its obvious that this engine is 11 years old. And it struggles to compete against more recent efforts. Saying that, its obvious that, in certain areas, the developers have put a lot of effort in, and the game looks absolutely amazing. I certainly paused in places to have a look around and enjoy the views. But, at this stage in development, that quality isn't consistent. And that's the problem. Its 2015, and at times, I would be hard pressed to tell the difference between this game and the original 17 year old game (yeah... that's made me feel old).
So its hard to recommend it, but I will. I loved the original, and this game has allowed me to revisit that world, but in a much prettier way.

Splinter Cell... The game that launched so many ships, and has attained the status of classic for the stealth game genre...
The very first entry of the serie, sadly, aged pretty poorly. Having only played it relatively recently, I don't have the nostalgia googles most people have(mostly because it was on a console I didn't own when it came out, and one I didn't bother to get). So I need to adress the fact this game has a lot of issues. Controls are horribly wonky to the point of being irresponsive at times. A lot of game mechanics are actually pretty broken like the segment where you must avoid being sniped in a minefield, and you will get hit even in complete darkness if the game feels like it wants to do so. The control scheme itself shows it was thought with console in mind, and isn't instinctive nor convenient. As for graphisms, well... You know. But graphisms are probably the the last of your worries.
It's not a bad game, mind you, but for today standards, it's certainly not a good one. At best, it's mediocre, and it's there either for nostagics, or for people who want to get it due to its classic status to know what they have missed a few years back.
I suggest you get it in a pack, to understand the origins of the franchise, and how it evolved from there, and for a very low price, which shouldn't be too hard. Understand what you're buying though, because no matter what, you will be disapointed(unless you wear the aforementioned nostalgia googles).
I only recommend the game out of the proverbial classic status, because it's a game one should at least play once, just for educational purposes. See how it began, why it, and other stealth games, evolved the way they did, and measure how far down the road they went.
Remember kids, this is how the light bulbs genocide started.

Let me start with a disclaimer: I am running this game on slightly below reccomended specs, but above minimum. That being said, I have had few problems running this game. In one section of the game I had it crash twice, but haven't had any other difficulties besides that. I personally have not experienced any major drops in framerate or have it ever go below 30fps, generally it holds around 40-50.
All technical aspects aside, this game is really good, from what I've played so far. Based on the locations section of the journal, I'd say I'm roughly halfway through the game right now, unless it picks up speed toward the end. The game is incredible so far, an improvement in almost every way over the original. Some highlights:
Emily's new powers - Between Mesmer, Domino, and the unique ways you can use Far Reach, I've had a lot of fun taking out enemies with Emily's powers. I haven't even scratched the surface of the powers though, never having used Shadow Walk, or Doppleganger. Plus there's the bonecharm crafting system I have yet to really get into, and the other enhancemnets that are passive bonuses.
Level design - These levels feel even more vertical than ones before, giving a wide range of options on how to get around in the levels.
Non-lethal options - Between chloroform bottles and non-lethal options in combat, going non-lethal assault is more viable than previously. The non-lethal drop assassinations, as well as mid combat chokes make the combat feel more fluid if you're going for this approach.
TL;DR - Personally, I've had no problems with the technical aspect, though that doesn't mean they don't exist, and in terms of gameplay its an improvement on the orignal in every way.

Such an adorable and chill game, one of the best I've played. The $20 is totally worth it, and even if you wait till the game's finished, it'll stay the same price. So if you'd rather wait, there's no issue there!
The gameplay concept is super simple: Make corrals for slimes on your ranch, make gardens and Hen Hen coops to supply food for them, use the slime plorts to earn money. And when you have enough, you can unlock the lab to make devices to obtain resources for making cool stuff!
The world is amazing, and so beautiful. You start out in the Dry Reef, which is nice and perfect for getting the starting slimes and food. It won't be too long before you get Slime Keys from the Gordos scattered around the world to unlock the doors to the bigger and greater parts of the world, giving you access to new resources and slimes! It doesn't hurt to take the time to explore every inch of the world too, you never know where you might find a treasure pod!
There's very few dangers to the game, so if you're not a fan of super-stressful things, then this is a good game. All you have to worry about are Tarrs(slimes that ate one plort too many and turn hostile), feral slimes in certain areas(feed them or just run past them), and the Slime Sea, which is an instant KO if you fall into it. Just be careful around certain slimes too, they can hurt.
TLDR; If you'd like a simple game where you can chill out as a farmer on a weird, alien planet with the cutest creatures and beautiful scenery, then this is a great game for you!

I have spent a while playing this game so far and I would say most of it has been spent playing over the same bits several times due to being killed by the alien/androids.  Unfortunately due to the save points being pretty far apart at times this is starting to make the game rather repetitive and frustrating.
I guess the good points are:
The game has a great atmosphere.  The corridors of the Sevastopol look great and it really does feel like you are stuck on a space station.  The lighting effects and smoke combined with the creaking and groaning of the metal of the ship add to this greatly.
There is definitely a sense of tension, panic and urgency when playing. You don't really ever feel like you can relax after the first encounter with the Alien.  I spend the whole game crouched!
Nice use of logs to build the story but also the other NPCs add to the story - I wasn’t really expecting there to be other people in the game.  (Just Ripley and the Alien)
The Bad:
Seemingly random Alien attacks.  For realisms sake this makes sense but in the game it is just far too frustrating - at one point I was running to escape from someone and the alien grabbed me from an air vent above with no real warning.  Another time I was trying to make my way to a save point when it appeared behind me and tore me in two.  Whilst the deaths are mildly amusing the lack of frequent AutoSaves mean you have to go and play through large sections again.
The Stealth... sometimes it works well but other times it becomes almost too hard to stay hidden.  The motion tracker is more of a hidrence to this.  It would have been good to have some sort of indicator similar to the one used in Metro Last Light to let you know when you are visible.
The music - in the end I have turned this off.  It drowned out a lot of the noises you needed to hear and although it added to the tension it just became annoying.
As I have already mentioned the lack of save points.  There really needs to be save points when going between sections of the game.  I don’t always have that much time to spend playing a game so always appreciate the ability to save when you need to.  If the player wants to save every five minutes - let them....it doesn’t change the gameplay just removes some frustration.
I really do want to like this game and It has exceeded my expectations but they we set pretty low.... I think I could recommend it but I found that I enjoyed the much-slated Thief remake much more than this so far.
So if you haven’t bought thief.... maybe get that cheap until the price of this drops!
For now this is a not recommended - if an update changes something with the save points this may change.

There comes another marvelous gem for which it is tremendously hard to write a review and do justice completely without presenting spoilers.
is the narrative of a series of staggering experiences concerning a girl named Alice - or many Alices in their different incarnations nonetheless - and her dream of an apocalyptic end. Here, we will participate in her dream many, many times to reach countless endings to try and discover a meaning to it.
The narrative opens with a basic chat screen where Alice talks to her friend M. Hatter and tells him of a disturbingly lucid dream that she has seen the other day. In this unsettling dream, the city is under the threat of getting hit by a series of nuclear missiles due to unknown reasons. The estimation indicates that she'll have a bit more than half an hour to find some kind of protective measure. Here, we become a witness to the before, present and after of a possible nuclear attack and try to lead Alice to some kind of safety while making choices of survival, logic, ethics to reach an ending. We fight against environment, we fight against ourselves; but mostly we fight against time.
Before each playthrough, we are presented the opportunity to choose Alice's stats enrolled into different abilities - consisting of survival, resources, fitness, social abilities, career and dating - to arrange a different incarnation, an alternate dream version of the actual Alice. The combination of different stats change the storyline and starting position for Alice, making different story paths to follow available. In each playthrough different choices and Alice's abilities - and also the exact timing that we chose to take the action during narrative - present countless different combinations, thus different story progressions for Alice. Mostly she dies, sometimes she survives. Yet there is always the reluctant feeling that something's missing is present. As if, that wasn't the way the dream was intended to end... There we go back, start a new game to craft a new Alice and try a new path to follow in hopes of maybe discovering what that was about this time.
We participate in Alice's narrative to make her choices and affect the happenings of her dream past in a frame tale fashion. Alice's narrative of her experience is dreadfully realistic, actualized through an elaborate vocabulary and shockingly pinpoint descriptions. It is confusingly easy to immerse into the narrative experience of Alice, finding yourself trying different combinations of stats and choices endlessly, nearly always discovering some new outcome. The main display consists of nothing much aside some beautiful and appropriately forlorn artwork and the ominous soundtrack lingering in the background to enhance the narrative towards its triumph.
At this point, it should be no secret that the game is inspired from Lewis Carroll's
yet it manages to craft the symbolic personifications into a genuine setting of its own; way more realistic and disturbing that Lewis Carroll ever intended them to be so. Aside all of its narrative glory and ever changing gameplay; it is an unbelievable fact that the game is a freeware. Can you even believe it? I'll go ahead and urge you to try this uncanny experience. Maybe this time, Alice will come back from the rabbit hole.

Early Access/Pre Zen Update
11hrs for £15 (so far).
Gameplay wise it hasn't changed too much from Half Life 1. So if you liked the original, chances are you'll like this.
There's been a few changes in level designs and I think the weapons have been slightly rebalanced, so don't expect a complete carbon copy of the original. Saying that, I liked most of the changes. Personally, I found some of the platforming sections annoying (as I did in the original - something I would have been happy if they had skipped recreating) and the bloody assassins are real pains, but getting past them gives the same sense of achievement. In that sense I enjoyed the game.
However, the big selling point, and the original point (from what I remember) of the mod, was to recreate Half Life with better graphics. And this is where the developers both succeed and fail. If this had been released a couple of years after Half Life 2, then I wouldn't have any reservations about recommending it. Unfortunately, the engine has aged (not as badly as some mind you), but its obvious that this engine is 11 years old. And it struggles to compete against more recent efforts. Saying that, its obvious that, in certain areas, the developers have put a lot of effort in, and the game looks absolutely amazing. I certainly paused in places to have a look around and enjoy the views. But, at this stage in development, that quality isn't consistent. And that's the problem. Its 2015, and at times, I would be hard pressed to tell the difference between this game and the original 17 year old game (yeah... that's made me feel old).
So its hard to recommend it, but I will. I loved the original, and this game has allowed me to revisit that world, but in a much prettier way.

I played the majority of Black Mesa Source before it came to early access, and I'm enjoying playing the current incarnation even more, being that it's more rounded out and has some great (and authentic) multiplayer. Some performance issues aside online, the game is running very smoothly and it is clear that the game is a labour of love by a dedicated team.
My only bone of contention, and it's arguable that I'm perhaps missing the point, is that in some ways the game doesn't quite go far enough in it's vision, or perhaps rather than it is at times inconsistent in it's execution. The approach, obviously, is to recreate, or 're-envision' Half-Life from beginning to end, using modern technology and methods that are more contemporary to gaming post 2000 (or even 2005). The result is a game that is not just visually familiar but one that plays very familiarly, for better and worse. Some of Half-Life's more irritating sections have been altered and streamlined, yet some are curiously left unaltered, issues intact. Something about this inconsistency speaks to the games origins as a mod by a team spread out geographically, with level designers with different ideas of what the game should be like spread out far and wide. The Sector C labs, for instance, have been extended and fleshed out with a great deal more detail, but this is more superficial, whereas the Office Complex unit has been edited and reshaped more substantially, to greater effect. Some of the original chapter's more bland areas are not just visually striking, but contain fresh secrets and nooks and crannies to explore, as well as some surprises, enemy wise. At the very least, the facelift is welcome, but at times it feels like the opportunity to really take the essence of Half-Life and build upon it is underused in favour of remaining faithful.
The game is still in development, of course. Xen is still absent, presumably because it was always going to be the most problematic chapter to rebuild in terms of making it actually enjoyable, this time around (it always was a bizarre end to the original Half-Life, tonally shifting entirely from intense combat to akward platforming mechanics and a really terrible boss fight at the end). I'm hoping the workshop features some other additions that allow other interpretations to be dropped into the single player experience as well as the welcome but predictable multiplayer remakes.
The multiplayer component, whilst suffering from performance issues at the moment (a few days after initial release), is a blast and really does take me back to the LAN party death-match sessions I would indulge in when I was fifteen and sixteen years old. The weapons all feel substantial and impactful, and the map design is first-rate.

Just wow. One of the best games I've played in the last years. A steampunk/dystopian setting, great graphics, a breath-taking story, a gameplay that offers you the possibility of playing in so many different ways, some more evident, others well hidden. Simply, a must-have.
That said, it is not perfect; personally, I found the story of Dishonored a lot more interesting - the half-game twist is still an unbeaten masterpiece, for example. Probably, since the first game could only be played as Corvo, the story was more focused; here you can play either as Corvo or as Emily, with (slightly) different gameplays, so you are sort of invited to play it at least twice. However, the story is exactly the same with both characters, and the gameplay is not that different at all: the powers of the two characters are either the same with different names, or different in their nature, but corresponding in their practical functions (e.g. Corvo can possess mice; Emily can take a shadow form that can walk through passages meant for rats). The possible endings, while different in nature, feel in any case quite short and disappointing; I suppose that, again, the real focus of the game is on playing it again and again in different styles, not actually on finishing a story. You can like this direction or not, but I believe this was all to detriment of the RPG/immersive elements.
