I'm becoming a fan of Big Ant for the quality of game they can produce in Australia on what seems like a low budget, especially in comparison with big sports game companies EA and 2K. That said, I think RLL3 suffers from a lack of polish.
The good thing is that they have managed  to create a reasonably challenging game here, the bad news is that the way they have achieved it feels unfair and does not proomote creativity. The biggest problem with the game for me is the pacing which feels like it affects eveything else. A slow game speed option would probably go a long way to improving things along with a rework of how ratings affect outcomes.
Too often, a knock on will lead to the opponents prop picking up the ball and running the distance for a try. Fullback positioning is terrible. Offloads have to be well timed and feel like too much of a lottery in comparison to reality. The passing game is stifled by a flat backline and the occurance of errors. What the game rewards you for is playing simple footy and trying to beat your opponent one on one with a side step or a fend - which is fine, but the lack of other options makes it a little boring. I think the problem stems from the lack of ability to establish a realistic and entertaining offensive game without it being overpowered against the AI programming, which is a shame. What we have is still rugby league, although one dimensional and repetitive. If you love sports games or Rugby League its probably work checking out.

Needless to say, Company of Heroes is one of the greatest games of all time and my favourite RTS. If you are interested in this game and haven't bought it yet, let me just sum up all the things which make Company of Heroes so superb:
+ thrilling campaign with cinematic cutscenes
+ insane multiplayer battles where even a certain loss can be turned into a surprising victory
+ unique resource system that forces you to play aggressively and fight across the entire map
+ completely destroyable environment and sophisticated physics system
+ very detailed graphics compared to other RTS games
With that being said, one could think CoH is almost a perfect game. It indeed is, but there is also a couple of things that sometimes make the game a bit frustrating:
- vehicle pathing. Especially in urban maps with lots of buildings. obstacles, etc.
- cheating AI. Yes, computer player cheats which means it can see the exact locations of all your units at all times as well as your building queues. Additionally, it can also use some abilities in ways human players can't.
So, what are you waiting for? Go get the game if you haven't yet! It's definetely worth the money and it still has a lot to offer, even today.

, the largely anticipated remake of one of the best first person shooter games of all time, certainly lives up to the standards of its predecessor. It was made by fans of the Half-Life franchise, and it is a very large project indeed. It originally started as a mod of
, but has now grown into a standalone game.
There are two versions of Black Mesa.
(The mod version)
(The Steam version)
BMS 2012 was released in 2012, as a mod that required Valve's free Source SDK base 2007 to run. It was a groundbreaking remake of the first Half-Life game's single player campaign, minus the final four chapters. After 8 years in development, it was worth the
wait.
BMS 2015 was recently released, you guessed it, in 2015, on Steam. This version features updated graphics, new content, new voice acting, and an all new multiplayer experience, featuring free-for-all deathmatch and team deathmatch modes. The final four chapters have yet to be added, and I am very excited for them, as I have heard that they will be packed full of gameplay. People have complained about the $20 price tag, despite the fact that the developers that make up
have stated long ago that they intended to sell the Steam version.
I am happy with the price, as the developers deserve to earn money for such a jaw-droppingly epic project. That said, it is not perfect; personally, I found the story of Dishonored a lot more interesting - the half-game twist is still an unbeaten masterpiece, for example. Probably, since the first game could only be played as Corvo, the story was more focused; here you can play either as Corvo or as Emily, with (slightly) different gameplays, so you are sort of invited to play it at least twice. However, the story is exactly the same with both characters, and the gameplay is not that different at all: the powers of the two characters are either the same with different names, or different in their nature, but corresponding in their practical functions (e.g. Corvo can possess mice; Emily can take a shadow form that can walk through passages meant for rats). The possible endings, while different in nature, feel in any case quite short and disappointing; I suppose that, again, the real focus of the game is on playing it again and again in different styles, not actually on finishing a story. You can like this direction or not, but I believe this was all to detriment of the RPG/immersive elements.

Dark Souls II has the most embarrassing PvP netcode ever written. Simply put, each player determines on their own end where enemies are in terms of hit detection and animation frames. It is an absolute embarassment to see PC gamers apologize for this garbage yet again, because it's literally the same system from Dark Souls. This means that you can still backstab someone from the front, still be hit by an attack placed in thin air, your roll or parry don't matter unless your opponent's computer says they do. For a game where the basis of combat is simple timing and directional aiming, of course you might not realize it but you are also doing this to the enemy, most of your 'legit' wins are a frustrating and cheap experience for your opponent. The PvP Covenants are absolutely terrible.
Small improvements still don't compensate for enormous disappointment. To aid in replayability, all From Software had to do was change up the location and type of enemies in each area, and add significant challenge to bosses. Instead, you get to play the same lifeless world every time with a couple of bonus phantoms in each area. The new 'Challenge' boss harkening to the only decent bosses From Software ever made (Kalameet and Manus), is a big dragon who is either the easiest boss in the game if you know to walk from big toe to big toe, or the most stupidly cheap if you provoke his bombarding fire breath. The majority of the bosses are still made unfun by knowing a simple fact, one of the most artistic and interesting bosses of Dark Souls was the Great Gray Wolf Sif, until you learned that he was a inept loser when someone stands between his legs in the right way. It's the same thing here, with a handful of minor exceptions.
Story and content-wise, this game is an immense, stupidly lazy rehash of Dark Souls. It has literally the same story, and if you believe in the most popular theory on the lore, it literally IS the same story as Dark Souls. Complete with sad-faced hollow king swinging a big sword at you to sad piano. However, there are a lot of great new armor sets and certain niche weapons are slightly less niche like whips, fists and claws. They lure you into playing New Game+/++ by making armor, spells and weapons that are only available in that playthrough.
A complaint I had about Dark Souls has been repeated for the worse, the PvP covenants like the Cat Covenant in Dark Souls had the player engaged in a story oriented PvP experience. In reality, the world was not dynamic or interesting enough to feel that such a thing mattered, and what actually happened is people just camped the forest on purpose for straight no-value-added dueling. Well, imagine the same half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥attempt at story with probably the most aggravating griefing experience possible - the Rat King Covenant. The premise is that you can force other players to come to your world, while hiding behind a gauntlet of traps suspending above death pits / water while monsters fight FOR you against the hapless invader. Honestly most people in the Rat King Covenant are probably victims of the Rat King Covenant, waiting for that sweet schadenfreude as they pass the new griefing on to someone else.
The Belfry's are just idiotic, if you plan on beating your opponents through a longer strategy, be prepared for more grey spirits to gang bang you to death while you try. Except that Belfry Luna has a rehashed Dark Souls boss, the Bell Tower Gargoyles. Everything you heard about Dark Souls II PvP Covenants before it released turned out to be a horrible disappointment, such as Blue Sentinels "Defending" people from invasion. Maybe once every 24 hours on any difficulty, and sometimes they just die before you get there. The Blue Sentinels are basically just butthurt Red Phantoms. When I finally became a Red Phantom after maxing out the other PvP Covenants I was surprised by the CLOWN CARS OF BLUE ♥♥♥♥S invading my world at all times.
Long story short, because fans won't criticize and From Software (Now owned by Kadokawa) won't listen, Dark Souls series will remain the worst PvP available. But a decent single/coop experience.

The freedom of view point allows camera angles previously reserved for cinema. It was a gaming experience like none other and few have come close to matching. The AI in particular is very impressive with a progressive strategy building heavier units as the match goes on. You can actually see on the replays where the AI builds certain units to counter the units you use most. I must admit the game was better in vanilla the patches just made things complicated. I'd develop a playing style and suddenly the mg was weak or my favorite tank was now a tin can. Tales of Valor specifically added some nice gameplay and a few decent units to unlock. The campaign really made you feel for those Germans who fought for country and home rather than agenda and hatred. This game creates a bond among gamers I've never developed longterm online friendships before CoH. My one gripe and this is true for many players the US 57mm AT gun is so overpowered. It can somehow outrange anything on the map minus a hummel and destroys everything in a few hits. I understand balance is an issue because let's face it the Germans had better soldiers and weapons. In a fair fight with equal resources the allies would stand absolutely no chance. 10 million dead Russians can attest to that.
Honestly the best strategy game i've played, but if you like this game and think that the sequel (Company of Heroes 2) will be any good... think again...

APB Reloaded is quite the interesting game. It's a fast paced 3rd person shooter MMO in a somewhat open world. I've enjoyed this game since 2013 (ah, the good old days.) The game itself is very buggy and can make no sense at all when it comes to combat sometimes. But if you actually get the hang of how the gun mechanics work then you should be set. Ad the driving, oh man the driving. these cars are hard as hell to drive. either too slow, too fast, car gets blown up too easy, can't blow up an enemy car cause it's too armored. This game requires a lot of skill and a buttload of learning. I say try it out and try to get past rank 60 and you might get addicted. And that stuff about being pay2win is all nonsense. the joker CR 5 has the same exact stats as an ntech. The difference is that you buy the joker CR 5 with real money. And if you actually pay for some of the packs, they come with awesome cars, clothes, and weapons. Every gun that is on the armas market (the place you go to spend real money) has different variant at the joker store (ingame store to buy guns with ingame currency). And speaking of gear, the customization is endless. Do you want to look like a soldier? A maid? A racer? Someone fro myour favorite franchise of games? you can do it all. I would recommend buying premium with this game. You get more contact standing, more money, and discounts on pretty much everything in the armas marketplace. You also get waaaaay more room to customize. It goes from a nonpremium member only having room to use 25 shapes to a symbol, to a premium member being able to use 100 shapes. I love this game and it has a special little home for me and a lot of the veterans on this game. Also, this was originally made by the people that made crackdown, so you'll notice some similarities.

Black Mesa is a very ambitious remake of Half-Life in the Source (aka Half-Life 2) engine.  Years ago, I tried the original free release and was impressed by the level design, but found there were a lot of gameplay mechanics that needed to be adjusted, fixed, etc.  I am happy to report that the Steam release is a huge improvement over the original free one, particularly in the combat portions, and is far closer to being a "completed" game despite it not currently having the last Xen levels done yet.
Many people online have been complaining that the $20 price is too expensive, but when you consider the fact that this group of people have been working very hard for years to make this happen, you can't help but appreciate all the time and effort they have put into it.  In fact, they have actually improved upon many chapters/levels from the original game in many ways and the overall presentation is excellent.
For a person that has played both HL1 and HL2 too many times to count, this was just as much fun in its own ways and think you'll dig it too.  I look forward to seeing it completed and fully tweaked, no matter how long it takes and wish the team the best of luck in finally being able to reach the finish line.

A timeless classic. Still has its atmosphere (largely thanks to the awesome soundtrack by Michael Richard Plowman) and I personally think SC1 has the best atmosphere of all Splinter Cells. Yes, Chaos Theory has better gameplay, but SC1 made me really think like "If my cover gets blown, I have no chance of surviving" - and you really don't have much chances of surviving. Like Lambert said in the beginning: "Invisibility is your best weapon". The story of SC1 is quite good, nothing really impressive, but my personal SC favourite.
The artifical intelligence didn't age really well - the AI will sometimes act weird, but nothing really gamebreaking. The only problem with AI I encountered and was annoying was in Kola Cell (which is a level that isn't shipped with Steam version, use one of guides here to find out how to get these three aditional levels), where I could be seen behind the wall.
And what about graphics? Well, this is what made me think "The graphics will never get better" back in 2003. Well, they did, but I am amazed to this day what this game is capable of doing with the lights. The shadow shader is still really neat. In my recent replay of this game, I was stunned by the shadows coming from the windows with blinds. Sad thing is, there is still a lot of new games that can't do this.
The controls are comfortable to use, although it's not natively supporting gamepads (tried X360 and XONE). The default keyboard + mouse configuration is easy to use. At the time, a lot of reviews praised the use of a mouse wheel as a speed regulator. When I first heard about it, I thought I will never get used to it, since mouse wheel is commonly used as a weapon switcher, but I was wrong, I got used to it in about 10 minutes.
BTW don't get mistaken by my playtime (currently 25 hours), I've replayed this game for about 10 times.

It's Dark Souls II. You already know if you want this game.
If you're genuinely unsure if you want this game, then you probably don't have the context in which to appreciate it anyway, so I might not bother. This sounds like the sort of fedora-tipping elitism you'd hear on yonchan or reddit, but frankly, it's true.
See, Dark Souls is a series built on the remains of its forebears, classic role-playing games like Wizardry and From Software's own King's Field series. It's unintuitive, bordering on downright cryptic, mercilessly unforgiving to the point of being abusive, and at times seemingly totally random and inexplicable. However, it IS a modern game, and as such, a combination of quick reflexes and thorough consideration will lead you to victory.
With easily 40 hours of content (or more, if you're a new player -- my first character was over 100 hours, as I learned the ins and outs of the game), and with some of the best gameplay and theming in gaming today, it's not obvious why I may not recommend Dark Souls II to the casual player -- it goes way beyond "it's really hard". Still, if you're any kind of hardcore gamer, you really can't afford to miss this game.
(One postscript I will add is that this game *basically doesn't work* without online play. It can be played offline, but the mechanics of the game are crafted such that you really, really need to be online to enjoy it properly.)

Dark Souls 2 sure looked a lot like it's predecessor, but I believe it was lacking in what made Dark Souls 1 so immersive; it lacked in it's very soul. Now I still enjoyed playing through the game, but many of the characters in Dark Souls 2 were easily forgettable and didn't really have much of a story behind them; besides Lucatiel who was somewhat interesting at the very least.
Something else I didn't really think was done that well in Dark Souls 2 was the level design and how half of the game didn't flow together and felt hashed in at certain points, I really think the level design could have been better, I mean without a stradegy guide I had to run through places multiple times to find out where I needed to go and there was barely any direction given after the four lord souls were obtained. Many of the areas in Dark Souls 2 looked very nice but were loaded with cheap deaths such as the falling deaths which got rather annoying at times since while walking through a certain watery area I had to literally point my camera top down on my character to make sure I didn't fall to my death.
Along with the level design missing out so to did the combat design, the enemies attacks would unnaturally track you down even if you attempted to roll away somehow they would almost always manage to pivot just right so they could hit you with their unproportionate hitboxes on their weapons and attacks. It seemed as though nearly every enemy had a hitbox too large for their attack, granted you could get use to this feature but it still was rather annoying coming from Dark Souls 1 where the enemies attacks would at the very least be predictable in their range.
I think in comparison to Dark Souls 1, Dark Souls 2 would only get about 6/10 on a scale of similarity and that mostly accounts for mechanics and appearance of both games. For a game score I would give Dark Souls 1 a 9/10 and Dark Souls 2 an 8/10.

The game engages the player - he must pay attention to his environment, and always be aware of the types of enemies he must face, or traps that he may encounter; every deaths teaches the player something, should he learn from it.
Dark Souls II also looks astounding, even on a mid-to-low end PC; the optimization is great, everything looks nice and smooth, and textures are fairly consistent.
Multiplayer will both allure and drive players out. For those who are new, being ganked or invaded could be quite frustrating. For those who are veterans, they may be confused, or even repelled by some of the changes From has introduced. As of the time of this review though, said changes may be altered and this comment may no longer be valid. Mostly, however, I had a satisfactory time playing the multiplayer. (Well, I do hope they disallow double buffing weapons.)
Overall, a solid successor of Dark Souls that will leave you Hollow (lifeless) for the next three to five months.

Good rugby game but not without flaws, graphically it's great and it has good gameplay options as well as a fantastic 'Fan Hub' section. The inclusion to add community created teams and players is excellent.
I love the indepth player a team customisation as well as the facilities to create custom leagues and tournaments.
However the gameplay in matches is not all that great, bodering on awful. The passing is a massive hit or miss experience, usually ignoring the button press entirely especially when a quick pass is needed. You'll find your player just carry on running rather than pass or pass many times in quick succsession until he thrwos it out of bounds.
Alternativly when you are on a break the opposing AI can grab you at any angle from seemingly any distance, going from facing the wrong way to an instant 180 and bringing you down. The few feet between players is ignored allowing the opposing team to morph the gap and grab you, allowing no real pacing breaks or runs. Because this isn't Union there is only 5 attempts per passge to try and get a run going. Another dead option is the drop ball, if you manage to catch the high ball your player is instantly barraged and the sloppy pass system means you lose a passage of play.
There needs to be an auto player switch on tackles or at very least an overhaul. It takes a lot of learning to get the right player in the right place and make the tackle, a little automated help would go a long way as it really interupts the flow of the game. The manual switching especially at harder difficulties is pretty shambolic, finding a lot of times a breaking run will occur because the switching has skipped the last player in play, frantically watching your player marker skip through the entire team. There is an option to skip to player closest to the ball but i find myself wondering what ball the computer thinks is in play, most of the time i'm running at the ball boy.
The 'tutorial' section is more like a challenge section with not enough of the games basics covered, a practice zone would of been better suited. With a game featuring this many rules and possible plays, a tutorial is a must, especially how to change the tactics which are scarcely mentioned. Look in the options for gameplay controls and find all the buttons and what kicks you can perform in there, this does a better job teaching you the game than the tutorial section.
There is a humungous leap in difficulty from Rookie to Amateur, it feels like beginner to pro in one quick leap, offering no subtle difficulty change meaning you will jump from dominating with no retaliation to instantly held and losing.
I'd barely recommend it, it can be fun but the issues with gameplay are just game destroying at times. Everything but the rugby is done well.

To be perfectly clear: this is a review for the New Steam Version of CoH.
Company of Heroes is probably my most beloved franchise of all time. So why am I giving this a negative review?
Here's what happened: CoH's original publisher, THQ, went bankrupt and CoH and its development house were sold to Sega. Multiplayer infrastructure is now handled natively through Steam. This sounds great in theory, but in practice, the game suffers from constant, crippling crashes. It really is unplayably bad. It's unconscionable that things could have been allowed to deteriorate so badly, but I suppose it was inevitable that such an old game wouldn't get the love it needed. The gameplay and graphics really do hold up quite well: in fact I'd say it bests CoH 2 in practically all regards.
What a sad and ignominious way for a beautiful game to live out its last days. CoH really didn't deserve to go out with a whimper. If you haven't played the single-player campaigns, you really owe it to yourself to play through the original and Opposing Fronts campaigns, which are brilliant. But as for multiplayer, this game is essentially over, barring the unlikely event that the netcode is ironed out to pre-Steam levels.
Fare ye well, CoH.

There are a lot of entitled people on the internet, people who will pay 60 dollars for their third copy of GTA 5 and pay a monthly fee for world of warcraft, but give them a total conversion for half-life 2 that reproduces the joy of the original half life for 1/3 the cost of a triple A title that also boasts a solid multiplayer experience? Ok this one is going to be long:
This game has been on development for at least 8 years now I think and now we see it first release in steam, for those who do not know, this is a remake of Valve's legendary game ''Half Life'' released in 1998 in an updated Source engine.
What I like about it apart from the updated graphics obviously is how the developers carefully designed the game with interesting dialog and replaced some of the level design with fun mechanics, for example now you may want to stay to hear scientists conversations or do some physics puzzles.
It's really more advanced than the free version that was released in 2012, also, they included a multiplayer mode, it feels and plays like Half Life 1 and with the workshop support, we can expect to see pretty original things in the future.
In conclusion, it's an early access you want to get, even if you played Half Life before, this is a must get.

I haven't spent much time with other MMOs, but I'm a long-time Elder Scrolls fan.  As long as you come into this game with the expectation that it's an Elder Scrolls-flavored MMO, and not multiplayer Skyrim, it's very enjoyable.  You don't have the total freedom of movement that other Scrolls games allow you - enemies don't scale, so you have to stay in areas where you can handle them.  The world still feels fairly open, though, and exploration is rewarded with skill points, quests, chests, and enemies that can't be found on the main roads.  The quests are similar in style to Skyrim and Oblivion quests, with plenty of personal drama, unique objectives, and just enough lore for seasoning.  Graphically, it's good for an MMO, but it still is what it is.
One other thing that I don't think gets enough attention - this is an LGBT-freindly game that features homosexual couples as main characters in several questlines!  Huzzah!
Highly recomended..

APB Reloaded is quite the interesting game. It's a fast paced 3rd person shooter MMO in a somewhat open world. I've enjoyed this game since 2013 (ah, the good old days.) The game itself is very buggy and can make no sense at all when it comes to combat sometimes. But if you actually get the hang of how the gun mechanics work then you should be set. Ad the driving, oh man the driving. these cars are hard as hell to drive. either too slow, too fast, car gets blown up too easy, can't blow up an enemy car cause it's too armored. This game requires a lot of skill and a buttload of learning. I say try it out and try to get past rank 60 and you might get addicted. And that stuff about being pay2win is all nonsense. the joker CR 5 has the same exact stats as an ntech. The difference is that you buy the joker CR 5 with real money. And if you actually pay for some of the packs, they come with awesome cars, clothes, and weapons. Every gun that is on the armas market (the place you go to spend real money) has different variant at the joker store (ingame store to buy guns with ingame currency). And speaking of gear, the customization is endless. Do you want to look like a soldier? A maid? A racer? Someone fro myour favorite franchise of games? you can do it all. I would recommend buying premium with this game. You get more contact standing, more money, and discounts on pretty much everything in the armas marketplace. You also get waaaaay more room to customize. It goes from a nonpremium member only having room to use 25 shapes to a symbol, to a premium member being able to use 100 shapes. I love this game and it has a special little home for me and a lot of the veterans on this game. Also, this was originally made by the people that made crackdown, so you'll notice some similarities.

Dark Souls 2 sure looked a lot like it's predecessor, but I believe it was lacking in what made Dark Souls 1 so immersive; it lacked in it's very soul. Now I still enjoyed playing through the game, but many of the characters in Dark Souls 2 were easily forgettable and didn't really have much of a story behind them; besides Lucatiel who was somewhat interesting at the very least.
Something else I didn't really think was done that well in Dark Souls 2 was the level design and how half of the game didn't flow together and felt hashed in at certain points, I really think the level design could have been better, I mean without a stradegy guide I had to run through places multiple times to find out where I needed to go and there was barely any direction given after the four lord souls were obtained. Many of the areas in Dark Souls 2 looked very nice but were loaded with cheap deaths such as the falling deaths which got rather annoying at times since while walking through a certain watery area I had to literally point my camera top down on my character to make sure I didn't fall to my death.
Along with the level design missing out so to did the combat design, the enemies attacks would unnaturally track you down even if you attempted to roll away somehow they would almost always manage to pivot just right so they could hit you with their unproportionate hitboxes on their weapons and attacks. It seemed as though nearly every enemy had a hitbox too large for their attack, granted you could get use to this feature but it still was rather annoying coming from Dark Souls 1 where the enemies attacks would at the very least be predictable in their range.
I think in comparison to Dark Souls 1, Dark Souls 2 would only get about 6/10 on a scale of similarity and that mostly accounts for mechanics and appearance of both games. For a game score I would give Dark Souls 1 a 9/10 and Dark Souls 2 an 8/10.

I thoroughly enjoyed Dark Souls II and its predecessor, Dark Souls.
To begin with, the game is nothing short of what it promised: tons of fun, challenges, and death.
The game engages the player - he must pay attention to his environment, and always be aware of the types of enemies he must face, or traps that he may encounter; every deaths teaches the player something, should he learn from it.
Dark Souls II also looks astounding, even on a mid-to-low end PC; the optimization is great, everything looks nice and smooth, and textures are fairly consistent.
Multiplayer will both allure and drive players out. For those who are new, being ganked or invaded could be quite frustrating. For those who are veterans, they may be confused, or even repelled by some of the changes From has introduced. As of the time of this review though, said changes may be altered and this comment may no longer be valid. Mostly, however, I had a satisfactory time playing the multiplayer. (Well, I do hope they disallow double buffing weapons.)
Overall, a solid successor of Dark Souls that will leave you Hollow (lifeless) for the next three to five months.

, before I leave a review, I do want to state that, to a group of select individuals, this game may be fun, challenging, and an all-around pleasant experience. However, to me, and the friends I've played with, this game did not offer any of that.
The game has a top-down perspective, which is a nice change-of-pace when it comes to Post-Apocalyptic games. However, the gameplay is very dull, and incredibly "unfair".
AI controlled survivors work incredibly slow, and it's either wait about four hours for them to complete the side-tasks for you, or try and do it all yourself. Hordes and bandits attack your homebase for seemingly no reason and sometimes they'll attack while you're not even at your base, so you have no way of defending yourself. The infected act in such an annoying way that combat, a part of the game that should be fun and exciting, ends up either being frustrating or too dull.
I played with a good friend, and even she said the game was boring after awhile. If a post-apocalyptic zombie game fails to captivate two players who are heavily into post-apocalyptic scenerios and zombies in general, then the game doesn't achieve what it is trying to.
This would all be fine, though, if it weren't for the fact that the game costs money. Something like this can easily have a charm to it if it was Free-To-Play, but the price tag just makes it a bit annoying.
There is no ill-will to the developers. It's a good start. Multiplyer connectivity works and the game doesn't have any glitches or bugs. However, I would recommend trying again, and fixing the flaws. The game was a great idea, but the price just makes all the annoying aspects extra annoying

This game is always fun to come back to.  The story is entertaining, the characters are generally likable, and the mechanics are a lot of fun.  It lacks a certain polish, in that the character faces are a bit generic and the plot could be a little deeper and there are occasional bugs and there is a finite amount of insulin in this post apocalyptic world where you could otherwise live forever if you're good at managing your growing city...  But none of that takes away from the feeling of accomplishment as you scrounge up the resources to trade for gold that you hoard until you can afford to buy the diabetic girl another day on this forsaken earth.  It's got the "tough choices" aspect that people seem to love in games nowadays, and they break up the tedium of gathering-heavy-materials-via-multiple-trips-across-long-distances by letting you give menial tasks to your people while you go fight zomblies and do plot stuff.  It's well done where it counts, I guess is how I'd sum it up.  Well worth five bucks, so if you see it on sale I'd say snag it.
One thought for gameplay: I found that guns weren't terribly necessary for the character I'm controlling.  Get a couple points in fitness and never sprint to the point that you're wheezing, and you can just knock down even the tough ones and stomp em til they stop fighting.  Which waters down the heart-pulsing feeling of fighting a zombie that's got a strain of virus that's almost definitely going to kill you if you get bit, because you don't have THAT antidote yet.  But there's enough humans looking to gun you down that it pays to keep a rifle nearby, and the AI isn't smart enough to just curbstomp every zombie they come across, so they benefit from zome firearms skill.  But when you're scouring the countryside for loot, you don't need to pack too many bullets if you can just boot-to-the-head.

If you are a RL fan get this, you will not be disappointed.  Similarly, if you are a RU fan you might want to take a look at this.  I got the Lomu Rugby Challenge and loved that, despite me being a RL bigot first and foremost.  This compares very favourably with that.
Pros
+ Easy to pick up
+ Vast array of teams and stadiums
+ Can create your own teams and rosters. Loads of options for team kits.
+ On harder levels the game feels more like RL i.e. battling for field position, territory.  The realism is getting better with each patch
+ Good developers who listen and support the product. They've already made positive changes to the game e.g. the AI doesn't fling the ball around as much as they first did.
Neither good nor bad
* Career mode is solid although not much depth to it
* Playing a season is good but game doesn't have the depth of ageing, youth development etc. that you get with the multi-million pound projects like FIFA, but that's a minor issue considering how desperate I was for a decent rugby game)
Cons
- Occasional squad and roster disruptions when you download teams (this can be remedied by deleting official clubs which returns the squad back to its default state)
- Some player look-a-likes aren't that great (this is more of an issue with the UK teams, which I'm more familiar)
- Player ratings in the Super League a bit out of date e.g. Alex Walmsley rated 79 (minor quibble though that)
- Custom players seems to be an issue as I can't create new ones
Overall I love it.  Love it so much in fact that a group of middle-aged men are having a fantasty draft into our custom clubs on a boy's night tomorrow :)

A good game and definately recommendable considering it's free. This VN is about a girl telling about a dream in which she  tries to survive the pre- and aftermath of a nuclear war and it's actually pretty damn open-world for a interactive novel, there are various routes which actually differ from one another rather than a singular route with a few dialogue changes and several different endings. Tip: read through the achievements after playing this game a few times because some possibilities like stealing a car seem like dead ends if you don't know they can be done successfully.
The writing is good, and it has an unique detail that the story is told by a girl to a friend of hers rather than a first- or third person perspective, allowing Alice and Mad H. to comment upon the story from a hindsight perspective rather than Alice having to voice her thoughts during her adventure. Something I haven't seen before and which added a more casual tone to the otherwise traumatising adventures she has. The art and music are good as well.
The only lesser point of this game to me is the coding and system itself. There are at times bugs which ruin an ending and the skip button doesn't always work. Half the problems I've encountered would be fixed if this game were in Ren'py. I'm definately not saying that Unity isn't a good engine, but Ren'py would have been better for this game because it's specifically made for VN's like this one and many of the problems and bugs would not have occurred. And I haven't seen anything in this game in terms of code and gimmicks which Ren'py can't do as well. The other half of the problems lie in the system which the producers of this game made, and the lacking explanation they gave about it. I had to figure out half the stuff during my first few play-throughs and I didn't open my backpack for a long time because I couldn't find the button to return to the main story screen. Turns out my computer screen wasn't big enough to show this screen while the rest of the game had adapted to the alt. resolution I used.
Conclusion: I recommend this game if you like VN's or post-apocalypse simulator games, if not you can give it a shot anyways and make your own judgement after playing the game once or twice.

Wasn't so bad. The background art helped to set the majoirty of the scene. You're Alice and you're relating a dream you had about some kind of nuclear apocalypse to the Mad Hatter. I'll not spoil the rest for you.
PROS
1. Simple Artwork
This is much better than other narrative games that I've played. It sets the scene for where the story takes place.
2. Multiple Endings
I died due to radiation poisoning but yet the game gave hints that there is another path. I like different multiple endings a lot.
CONS
1. The Tedium of Repeating the Story
As much as I love games with multiple endings, it is the process of getting to the endings that matter more to me. Using the Witcher series as an example, I would be excited to play the game again if I was given a New Game Plus which would accelerate the 2nd or 3rd playthrough.
2. Character Intereractions
Not very good. You meet a NPC. You deal with them by choosing 1 out of 3 options, that's it. The characters are not interesting to interact with. For a lack of a better word, the characters have no character. The Mad Hatter is an example of a character, he asks about Alice and seems to be a friend, gives guidance and progresses the story.

For those who only read the first little bit of a review, I'll make this quick. I don't play a lot of ORPGs, I have too many games to play to play one for longer than a week or two. Also, I hate the auto-attack combat and the boring, genocidal quest lines (Kill 5 rats, kill 10 boars, etc) that most ORPGs use. ESO, however, has improved a lot over the past year, has a better feeling combat system and quests that are more interesting than kill # (insert animal here).
I played ESO in the beta and despite some flaws, I liked it. I'm not a fan of subscriptions so I never played it past the beta or went back. When I heard it went with a one time purchase model, I decided to give it another whirl. Here's some quick pros (+) and cons (-):
+I enjoy the combat. It's more involved than auto-attacking and just feels better. However, being an online game it's not 100% skill based and it's basically auto-aim turned up.
+The quests are story based. No more killing 10 wolves in that field and then killing 15 dire wolves in another field right afterwards. You start off thwarting assassinations, finding lost colleagues in ruins or helping a family with a drug problem. You're given choices to help or kill and while sure, these are one time decisions with no real impact and some mission objectives get samey, it's still far better (in my opinion, anyways) than genocidal 'kill X amount of X' quests.
+I like how the skills work, separating your class from your weapon so you can use whatever weapon you want with whatever class you want. I like how the skills level up from use and you're given the option to alter it by choosing one of two paths.
-I find it odd how combat skills will get xp for just being in your bar and not from using them. Also, more 'morph' choices would be nice to better differentiate characters.
-Game likes to boot me to the login screen randomly. Doesn't happen frequently enough to frustrate me but it can get annoying while playing with friends.
+The game looks good. Even on medium the graphics are pretty good.
+It maintains the TES feel of being able to go in any one direction and coming across quests or cool locations at random.
+The world itself looks good. Ruins, villages, swamps, forests all look good and are worth exploring.
+The crafting system, after a quick primer it's easy to start making your own equipment.  Plus the equipment you make can be as good as what you find, at least to a certain point, since I'm not at the endgame I can't say for sure at that point.
-You seem to be given almost too much freedom with building your character. Current you can get 300+ skill points which is more than enough to get every skill you want, including crafting skills meaning potentially, one character could craft, upgrade and enchant their own weapons and armour while still being able to produce their own potions and food.
+/- The new justice system is a mixed bag, allowing you to steal or kill but be caught as in other TES games. It's the beginning of what could be an interesting system depending on how far they take it.
Overall I enjoy the game, I think it's managed to separate itself from other MMORPGs and not be considered a 'theme park' ORPG.

This is not just Half-Life with a new coat of paint.  It is the classic you fell in love with years ago.  But it has been completely overhauled.  You'll start out just like the classic, visit familiar places and meet old friends.  But the locations have been upgraded and feel more alive.  The people you meet are more varied in appearence however there are some duplicate faces.  You get the best of both worlds in that way.  It is all familiar but new at the same time.  The old dialouge and story remains but new lines of dialogue are available and there are enhancemetns of new "puzzles" and new rooms.
The best analogy is to think of Cloud City in The Empire Strikes Back...remember how the hallways looked the same except where once there was a blank white wall you now saw a window with clouds and ships flying around after a CGI update?  It's the same here.  Where there was once an empty wall there may now be a new room.  And these rooms are populated and you can go in them and converse with people.  You can still do things like set off the alarms at the security station and blow up the meal in the microwave.  But there is a lot of new places to explore and things to try out.
The old enemies are back but enhanced in appearance.  They now more resemble what you see in Half-Life 2 and the expansion packs.  Not all the puzzles are the same.  Some are changed completely or just have a new twist to them in general.  If this game were just a "pretty new version" of the original it would only be worth playing for a few minutes without paying for it.  But it is a whole new yet completely familiar gameplay.  It is worth the $20 cost.
I am loving going back and spending lots of time back at Black Mesa.  There are some issues (though the worst so far is the flickering fluttering ties of the scientists...c'mon, fix it).  But overall I have not experienced any major bugs.  I have only played the single player game so can only comment on that.  And for players like me who are getting older, whose panful fingers have gotten stiffer with age and reflexes aren't as quick, know that you can use cheat codes if you have to that you wouldn't need before, but are a welcome help to offset these issues that come with older age.
Don't hesitate!  It is no wonder so many reviews are positive...this is a GREAT game update!!!  C'mon Gordon...they're waiting for you in the test chamber!

A mix of a visual novel and Groundhog Day, this game is about trying new options - and when I say options, I mean more than your dialogue choices. Something new about this particular VN is the ability to customize the protagonist's stats and inventory at the beginning, giving you different options as the story progresses, and affecting the success rate of certain choices.
There are a few bugs, but they aren't game breaking. For example, when equipping inventory, the first item may be visually unresponsive until a second action is done. The game only features about two songs in it's soundtrack, but this is natural for the game's length, and size, as well as price (Free!). It would benefit from a "Skip Read Text" section, as your starting stats and inventory choices may affect the text sublety, which you may end up skipping entirely, or reading the same text over and over again to find a simple - but possibly vital change in dialogue.

Great visual novel.

An accurate and highly improved remake of the original Half-Life. Not only they managed to retain the feel of the original game, but they also seamlessly enhanced the experience with a few changes here and there to keep the experience fresh even to those who finished the original hundreds of times.

Absolute garbage. While the free version runs smoothly for me with most settings maxed out, this one suffers from FPS drops and momentary freezes even on the lowest settings, without offering significant graphical improvements. Performance is especially bad when playing online, often making the game unplayable. Even just connecting to a server can take minutes. There's little new SP content. Xen is still notably missing, years after the original release, with zero indication of any progress on it.
If you're a HL1 deathmatch veteran who's in it for the online play, you'll be quite disappointed to discover nothing more than a Half-Life-flavored turd. All movement and weapon mechanics have been altered beyond the point of recognizability. It seems as though much effort has been put into slowing and dumbing down every single aspect of the game. All trick movements are gone, including the basic strafe-jump. There's a forced delay between consecutive long jumps or gauss jumps, explicitly preventing fast and fluid movement.
Crosshairs are far larger than they should be, with no way to adjust them. Fire rates for most weapons are significantly lower. Annoying recoil effects have been added, forcing you to readjust your aim after each shot. Zooming in with the crossbow is excruciatingly slow, and now requires holding down the mouse button. Laser-guided rockets are almost entirely unresponsive, and feel like they come out from somewhere other than your RPG, sometimes resulting in accidental suicide. SMG grenade trajectories are unnaturally straight, while hand grenade ones are unnaturally curved, reducing the usefulness of both weapons.
Unlike either HL1 or HL2, thrown hand grenades are hard to spot once they land, due to their reduced size and increased map decoration. Multiplayer maps are very detailed, far beyond what is appropriate, hindering both navigation and the ability to spot enemies in the distance. Ladders are far more annoying than either HL1 or HL2 ones. Map layout is more confusing, with details like jump pads and ladders getting lost in a sea of visual noise.
In short, absolutely abysmal game design, wholly unworthy of the source material. I strongly regret wasting $20 on this turd, and can't recommend it to anyone. Do yourself a favor and play the free version, since this new and expensive one offers more grief than improvements.

When I first booted up this game, I wasn't quite sure what to expect. But after having played it, I can safely say that I definitely didn't waste money on it.
First thing I wanna mention is the surprising amount of detail in this 12-year old game. Everything from Sam's chest moving with his breathing to all the small details in the background. The graphics in this game are really impressive for the time, if a bit dated.
The best stealth games I had played before this are the MGS-series, and, while I wouldn't necessarily say that it's better than those, it's definitely in the same league and probably has the best and most detailed stealth system I've seen in a long time. The system works like this: The darker the place you're in, the less likely you are to get spotted, and if the place you're in is too brightly lit, you will be spotted and killed almost instantly. You can lean up against walls, grab enemies from behind and drag them to a dark space to take them out, the amount of things you can do is stunning!
In this game, much like in MGS, GUNS are ♥♥♥♥ing GUNS. They will kill you in seconds if you're not careful. Your enemies are almost just as dangerous to you as you are to them. and that's one of the things I love about stealth games; avoiding enemies can be just as exciting, if not more exciting than engaging them.
To sum-up: If you like stealth games you're definitely gonna have to pick this game up, and if you haven't tried them before, Splinter Cell will make you realize what you've been missing out on.
I feel obligated to mention though, that the cutscenes ran like absolute crap. It wasn't because the framerate or resolution was low or anything like that. My screen just kept flashing all the time and it never stopped; it felt like I was having a seizure. Now, that may just be because of my PC running Windows 10, but to tell you the truth I have no idea what was causing it. This was only during cutscenes though, the gameplay, as far as I could tell, didn't have any problems like that.

I'm currently stuck on the last mission of the game, and thought this would be a good opportunity to review this game.
I have mixed feelings about it. It does not handle well, many features are almost or completely useless, environmental effects don't always work as intended.
I found myself using thermal vision twice during the game, both in late game. The tutorial shows you how to do a split jump maneuver where you wedge yourself between 2 walls several feet in the air. In the main game, I used this tactic a grand total of 0 times. The pistol is by far the most inaccurate firearm I have ever used in a game, requiring me to get with 10 feet to be at all accurate, and the assault rifle isn't much better. Kudos to the Rifle though for possibly being one of the most useful rifles ever thought of, as you can use the grenade launcher attachment to fire a wide variety of things that will help you in your game (though I didn't actually use any of them until the 3rd mission from the end).
The game has a light scale that shows you how visible you allegedly are, and I regularly found my slider telling me I was in full light, while I was in actuality in complete darkness.
The story itself isn't very impressive, it's your basic Tom Clancy's game where you have a foreign terrorist group intent on destroying America and her Allies. Having been made in the early 2000's, the accents are laughable.
All in all, the game is almost broken, but for some reason, still enjoyable, and one of few games in my Library that have held my interest for more than a few hours

I have been playing mmorpgs casually for the last 8 years and Twin Saga since open beta. Twin Saga is a full featureded casual mmorpg from X-Legend. It is 1 of 4 games that they are publishing in the west. If you want a game to play hardcore and/or PVP is an essetial part of your MMO experience you may want to look else where. The cartoony graphiics and fact that yor avatar looks about 10 my be a turn off. But while kid friendly most of the player base is over 18 and many players are in their 40s or 50s. Is it pay to win?. Icf by that do you mean you can advance more quickly and put extra bonuses on your gear then yes it is. Do you have to spend money in the cash shop to enjoy the game then the answer is no. All the game features ar available to free players and you can get geared up to do the content without spending a dime..
The 2 main features in the game are the ability to play any class and the terra cottage. The game tries to streamline and simplifiy all the game systems. As such all classes use the same gear. And character and class level are seperate. Since gear is determined by character level you will not have to go back to the starting zones when you start a new class. Main function fo terra cottage is as a base of operation. It can be accessed from anywhere in the open wolrd and gives you access to bank, vendors, potions, action house, and all your different crafting activites. This is very handy  but does mean there is little reason to go into town.  If you like story there is a lot here. Both the main quest line, conversations you can listen in on, hidden quests, and asteral adventures. Many of these will give you titlies whch will provide small bonuses.
Character creation is rather limited, you can only be human and a few hairstyles, colors, eye colors and skin tones. You will get a lot of choices with clothing appearance. X-Legend chos not to illistrate armor but rather give you outfit/costume choices. You will get an outfit to start out with a few more to choose from with sme early quests. You can also craft outrfits and buy costumes in item mall. Will also get 1 free costume in first 10 days of playing. Should note there are several in game currencies the most important fo which is loyalty pionts. Many things you can buy with cashcan also be gotten with loyalty points.
While much of the game can be done solo there are several things that can be done as group. There is a good guild system with guild activities. Several different forms fo dungeons, which include solo, party, hard, meta, and nghtmare. There is a good in game paty finder. Pick the dungeon you want then rtecruit and bradcast. You can do open world acctivities till you get your party togather. Then just hit the warp button and it will bring all party members to the dungeon entrance on the same channnel. You can change dungeons without having to start a new group. The game has a very nice community with lots of friednly and helpful players. If you want a great casual game you would be hard pressed to find a betterr choice.

Twin Saga is a MMORPG in an Anime style. Sadly this is the best to tell about this game.
The combat system of Twin Saga is extremly simple. You just have very low cooldowns and spam mindlessly your buttons until the mob is dead. There isn't really anything to do within combat which would justify to do more. Rarely a boss mob appears where you need to circle the boss to avoid damage, but even receiving the AoE damage is barely noticable. You also have an auto-use function for potions (of which you easily have 100+ only by doing quests).
This is actually the biggest flaw of this game. The questing is extremely bland (mainly due to the fact that you can auto-run to everything by clicking on the quest objective). Thus exploring isn't necessary and you don't even have to think about anything as the game does the thinking for you.
Additionally, before taking any quest, you are bombarded with a textwall every time. It is more like reading a book completely made up of dialog (aka stage play). Even when you're tasked to pick up 3 flowers for something the text walls just increases the dislike to read anything, especially in an MMO.
The is mainly thanks to the bad questing, but even when you want to look at the world, it doesn't look that pretty. Within an area every location looks almost the same and you don't have to orientate for anything, thus leaving you disoriented at any given moment.
This were this game fails the most. It brings nothing new to the table of MMOs. You've seen everything anywhere else and executed better.
This game may appeal to an audience which hardly wants to play every anime-styled game there is AND wants to read a lot (if they want to know the lore). I am not one of those and thus do not recommend this game.

First off, i want to say that this game gets much more hate than it deserves. It is almost like the COD hatetrain where everyone just throws hate at everything without doing any research.
The majority of the weapons on armas are
of weapons that already exist in the game, for example: Joker CR-5 = N-TEC 5, PSR = N-HVR, STAC = Joker SR15 etc. PLUS,
Flamewars aside, there are some good things and some bad things with this game:
The gunplay in this game is fun, satisfying and pretty easy to pick up. The game uses a hitreg system which means that all the shots are instant which means that you dont have to lead or compensate for bullet drop like in ArmA or Battlefield. There are various of weapons to use: Shotguns, SMGs, LMGs, Snipers, Assault Rifles, Rocket Launchers, Crowd Control Weapons and many more.
. There are four types of grenades along with other throwables (like bricks): Frag grenades, Percussion grenades, Concussion grenades and Low yield Frag grenades. Frags: standard grenades. Percs: explode on impact, less damage than frags. Concs: Small explosive radius, full damage (if you get hit by a well placed Concussion grenade you will die from basically anything afterwards. you can also "one shot" most cars in the game). L-Y Frags: weighs less than the other grenades so you can carry 3 instead of 2. Flies faster but does slightly less damage than regular Frags.
This variety of weapons to utilize means that you can play the game at any range you want, with any playstyle you want.
The customization in this game is insanely good, and that is something you will think about whenever you decide to customize in this game. You can make your own symbols, put them on your cars and clothes, put them on your forehead (if you like that kind of stuff). The clothing variety also means that no one looks the same in this game, and i mean it. If you want, you can even spend a penny or two to buy exclusive clothing at armas like backpacks and top hats. The vehicle customization is also insane. I have spent a good many hours in the vehicle editor to get that perfect design and it feels great when you can roll out on the streets with your fresly painted cars. The character customization is also very good. It is insanely detailed which opens up for some serious character roleplay. You can put scars on your character, make a full body tatoo and look like a smurf, the editor is so detailed, that you can even change what kind of body hair your character has. The fact that the game runs on a pretty old engine is a bit of a problem for something like hairstyles though, as they often look very plastic and glossy. This will probably be fixed in long awaited engine update.
Yes, there are quite a lot of hackers in this game, but that is not because it is a bad game, it is because it is a free to play shooter. all free to play shooters will at some point have problems with hackers. It is much more availible to cheat in a free to play game than in a paid game since you dont run the risk of losing the money spent on purchasing the game if you get banned (which you will). There is tho a big problem with hackers at the time that im typing this since there has been released a new cheat which seems to be much harder to detect bur very obvious to spot. You will see someone teleporting around the streets, their heads and bodies spinning as they shoot. If you see one of these guys, please take your time to report them using the /report [player] command in chat.
We are all praying that the engine update will come soon. Veterans such as myself have seen the engine update being delayed too many times. The only thing that i know is that the game, in its current state runs on a very old engine and it needs a new one. How good or bad the engine update will be is something to discuss when it is released.
The community while somewhat more toxic than other games is pretty ordinary. I think it has to do with how lucky you are when you meet people in the game. Stay with the people you know and like, ignore the jackasses who flame, its as easy as that.

Solid game. I doubt you'll play it for the entire duration of the game, but there is 60$ worth of entertainment out of the box. ESO could be one of the greats if they only adjusted a few minor things. Here goes what I suggest they do to "complete" the Elder Scrolls experience.
1) Once the game is beaten, scale all low level content to the player's level. If you're lvl 50 in a lvl 1 zone, the zone should be adjusted to lvl 50. The only excdeption would be if a low lvl friending invited you to help him, then you would enter his world-space. The fundamentals of this are already in place via Megaserver tech.
2) Remove faction boundries and let all players go anywhere in the world. Make Cyrodill a Guild Vs. Guild thing instead of a RvR thing.
3) Minor tweaks to quests for continuity and immersion. Either drop a quest chain (dependent on player's point in game) or simply alter a few lines of dialogue. Not a-lot has to be done here. Other tweaks such as Morrowind/Oblivion style crafting are now implementable. Since all zones/content is now end-game content, making crafting more in line with Skyrim or Oblivion than it is currently starts to make sense.
What is my reasoning behind these three major changes? Well, it would turn ESO into a full-on Elder Scrolls game instead of an MMO set in the Elder Scrolls universe. Right now I can only experience high level versions of opposing factoin conetnt, not my own. It would give me a reason to go back and explore other areas in a way that seems natural to an Elder Scrolls game. It would let me team up with players from other factions and it would make Cyrodill three times larger and that much more interesting. It's the right thing for the game.
Now, how to package and deliver this? I would suggest making most or all of this a free update, but if development costs soar and you need some return on the investment, I would suggest selling it as a "Veteran Content Upgrade" for say 3000 crowns. Throw in the Imperial Race on top of it. Elder Scrolls fans would feel right at home and virtually every single serious player would buy it.

Posted on the forums, had a terrible feeling we were getting another shoddy pc port of a game, dev replied within minutes of me bringing up the issue and told me how to fix it for the mean time and that there would be a patch in the next day that would fix the issue completely.

Now to the review itself. Big Ant and Tru Blu really do have to be commended for the product that they've released. As a small time dev and publisher they've released a game that can be held in the same regard as fifa and the 2k series, despite the modest budget that they had to work with.
Everything about the game of rugby league is captured in this digital rendition. Players behave like they should, they move like they should, and they mostly look like their real life counter parts.
The game has all of the official players and teams for the southern hemisphere but not for the North, depending on where you live this is either going to be a problem or not one at all, and even in saying that, there is the awesome fan hub which allows you to download created players that other people have made, some of them are truley awesome and look like the real people they are based off of, so getting the right players for the northen hemisphere should be no trouble at all.
The game has all the usual content you'd expect from a sports game. Quick match, online, career and so on, but it's the options like being able to take control of your favourite superstar and guide him through his career or take a rookie from the age grades on up to representative footy that make this game even more fun than it already is.
During your season you will be faced with optional challenges to raise your clubs finances, like completing so many tackles or fends in a match, these finances help when you're trying to lure the next super star to your club for the next season as you have players coming off contract, but these optional challenges are not actually required for you to be able to recruit and don't break the game in anyway.
You'll also have the a few judiciary hearings along the way as no doubt your players are going to get pinged for wreckless tackles and face suspension, another facet of the game that just adds to the realism, being able to decide how you plead is icing on the cake
The graphics for this game are really good, the game has amazing IQ and is capable of supporting 4k resolution should you have the machine capable of running it.
The commentary is sadly mostly the same as the Rugby League Live 2 with Andrew Voss and Gus calling the plays, It's not too bad and is actually a lot better than other games that you'll play
The sound is great at capturing the atmosphere of a real life footy game. What with the sound of the excited fans the explosions of fire works when someone goes over for a try or when a forward crunches into a would be tackler, and it's even better with a good pair of headphones.
If there was one negative that really needs to brought to attention it'd be the fact that the game has to be online to be played. I can understand why the dev and publisher took this route though, League is niche game and piracy eating into already small sales would cripple this franchise and bring about the end of future pc releases.
All in all this is a fantastic sports game and shouldn't be avoided if you're a fan of League. Even comparing this game to the rugby union games that have been released in recent months and years just shows that you don't need a "AAA" budget to accuratley capture the heart and soul of  a game, just a dev that wants to please the fans and put out something that they're proud off.
I have no doubt that Big Ant and Tru Blu are very proud of this, and they have every right to be.

My excpectation is not as high as many of these down voters, I am more cautious, because a lot of these games are very complex to made and people behind these games work so hard to complete it. Thankfully I didnt play this game on the first day, so I never encountered the major performance issues. A day later after the game came out, I decided to play and I was surprised with a huge update, took nearly 5 hours! I got curious about this monster update and I learned a major problem with "game breaking" issues with framerates. There's another catch, since im still using windows 7, the game refused to launched! it turns out my DirectX 11 needs upgrade to 11.5. My PC is really old, but it had been recently upgraded,  it comes with Intel Core i7 920 2.67 GHZ with 18GB memory. My video card is a single GeForce 970 GTX with 4.8 GB. This is far from a high end gaming PC.
The game was automatically set to "high" and the framerate is reasonable. When I reached Karnaca for the first time, I had noticed a very slight stutter, its not really the game breaking people had been talking about earlier. The 6GB upgrade, along with driver upgrade from NVidia, fixed most of these nasty problems. I completed the game (logged 42 hours ) with no major issues, except for a bug that might tarnish your non lethal playthrough, but a workaround is available from message boards. I only encountered a single CTD, I considered this a hiccup rather than a fatal one. The plot is not Oscar worthy, but it is compleling enough to keep you playing, the visuals are amazing and the gameplay is superb and the control is fairly responsive enough I was able to escaped several sticky situation. The level design is excellent and the clockwork mansion and the time bending stage is quite innovative. The overall experience is not as strong as the first one, but I still  had a great time playing it. I recomended this game for experienced PC gamers, who does their own homework.

Alright, so I've played through Black Mesa a few times ever since the initial mod release a couple years back.
Today was the day I was waiting for three years for: to see the mod finally up on Steam and having some semblance of progress towards a full release. I LOVE this mod, not because it simply updates the old Half-Life game...
No, this mod retells the story that Valve first told decades ago in the late 90s, much better, ironically, than they ever could have done. You don't play through the Black Mesa Incident anymore, you live through it. You don't simply stroll on in late to work, you stop and talk to people who know and work with you every day, people who all have their own relationships with you...
Which makes it all the more hard-hitting when the Resonance Cascade hits, and hits hard at that, and you are left to piece together what happened from the ashes not only your home, but the homes of many others. This is not a Half-Life remake, this is quite simply, what Half-Life is.
Now that my gushing over this amazing mod is out of the way, I'd like to take a moment to address the "controversy" over this being a paid mod. Not a few weeks ago, the whole Skyrim Workshop debacle got me just as ruffled up as anyone else. It was a very flawed system, and I did everything I could to help contribute to getting the system removed. That said, BLACK MESA IS NOT WORKSHOPGATE 2.0!
For one, they've said for at least a year now that they would have a paid version on Steam, so it shouldn't be surprising to anyone who's actually followed the mod. Also, you can still get the mod for free off their site. Finally, this game, and its very talented development team, deserves to be paid for. Not only has the Crowbar Collective matched Valve's quality, it has surpassed it. For years, this team has worked on this mod to retell one of the most influential stories in gaming's history, and in my opinion, their work is more than worthy of my hard-earned cash.
Also, if you haven't gathered this so far, the Crowbar Collective isn't some team of chuckles that simply makes mods, they put love and effort into their work. Yes, they may not work as fast as we want at times (believe me, two years of waiting to see this mod finally up showed me that much), but they deliver something that is worth the wait.
So, now that my review is done, all I can say is good work Crowbar Collective, and I recommend that any person who enjoys the Half-Life series, mods, First-Person Shooters, or video games in general give this mod a shot. You don't have to buy it immediately, you can check out the free version, which does a great job of showing off the mod. Then, if you're like me, and believe the Collective is worthy, you can give the team a bit of your cash for their well-done work.
10/10 Crowbar Collective, Black Mesa has always been, and I anticipate will always be, one of the shining beacons of what modding can be.

Twin Saga, a game filled with adventure around every corner! I have played a lot of MMORPG's in my years of gaming and I must say that this one, at least for me, tops them all! I can proudly say that Twin Saga is the best MMORPG I've ever played! Twin Saga was released on Steam on September 1st 2017, one year after it's initial release. Don't be confused by the time it says I've played this on Steam. I've been using the download I got from the Twin Saga site, and I prefer to use it instead. I started playing Twin Saga with my fiancé towards the end of January of this year. I can proudly say that we've loved every minute of it! For us, this game never gets boring. There is always something to work on! My only regret in Twin Saga is not finding it earlier. The graphics are anime-styled and absolutely gorgeous! If you have a graphics card that can handle high graphics settings I suggest using them! Sometimes I take a break from my dailies, and just look out at the beautiful scenery this game has to offer. The storyline is also great! But cuteness and a great storyline is not all this game has to offer, it's also got switchable classes! Your weapon also automatically switches to match the class you pick! Yes, you heard that right! You can switch your class at any time, and the weapon switches with you! Speaking of combat, every title you obtain has stats attached to it and... They stack! You don't have to wear the title in order to receive the stats it gives! If you prefer to play solo, it is doable. However, I suggest playing with some friends because it makes the game more fun! Don't have any friends that want to play Twin Saga with you? You're sure to find some in game, because the community here is awesome!
Now, let's talk about what most people complain about regarding this game. Spending money. You don't have to buy AP (Aeria Points) if you don't want to. It is not a must in order to progress in this game. It will get you things quicker, but there are other methods to getting what you want in the game. There are many different types of currency in the game that you can use, that do not involve spending money. Loyalty points are one type that can be used to buy many things in game! You receive these by simply doing daily quests, weekly quests, senshi quests, and more! You will understand what I mean once you begin to play the game.
This game has much more to offer than just these few things, but you'll get to explore the rest for yourself!
Enjoy, and have fun!

Been playing for a while now and it's very disappointing to see some of the issues I'm seeing.  I know the game is old but I don't think that excuses it from being held to some basic standards.  For example, there are plenty of times when there are no lights in the room but the game's "light detection system" shows the area as being well lit.  Without night vision, it's pitch black, but the light indicator shows full visibility and enemies easily see you.  It's either shoddy design or a nasty bug, but it happens way too often to be excusable in a game that relies on stealth through darkness.  I've died too many times while shuffling through a dark alleyway to find out that every enemy sees me clear as day, and it becomes a game of watching the light indicator to ensure that there are no bugged out lights in your path.
There's also sound issues.  You can be 20 feet from an enemy and he'll turn when you make a slight mistake.  Normally you are able to move comfortably at a much closer distance, but sometimes enemies have superhuman hearing that ruins your plans.  Another big issue is that when you move diagonally, you have to press 2 keys (W+A/D) and the game registers that as 2 movements, meaning anytime you move diagonally, you move twice as fast and make twice as much noise.  You can work around this by only using W and moving the mouse to turn, but sometimes you need to keep an eye on other enemies and it isn't practical to make the compromise.  Also, it might just be the design of the game, but your stealth walking speed is slower than an enemies normal walking speed, so if your behind an enemy who's walking away, you will not reach him to eliminate him.  You'd think an NSA Splinter Cell would know how to move quickly and quietly but he's slow as a snail.
I would love to enjoy this game and I did for the most part.  I just can't bother myself to finish it when the core mechanic of the game (stealth) is so flawed by bugs.  The quicksave and quickload features got me through 9 hours of this game but I hate that I have to use those features because of the game's problems and not my own mistakes.  If they ever remake this game with a new engine, I'd buy it in a heartbeat but I can't play it as it is.  Stealth games should have working stealth mechanics and this game is just bad enough that I don't want to play anymore.
