Oi, most of the ♥♥♥♥♥ing from players that have less than 4 hours in the game? Mate, let me explain this game, although i may jump around a lot the point is there. Controls are simple, like real simple. There is a take all button but not for buildings, I assume this was done because most buildings have heavy building materials (wish there was a hot key though, but they make up for this by saving the last position of your cursor so it's basically double clicking for take all instantly.) Pistol is ok early game but about 20 minutes in you will find a shotgun, and should probably only use the shotgun until a few hours later where you can get your hands on a sniper rifle which does increase the viewing distance by what feels double, and allowing you to target zombies before they can see you. The fog you move through is understandable but the sniper rifle viewing distance should be the default. Story is actually engaging minus the fact that even though you are playing as Joe, it really feels more like you should be playing Alice, because of her serious insulin problem which the majority of the story is written around knowing there is a finite number of insulin so she will inevitably die, but you can 'complete the game' before that happens.  The AI for the people you recruit is almost aids sometimes but if you build your defenses correctly and assign members to defend, you literally wont run into any problems at your base, but while you're out and about, let's just say you better prepare each individual you take with you for what ever you plan on doing because if not properly prepared chaos will occur without a doubt. As an example, if one of your guys runs out of bandages, they will probably run nonstop if being chased by someone shooting at them, making it impossible to save their life, but again if you assess your situation and set up a strategy, you're golden. What I suggest is take Joe, Alice, and Isham all with shotguns with about 100 rounds each to where ever you're going and that should be good for just about every situation and assign all of your other members to do stuff at your base. Just make sure to bring a few bandages as well incase you do get shot. If you are vigilant, getting bit is highly unlikely. What I also suggest is instead of sprinting, use the fast forward buttons during traveling (omg theres so much walking not even funny, so glad for fast forward.) There are magazines in the game that give +1 to a respective stat and these do stack and if you know where all the locations of these magazines are, you could effectively max out firearms, have a sniper rifle, and be a 1 man army very quickly. Back packs, without them, the game would be unplayable but at max fitness and the largest back pack, you can hold a ton of stuff except building materials which are insanely heavy but you really don't need that many building materials as there aren't really that many options for buildings but enough to get you through the game. I don't think the dev's focus was on building a city, it was surviving the zombies and for what you get, you can actually set up a really sweet base camp just west of the bunker almost directly north of the building you get the chips in for the first 'eating quest' there's basically a little nook there that only forces you to build about 6 fences, 1 gate, and 1 watch tower and have 1 guard with max firearms and an assault rifle (literally only use for assualt rifle please do not even bother trying to use in open world or for anything else besides a max firearm base guard it's probably the worse weapon in the game) Be careful with the decisions you make in the game as they will constantly remind you if you make bad ones, including the loss of respect/approval for gaining trust of another survivor. At a certain point in the game you realize you are just doing the same thing you did at the beginning but just faster and more difficult and end up just going on a one man mission because you will probably find it easier to control just Joe with the magazines to max his stats out, sniper rifle in hand and the double tapped fast forward button. Gifts, lots of gifts, get the brain scanner to see what people like for gifts, dont offer the wrong gifts to people. More gifts than weapons? Smoking causes lung cancer be careful who loots zombies corpses, they may die unexpectedly because they have been secretly smoking without you knowing. Sneaking is totally a thing, distractions are totally a thing, just think outside the box.
All in all this is probably one of the best games I have ever played at this cost, and I picked it up for 50% off. I never thought I would have spent over 50 hours playing this but I felt I couldn't get enough. If you can look past having to almost inevitably lose progress from a single poor decision or mistake then this game will entertain you for days or even weeks. If you can't look past losing progress a lot, still get the game and atleast have a go at some of the achievements as they can be very challenging and interesting.
Note that you can solo the entire game without the aid of any community members or building a base and allow Alice to die with no real threat to the completion of the game, just be prepared to save the game before every encounter.
Best $2.49 I ever spent.

Borderlands 2 is a fun game the first time you play it through. The characters are awesome, the landscape is great, picking through the enormous pile of guns available to you is hella fun, the combat rocks.... but there are some rough edges. The Fast Travel system interface is confusing as hell unless you have a quest to go somewhere specific. The constant back-tracking and tedious walking around you have to do is lightened up a little by all the extra hidden stuff there is to find, but it's still a chore. Several I've found myself getting killed because I've been stuck on... well, nothing - the quality of the level design leaves a *LOT* to be desired. But for all that, I really enjoyed playing through this game first time. 9/10, great effort.
However, when it comes to the second play through with the difficulty ramped up... Quite simply, it ramps up too high, too fast. With one of my characters I have actually got myself into a position when I can't do anything at all to respec (thanks to the point of the storyline I'm currently working through) and need to kill something completely unlike anything I've seen so far, which can melee 2HK me *from 50 yards away* and is surrounded by landscape and features so ridiculously bugged, it's unreal. Put simply - play this game through once with each character class, then uninstall it and never play it again. The replayability features are *HORRENDOUSLY* badly done.

Dear potential customer,
please be very aware about the state of the game: When it does not have latency issues it is a pretty solid call of duty. SP is worth playing and somewhat challenging and MP is pretty much CoD + a bit of Titanfall. It even suffers from the same issues, e.g. when it comes to balancing the first assault rifle is better than pretty much everything you can unlock. However currently it is not playable for various reasons:
- Some maps tend to load slow on modern hardware hiting the connect timeout leaving you stuck connecting.
- Obvious bugs that did not see an easy fix yet (e.g. akimbo smg + silencer can be heard by every player on the map, bf4 anyone?)
- Game balancing was obviously only done on consoles. They nerfed everything that isn't smg. One of the biggest discussion on BO2 was about Akimbo PDW being overpowered. Same goes for akimbo in mw3. Same goes for akimbo sparrows on mw2. They did not learn from this. They even created a balance that attracts even more of that discussion by adding an akimbo smg (akimbo only) that works like a headshot magnet. On the other hand the best sniper in the game for quickscoping (and I'm not talking camping here) was nerfed to do about 1/3 hitmarkers only. Clays were reduced to delayed easy to dodge explosives. You don't even need to be careful anymore as they have a sound playing once they get activated leaving you with enough time to get away from them. Don't get me started on map design, as they removed EVERY tactical spot on those maps. There is not a single map left with a spot that might majorly influence the match' outcome.
- Spawn system is terribly broken often leaving you in front of an enemy. In wide areas (e.g. a prison yard) this can easily be abused.
- Connectivity issues. Beforehand they promised dedicated servers, after release they announced it is some sort of mix. Actually my belief is that it's only p2p for games leaving dedicated servers for the ingame voice... If you compare the netcode of let's say mw2 to AW it is obvious that this sucks. When mw2 came out, people flamed when their bodies dropped after passing the line of sight. This was obviously lag related. In BF3/4 that got somewhat default and got accepted by the masses and now even cod has this. Expect to die a lot in unfair situations that are obvious lag related.
- And the worst: Skill based match making. It is combined with a portion of connection based match making, so your match is probably not going to leave your continent areas. However the further you get in the game, the more punishing it gets. I'm currently on prestige 8 and it's no fun anymore as finding a game is getting more difficult. With the small size of the PC cod community this is toxic and creates more frustration then solving anything (it does not resolve noob stomping anyways as they will still get matched into your games). SBMM is simply reducing very even games to connection issues. Even if the teams are balanced skillwise, the match will come down to lag shield winning.
I can only highly encourage everybody to pass on this one and wait for the next installment by Treyarch (should be the next cod). In my humble opinion it feels like fraud if the publisher/developer knows about this (as CM confirmed on twitter) and they do nothing to solve those concerns. They even create a new playlist claiming to include favorite maps just to hide the first issue with not loading maps. They also pushed a free weekend to overcome the fact that high rank players cannot find valuable matches anymore (and dropping them into a lot of unfair matches consisting of high rank player + noobs vs. somewhat experienced players).
Thanks for reading.

ABSOLUTELY BRILLIANT! The game on PC really puts the console versions to shame. The visuals are absolutely stunning, esp with Sweetfx enabled. The grass in particular is the best I have seen of any sports game, and the created players really come to life. In terms of eye candy, you simply could not ask for any more. The gameplay is extremely smooth and responsive, and it runs perfectly all settings maxed out on my fairly moderate system.
This game has real depth and the more you play it, the more you realise just how much of a simulation it is. The ball physics in partcular are first class. I feel that the compeition options and customisation could be a bit more expansive like DBC, but hopefully this will be added down the line in patches etc. The fanhub is again the best player creator I have seen to date, and with enough time and patience, it is possible to create players who really look authentic, visually. BUT.......I personally do not like everything about the way the stats system is done. I realise they did it this way to prevent cheating and having super players, but as it stands you are not able to create players with their unique and specific skill set. Many people have voiced their concern about this on the forums, and seeing as Big Ant are great listeners to the public, I hope that this will be changed in a patch, so that we can alter the stats individually, so that each player has a true to life representation of their skill set.
Another area where the PC version shines is in the modding department. Already we can load custom Jerseys and Logos, but hopefully this will be greatly expanded down the line, to include Balls, Referee Kits, Field Markings, Adboards, Crowd Clothing etc. The mere possibility is extremely mouthwatering and adds such great authenticty, especially for the retro/classic content.
So is it worth getting the PC version.....ABSOLUTELY!!!!! Why? The visuals are far more stunning, it runs alot smoother, the mods will be epic AND it will see alot more patches and support (ala DBC).
The lads at Big Ant deserve a medal for this masterpiece and I know with a little fine tuning and expanded options and mods it will be the ultimate Rugby League gaming experience. A wonderful company who really care about what the fans think and their willingness to listen and support is second to none.
For those of you baulking at getting the PC version.....IT IS WORTH EVERY PENNY!!!!!

The graphics are stunning, and it all runs very smoothly (over 100fps on my GTX970)
I'd go as far as to say this looks and feels like a FIFA or 2K title.
The gameplay is tough and whilst there are Drills which help improve the basics you'll have to figure out the rules and tactics of the game as you go along.
It has all the key elements of a modern sports sim, with a My Player career mode, coach career mode, exhibitions, leagues and multiplayer etc.
The sound is pretty realistic and on the whole very authentic, with some great bone crunching tackles. The commentators aren't quite as varied as their FIFA/2K counterparts but they are a million times better than Blood Bowl 2...

The easiest way I can review this game is to say that it is to Dark Souls as Street Fighter III Third Strike was to Street Fighter II Turbo.
They are games in the same series, and they share similar mechanics and features, but they are each different games in their own right.
Honestly, I enjoyed parts of DS 1 more than I did DS II, and vice versa. I preferred the beginning areas of DS 1, but I prefer DS 2's middle and ending areas more.
I preferred DS 1's humanity mechanics to DS 2's, but I prefer DS 2's covenants, invasions, summons, and overal online interactions. I didn't play DS 1 until 2013, so the community had begun to wither by then. Being able to interact with so many people in DS 2 is just incredible.
I prefered DS 1's NPC interactions more, but the NPC characters in DS 2 are just as engaging and do a great job of painting the narrative picture of Drangleic.
I greatly prefer DS 2's upgrade systems, combat, and variety of weapons.
All in all, it is a great game, but vastly different from DS 1. DS 1 has an ethereal sort of charm to it, a desolate beauty. DS 2 has more of a hopeful, nomadic feel to it, but in the end both games are incredible and I'd highly recommend DS 2.

This game is a step in the right direction for horror but still needs some tweaks. Like all games there are flaws due to the fact you can't make the perfect AI and that is where a lot of this game's length comes from.
The atmosphere is very well done, it has just the right amount of dark and spooky for a near abandoned space station. The game is bright enough you don't need to burn though your flashlight batteries in most areas but the vents are nearly pitch black. It has it's creaks and groans along with the noises from you and the alien stomping around but otherwise is near silent. The silence really helps as it allows you to hear doors down the hall opening enabling you to track foes without popping up your motion detector. My only audio/visual complaint is that the lack of dynamic shadows; as it is you can't tell if somebody is around the corner without peeking and possibly being seen since they don't cast shadows.
The gameplay is pretty good, it works as intended most of the time. You can lean in all directions like in the Thief games, which is helpful for peeking around corners and silly at the same time, I see no use for leaning backward or forward in this game. You get a few guns so you can fight back against the humans and much sturdier androids though they do no damage to the alien and the noise will attract it so you are usually better off sneaking around them. You find blueprints and use scraps to craft things like noisemakers and molotovs. Crafting and healing are done in real time so you have to choose ahead of time if you would rather a pipebomb to blow up a few humans or androids or a couple noisemakers to distract them. My biggest gripe is that you can't seem to be able to pick up stuff and throw it, if you want to distract something you must use a flare or craft and use some type of grenade.
The main thing that makes or breaks the game for people though is the AI, specifically of the alien. It can hear and see very well. It can hear the beeps from your motion detector and see the light from you holding a molotov. If it suspects you are in a locker it will attempt to detect you by your breath. It is also smart to an extent, if it sees a door opened it will  check the room within because it knows that means something passed through or near the door recently.
The problem is his movement. It cannot stray more than a few meters away from you. It could never see you but as soon as you get too far away it will jump in the vents to run ahead to your new area. This doesn't mean it is always breathing down your neck though. Instead of moving around in set patterns like guards in most stealth games it moves around pseudo-randomly. Sometimes it will decide to double back, other times it will wander into a side room. It can also jump up into the vents and move around giving you more freedom for awhile. On one hand this is great as it means it's not just a matter of watching it's pattern then moving when it's on the other side of the map. you actually have to be careful. On the other hand sometimes this randomized stupidity means you have to sit around for a long time hoping it will leave the room you are hiding in. One time I sat under a medical bed for around ten minutes waiting for him to stop pacing around the doorway. This means the more often than not you are in an area for far too long due to the alien needing to be encouraged to leave the level exit area.
Overall it is a fun and tense game, never knowing when the alien will decide it wants to actively hunt you means you have to check every room for hiding spots before moving too far into them and trapping yourself. Even in 'safe' areas I'm always checking the motion detector because I never know when the alien might crawl out of a vent. Unfortunately though, the amount of time it takes the alien to decide he wants to check another room means one section could take anywhere from ten minutes to an hour. It is definitely a good game but only if you can enjoy a slowness even larger than that that usually comes with playing stealth games.

The reviews are pretty mixed. As a huge dishonored fan (i absolutely LOVED the first version), let me walk you through why that is.

pros:
-interesting story line (although i feel Dishonored original had a more gripping/emotional story)
-lots to do (took me 12 hours to do my first playthough, am currently on the second)
-plenty of ways to play; whether you like going high chaos (killing everyone) or truly playing as an assassin, this game makes any combination of play-styles fun and rewarding (although, it is much more challenging taking it slow and avoiding killing anyone)
-artwork in game is beautiful. No, it's not ultra realistic, but it's beautiful in its own way
-lots of interaction with the world (killing someone or sparing someone will change the story)
-plethora of side-quests/extra actives
-supernatural abilities are f***ing cool, no other way to put it.
cons:
-performance is pretty bad. I have a gtx 970 sc and get 60+ FPS in indoor areas, but many of the "larger" areas (such as long streets, or the view from the top of a big building) drops my fps to 45. It's still very playable, but
or the negative reviews are from the FPS. Some people reported artifacting or screen tearing, i have not experienced these issues.
overall, i love this game. I bought the special edition pre-order (with the mask and ring) and do not regret spending a penny of the $100 price tag. If you have not played the original Dishonored, i highly recommend you buy that before purchasing dishonored 2. It's not critical to the in game story, but many of the letters you find or smaller "lore" findings need the original dishonored story to make sense.

Very surreal, but very beautiful and relaxing.
Ran smoothly on my 5+ year old toaster desktop, no glitches or stutters, no hitches or crashes. Ran like butter.
The art style is very pretty, very surreal, very colorful, and very well suited for what this game* is. It really is an experience, more so than a game. No rush, no need to hurry through things. Somewhat unintuitive, clues as to what to click and when aren't really there. You just click, see what does what, what changes what, and see what doing hings in different orders does.
Which was really part of the enjoyment and charm of this title for me. I love exploring, and just playing with stuff to see what it does and what happens. With no pressures to hurry up and complete a goal or finish a quest. I can play around and just enjoy the sound and sights. Very good experience for me, relaxing, and very stress relieving.
Very important things for me right now, as I go through chemo in my middle age. Yeah. Stress relief is important to me right now. And this title gave me that. And although some may see no replayability here (other than idling to get the last achievement), I honestly think this will be something I will come back to when I just need to stop the world, breathe, and dream a bit.
My only real complaint is that there needs to be some sort of contrast added to the cursor and hand icon, and possibly the character. Even a very thin black outline. Because in the brighter, whiter scenes, they all just disappear, leaving you clicking blindly and moving the camera around to try to find them again. That blindness was a bit disorienting, and did detract somewhat from the calm, relaxing feel the rest of the experience has.
Well worth the full asking price, very inexpensive, and the experience is worth much more. My opinion. Your Mileage May Vary. Widely. But I still think you should pick this up for some good downtime relaxation.
I'll be back. I have all but the last achievement. And that one will come on it's own, with time. I just want to go back with the new Dreamwalker. And see if I missed anything. And just breathe.

This is like one of those games you could say "an oldie but goodie"... sarcastically, solely because you hold on to the feeling that you *need* to play some type of zombie survival thing; not because it's good. It's got potential, got a story, and some stuff that obviously required some deep thinking to implement; but also got very simple faults that'd keep any seasoned player from enjoying the game.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Here's a few reasons why it sux:~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
-About the ui-
The game feels really old, like it was made in 2002 or something, because the interface is really bad, like "you had better things to do and let your 10yo kid design AND code it for you" bad. Like first-timer bad. There isn't even a loot all option, you end up interacting with each item stack one by one everytime. Say you wanna get 100 pistol ammo. You can't just type 100 after you find the ammo.. you know, like usual.. you gotta use your mouse to adjust the number with the slidebar popup. Then you hit enter.... 2 more times and nothing happens lol. Items don't have icons or different colors, or anything that'd make em look different than all the other stuff in your inventory. You end up scrolling through a name list of everything if you're looking for something specific.
-Viewing distance and fog of war-
The distance you can see and shoot at, relative to the distance a zombie can cover in a second (zombies always run btw), is too short. Kind of makes having eyes useless, you have eyes but can't see beyond like 10 paces. Makes having guns pretty useless too though they deal way better dmg than your fists. Makes you feel like going to find a sniper rifle to use those sniper rifle rounds you found on a zombie with and try to shoot your own character's d'ck off or something.
-Carrying limit-
You have to find a backpack somewhere to be able to carry like 60kg of stuff, without one you can carry like ~20kg. Everything is so heavy. Can do very little without a backpack. Even with a backpack it feels rather useless, things get repetitive and boring quickly. Someone needs to reinvent the wheelbarrow in this thing.
-Descriptions-
There's no saying what does exactly what. You got a pistol? It says it's not very useful but alright for noobies. A shotgun - slow but good for close encounters. No tooltip indicating damage, range dependencies, aim lock on timer, nothing. You got an assault rifle? Says it's got medium damage, alright range. Just childish.
You got some abilities like fitness, guns, crafting, farming but no telling wth. You have a fatigue meter - gets filled when you're running or when you melee stuff but you have no idea how and if it gets affected when you increase your fitness. You have health but no idea how much health. A bar starts showing blood loss when you get hit but can't be sure if you're about to die or if it was like a papercut. Etc etc.. No numbers anywhere. Made for simpletons I suppose.
-Saving games-
It doesn't autosave unless a mission gets to a checkpoint, nor is there a timer on those so if you forget to save you can lose a lot of time when a bot does something stupid like forgetting to kick the zombie and gets his face chewed off. If it were up to me, I'd have 10-20 autosaves saving every 5 mins or so, so ppl wouldn't have to worry about getting owned so bad. Saving isn't too hard but you can overwrite a save without meaning it, or load while trying to save... happens specially when you're annoyed with such half-baked interfaces. Or, more usually, if you forget to save when you get immersed in the story or action. F9 is quicksave - only 2 slots allocated for those, so if you accidentally hit it twice overwrites the other. F11 to load the last.. I think. It doesn't say these anywhere, I just found by trying.
-Companions-
Say you're rolling with 2 others in your team. You're inside a camp area with wooden walls. There are zombies outside, you can hear their noises. You get close to the gate, also wooden, you can't see outside though you have guns.. Suddenly the zombies outside become aware of your presence, you automatically get in combat as usual, but in 2 secs you see your companion *bots* open the camp door and rush out to get bitten. And you go like ooook maybe I should come back in 2 years and give this game another shot... Funny though it doesn't say early access...
-Music-
There are some midi-like tracks. They're not all so bad but some just make your head hurt. Music is by default on full volume and plays with shuffle on and there's no way to create a playlist or turn shuffle off. So if you want to listen to one track, you end up going to the esc menu-settings-sound- and then you keep clicking the track playing there until it finally shuffles to what you want after randomly trying to play the same things a few times. You may get to listen to what you want after like 10-15 tries every time. Thank god they didn't forget to implement the music volume feature in options.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
And now some things I liked:~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Characters use things they got on them automatically if they can get the full benefit from those items - like when eating, drinking etc. If they're about to bleed to death, they don't wait for you to find a bandage and use it, they just do it as many times as they need.
Story is not bad.
There are quests, character interactions, economy, communities...
Having a distinction between stuff you can do and stuff you can't before being seen as a villain - like not being able to just break into ppl's homes when you're visiting another community...
You get a companion that has diabetes. As time passes, she needs insulin and as her need gets more apparent, affliction begins affecting her - stamina stops regenerating, her face changes to unhappy, you feel her despair when she basically says she'll ffing die soon unless you can find her some insulin...
There's some deep stuff in there that makes this a good game, it could be great; if only the playing part itself wasn't so sh't...
Will update after I play more, and when I have time.. This should be enough for now.

So Tom Clancy Splinter cell
This is pretty much the original Stealth-Sneaky game as far as i know.Interestingly because of the initial disinterest in it ,the devs were gonna make it as a James Bond game(lol)
The game originally came out in 2003 and gained notriety quite quickly as a result of the games involvement with Tom Clancy.(Tom clancy(rip) is actually a damn good thriller writer,check him out if you can)
So the game is not like todays "stealth" games,Theres no easy QTE missions or a nice gun that you can shoot your way out with the only punishement being a score penalty.
Your gun has just 30 bullets for a entire level,takes 5 seconds for it to be accurate and needs 3 shots to kill a enemy,AND several missions have the requirement that you cannot incur any fatal injuries.
The setting is quite great for its time like a nice Central asian city,a oil rig and even a Cia Facility(Langley).
The graphics are obviously a bit dated but in my opinion hold quite well for its time.The animations are quite well done and there are a variety of moves that make the gameplay interesting and not blocky/restrictive.
The story is actually quite nice,following the path of a typical dictator-gone-wild-revenge-on-usa thing.
The stealth aspect of the game is actually done quite well,darkness,light is well represented with the option of shooting out lights to create darkness for you to hide,There is ZERO handholding,there wont be any markers or compasses to show you where to go,what you have to do and the location of the enemies.You have to solve everything yourself.The AI as well is quite good for its time as many stealth games are put down as a result of extremely wonky AI that acts like a 5 year old with no consciousness.
The controls MAY take a bit time to get used to as jump is with the shift key(inb4 random sticky keys notification) and there is no ADS and you pull your gun out with E.
Anyways now on to what i hated
The Save/Load system is horrible.The game Autosaves ONCE in 45 minutes that is at the start and the end section of a mission and you have to manually save everytime and you have to type the save game name again to overwrite it.
There are no checkpoints(maybe im spoiled from modern games) so yeah sometimes you forget to save and die and then you gotta do 20 mins of work again.
Some places where you have to find a pipe to climb etc are poorly representated.I understand it being a part of the difficulty curve of the game but sometimes it just bugs out or doesnt detect that you are holding a pipe and you fall,or you realise that the actual thing you had to climb was in that doorway just behind you.
Some extremely dumb bugs like you getting magnetically sucked into a hole that you cant escape which is actually just a normal texture (Eg at the start of the Oil Rig level,wont spoil anything)
Barring nostalgia and the fact that im a fan of all things Tom Clancy,This game has actually aged quite well,with the graphics and animations being bearable for the entirety of your experience.The story is quite servicable if you dont know the genre and the Stealth gameplay is crisp,interesting and brutal,just as it should be.

Liking it so far, some normal release bugs, not impressed or disappointed I knew what I was getting myself into.  As a free game though it's definately worth a try if you enjoy anime or mmorpgs.
Graphics: 8 (I run Fullscreen 1920x1080 with everything maxed, solid so far no issues.  I wasn't impressed or disappointed.)
Audio:  8 (Nothing unexpected or new, but nothing terrible and cringeworthy. Japanese with English subtitle translations have that awkward anime feel.  I have a minor in Japanese so I enjoyed the audio more.)
System:  8 (I haven't experienced any unexpected crashes as of yet.  Latency issues only twice so far, very briefly, low pop. channels.)
Quests:  6.5*  (MMO style, cookie cutter archetypes with lower required kills in area map and are generally quick and close.  Main quest chain is good so far. World map daily quests cap at 10 and have varied outcomes and cutscenes with no voice.  The score killer here was a lack of an effective quest reset.  Abandoning and reaquiring a quest did not resolve a main questline issue, very likely my fault for logging out at a bad time. Had to eventually re-install the game. That aside, completing certain quests for the first time gives you permanant stats bonuses.)
Crafting:  9 (Multi-layered and robust you can craft various useful equipable objects and home decor.  Materials are everywhere, and can afk farm at nodes.  Not imputing commands for rarer finds doesn't break node channel.  Various crafting levels in all professions give permanent stats boosts and other various useful bonuses.)
Achievements: 9 (Semi-meaningful and gives useful permanant stat. unlocks.  Titles from achievements also give small stat increases, finding a matching pre/suffix combo is interesting.  Lots of titles to choose from.)
Dungeons: 7.5* (A little short for my taste, several difficulties with dailies involved.  Must complete solo first in main quest chain to unlock party functions.  Everything as far as mechanics in the dungeon seem to be spot on as far as I can tell.  Loot system is rewarding and click-looting is non-existant, everything goes straight to your bags.)
*=subject to change as content is explored

TL;DR: Wanted to like it because it's about selling poop but I couldn't deal with the fact that those cute slimes devour those super cute baby chicken, it's just... so cruel! Wasn't meant to be, I guess.
(Since it hasn't been clear to everyone, please note that this isn't a real tl;dr but an ironic comment.)
The map is painstakingly linear, the running back and forth between pointless connecting "tunnels/canyons" gets tiresome really fast, especially since your vacuum gun/machine has only four slots. Every time you find something interesting a horde of angry rainbow-slimes shows up and eats everything in a matter of seconds. Which is scary at first, but oh, wait, go out of that map section through the connector, wait 10 sec, go back in, respawn.
The vacuuming mechanics for everything annoyed me real quick, sucking up slime poop (so called
) without sucking in all slimes is tedious. But you need the poop to sell and make money to build more tiny-sized ranches. Which you can upgrade to twice the size because there are bouncy slimes. After you do that you'll notice the slimes sitting on top of each other lifting themselves even above the double height. So you install an air net. More money spent.
Then there are these completely unclear hybridization mechanics if a grey wiggly bouncy slime eats a rocky plort it turns into a huge blue rocky slime which is still kinda bouncy and poops one grey and one rocky plort. Somehow slimes LOVE poop, eating it all the time, faster than you can vacuum. Naturally, you can't suck up the big new slimes, they'll just clog up your vac gun until you shoot them off again. Rinse and repeat until all plorts are gone.
Well, that's about it. I couldn't check out all the super expensive ranch expansions simply because I didn't like the base concept enough to grind my way up to it. If you're looking for a kinda repetitive but meditative farming game a la Stardew/Harvest, then you might like it if you're into cuteness factor and don't care about variety or story.
I was just annoyed with the fiddly mechanics and gave up early. Also, I think it's cruel to feed chicken to slimes.

I swept my 18 wheeler into the opposite lane going around 75 in a 45, eyes almost glued shut from lack of sleep after 18 runs of 18 tons of goods.  A young mother, distracted by her 2 kids, managed to look back at the very last moment before I slammed into her Peugeot, another statistic on the long list of accidents I had made on my perilous path towards the top of the European trucking industry.  Only Estonian pop mixed in with the muffled static was the only thing I was able to hear when I bounced off of the retaining wall on that narrow Austrian byroad.
My journey started in Oxfordshire, a county in the middle of the heartlands of England.  Taking little oddjobs across the A and B roads had earned me quite the pence, each a brick on the foundation of my new empire.  I had recruited a few other drivers in the home garage and was planning on expanding operations to Amsterdam and Nice, and you were likely to run into my bright orange Volvo dashing across the countrysides hauling goods for several large companies.
At times it was only the soft fuzz of my radio playing 80s hair rock, German pop, or slavic hard bass from Russia that kept me busy on the long stretches across the continent.  The rolling green hills provided different shades of culture new to me and landmarks only seen in movies.
I looked down and saw a small fine of 350 Euros in my PDA, looking on as the red Peugeot stared blankly into the distance.  My metal giant snaked across to the right side of the road and I eventually had found my way to a rest stop, taking off several hours of my time, only able to make my destination with minutes of time left allowed.  I eagerly picked up my next job from the same company and sped off looking to expand my empire.

Company of Heroes®: Tales of Valor™ is the expansion to the Game of the Year winner and highest rated real time strategy franchise Company of Heroes®. Featuring new campaigns to overcome, units to command, and battlefields to conquer, Company of Heroes®: Tales of Valor™ delivers evolved gameplay mechanics and 3 episodic adventures including 9 new missions, 3 new Multiplayer Modes, and new abilities to master.
- 3 Immersive Storylines — Embark on the definitive WWII experience from all sides of the war. Each episode contains new missions and objectives in a persistent environment.
Episode 1: Tiger Ace: Control Tiger Tank Ace Hauptmann Voss's highly decorated Tigergruppen against the British 7th Armored Division on D-Day in one of the most famous tank battles of WWII. Episode 2: Causeway: Command an American Paratrooper Company in the hours following the initial D-Day landings. Episode 3: Falaise Pocket: Command the Wehrmacht Army as your soldiers try and hold off the advancing Allied army.
- Direct Fire Control — Not only can the player's tactical and strategic decisions influence the battle, but players also directly control units on the battlefield. Players will aim, fire, and maneuver in real-time to capitalize on the changing battle conditions.
- Command New Units — New infantry and vehicles such as the Schwimmwagen and Staghound will be available. The Schwimmwagen is an amphibious, all-wheel drive off-road vehicle while the Staghound is a highly maneuverable 4x4 Armored Car.
- Conquer New Territory — New maps based on famous battles such as Villers-Bocage will be available for competitive players in the online battlefield.
- 3 New Multiplayer Modes — New multiplayer modes to experience with your friends. Become a tank commander and square off in Panzerkrieg, choose a hero unit and join the battle to push back enemy lines in Assault, or team up and defend against waves of attackers in Stonewall.

This game is a very good MOBA. There are players that think they are competing in some tournament for large prizes, and they are not afraid to tell you how great they are. The idea of playing this game is familiar like DOTA2. It is in a sort of FPS view and you travel up lanes in CONQUEST game mode and battle other players or AI depending if you wish to play alone and you can do that, it is up to the player. In ARENA mode you take on other opponents in an arena and have your minions travel from one point to the goal at the opponents side of the arena. It can be played alone as well, up to the player if they so choose. There is JOUST game mode which pits 3vs3 game and you travel up a middle lane with side jungle areas. There is side areas in ARENA with beasts to conquer for powerups, and there is jungle with beasts to conquer for powerups in CONQUEST. There is ASSAULT mode where you have a middle lane and go head to head with the enemy however like in the other modes if you return to base you can get healed and replenish go into inventory and store to purchase equipment to help you. In ASSAULT mode you hop down off the base to enter the battle and therefore cannot hop back up as easily, so you will continue on until one side pushes the other back to the titan that is under the teams protection. This is the same for CONQUEST as well the idea is to knock down the towers, defeat the pheonix, then take on the enemy titan. There is a siege mode and I have not played it very much but I am sure someone will add to it that is probably better at it than I, so, there are many game modes to choose. There is many many gods to choose to play and master to compete in the game. Some are all out warriors, some are hunters, some mages, and some guardians, but beware of the quick and deadly assassins. The community is good, but as mentioned there are some that can be toxic to new players and just do your best and have fun. If another player gets mean or whiny that is their issue.... NOT YOURS. Try playing all the gods and master them all if you can. There is a cash shop if you wish to buy some different skins, or voice packs, that is in the store too. Some players will be difficult to beat as they do play quite well, but if you are having a difficult go, try and switch with a team mate or get help over to you and try ganging up on the enemy. Above all just have fun with this MOBA, it can be quite entertaining if you let it entertain and not an obsession. Have fun folks.

The reviews are pretty mixed. As a huge dishonored fan (i absolutely LOVED the first version), let me walk you through why that is.

pros:
-interesting story line (although i feel Dishonored original had a more gripping/emotional story)
-lots to do (took me 12 hours to do my first playthough, am currently on the second)
-plenty of ways to play; whether you like going high chaos (killing everyone) or truly playing as an assassin, this game makes any combination of play-styles fun and rewarding (although, it is much more challenging taking it slow and avoiding killing anyone)
-artwork in game is beautiful. No, it's not ultra realistic, but it's beautiful in its own way
-lots of interaction with the world (killing someone or sparing someone will change the story)
-plethora of side-quests/extra actives
-supernatural abilities are f***ing cool, no other way to put it.
cons:
-performance is pretty bad. I have a gtx 970 sc and get 60+ FPS in indoor areas, but many of the "larger" areas (such as long streets, or the view from the top of a big building) drops my fps to 45. It's still very playable, but
or the negative reviews are from the FPS. Some people reported artifacting or screen tearing, i have not experienced these issues.
overall, i love this game. I bought the special edition pre-order (with the mask and ring) and do not regret spending a penny of the $100 price tag. If you have not played the original Dishonored, i highly recommend you buy that before purchasing dishonored 2. It's not critical to the in game story, but many of the letters you find or smaller "lore" findings need the original dishonored story to make sense.

This is the game that started and defined the franchise. Given that this game is thirteen years old at the time of this review, It still holds up today, and with some minor modifications you can even run it at high resolutions and wide screen. There are plenty of guides available.
The missions are diverse, stealth truly is an integral part, and you cannot do without. The missions require patience, and you do have to pay attention whether lethal force is granted or not; if you don't you will fail missions. The atmosphere and immersion are fantastic, and I have completed this game a good number of times since its original release. It was one of those defining games back in 2002, something that pushed hardware, and capabilities to the limits.
If all that does not convince you, then let me tell you this: Just the fact that the main protagonist, Sam Fisher, the character you play, is voiced my none other than Michael Ironside, makes this game a mandatory purchase for anyone who even remotely likes military, stealth, action and high-tech based games. My very first Splinter Cell game. No, I didn't play this when I was a kid, I just started the series and plan to play them in order. Talk about being late! Back then I heard this game was aimed to be a Metal Gear Solid 2 killer. Ha! Not even close. Splinter Cell is a great game, just not on par with MGS.
As you may already know, you are Sam Fisher, a secret agent of Third Echelon, a section of the NSA. A coup has occurred in Georgia, and a man named Kombayn Nikoladze has come into power. The CIA sends in two agents to see if this guy is up to no good. Suddenly they lose contact. That's where you come in. The story is decent and so is the voice acting. Music also sets the mood too.
Obviously, stealth is a must in this game. Why? Because #1: you have limited ammo. #2: Sam can get killed easily, even on the easier difficulty and #3: setting off too many alarms will cause the mission to end. This game does not hold your hand, you have to figure how to proceed by yourself. What I like about this game is the use of light and darkness to proceed. There are cases where you can be nose-to-nose with an enemy yet because you're in pitch darkness, he wouldn't notice you. Note, that's an exaggeration, he'll notice if you get too close, so don't actually do it :D
Of course, there are faults. One is the melee attack. There's JUST one: an elbow strike. You can knock out enemies from behind with it, but the real problem is using it face-to-face. When you're sneaking from behind and they turn around and spot you (which will happen very often), it takes two strikes to dispatch them and by the time you do that, they pumped 2-3 bullets (more if it's an assault rifle), bringing down a good chunk of health.
Another thing is the aiming. For some reason, this highly-trained NSA agent cannot aim his pistol right. As in, even if you're crouched and still, you can still miss. Not a big deal since you're not supposed to kill too much anyway, but it's a problem when you trying to shoot lights out. What I do is that I quicksave before I shoot. The SC-20K is MUCH better. Not only is it more accurate, but you can do a lot of stuff with it, like sniping, shooting non-lethal darts and sleeping gas. And the last thing is once you beat the game, that's it. Fortunately, it's worth a second playthrough. Try it on Hard.
This game has done a good job of introducing me to the SC series. It's worth the low price now. I want to play Pandora Tommorrow now but it's not on Steam. Please Ubisoft, fix whatever problems it has and re-release it.

Edit 2: Removed previous introduction (which is now unnecessary) and changed format to match my other reviews. Fixed some spelling/grammar errors.
Review:
I wonder how people can review this game calling it "classic" or "unforgettable". They're not
, but I think its an "unforgettable", "classic" blunder of a game. I'll start with the pros, at least.
Pros:
+ The gadgets at your disposal are nice, although I never used the cameras and rarely use the fiber optic.
+ Animations are fairly top-notch for the time it was made in
+ The thermal-camera being used to see fingerprints was a fantastic idea
+ Interesting "movement intervals" mechanic to adjust speed.
+ The levels aren't always detailed but they are varied enough to not be uninteresting.
Cons:
- Terrible stealth detection. There were more than a few times when being in complete darkness did nothing to hide me from enemies. There were a few unavoidable patrols that kept somehow spotting me in complete shadow.
- The lighting has no rhyme nor reason on your light bar. Sometimes a dim light nearby would barely register, but sitting in shadow would shoot it up by 2 or 3 light bars. Sneaking through some areas is basically trial-and-error.
- Terrible shooting mechanics. I know this game isn't a shooter, but it tries too hard at times to be one. There are some unavoidable "horde mode" attacks throughout the game. The "aim decay" is so ridiculously high that firing accurately at enemies is impossible. I've been sniped by enemies with AK's across long corridors that I can barely hit with one semi-auto shot. There are also times where peeking out to shoot an enemy is impossible since they shoot you dead before you even see their hitbox.
- The climbing system is broken. Getting off of a ladder/pipe/verticle climbable is impossible. If I'm missing something, tell me, because it's infuriating. The walljumping is nice at times but incredibly finnicky. The split jump is hardly useful. The last level is the worst when it comes to this. The beginning area requires absolutely perfect jumps to get up the cliff, and I had to reload more than 20 times to get it done.
- Player speed is either too slow or too fast. If an enemy is patrolling, you're either too slow to catch up to them and knock them out, or too fast and they hear you.
- The alarm system sometimes screwed me over. Even after taking down every single guard and hiding bodies in places it would be impossible to find them, I'd still get "body alerts" every so often. How?!? There's nobody to find the bodies!
- The story is completely forgettable. Oh look, another angry guy who is close-enough-to-the-middle-east-or-russia-to-be-evil-but-not-so-much-that-its-another-cliche-middle-eastern-or-russian-guy. Oh look, characters that have no arc, people dying I don't care about... The main character is only barely passable as one. Each level was just trip after trip to different places hunting down cheap russian/chinese bullet fodder and pressing buttons.
- I had to use walkthroughs far too much. The few times you do get a map, it's just a useless picture of rectangles connected to each other. No minimap. No directional pointer. Yes, I know, this is supposed to be a hardcore game, but I got lost way too many times. The map design is really terrible.
- On the flip side, the game as a whole is ridiculously linear. The only reason one could feasibly do a replay is to do something like a "ghost" playthrough or a "no alerts" playthrough (although good luck with that...). There are no multiple paths. No several points of entry. Nothing. It's literally just glorified corridors and rooms with one door in and one door out that you have to go through.
Basically, if I wanted to play a stealth game, I would play the Thief franchise, or Dishonored. Hell, the new Thief 4 game is better than this. At least Thief 4 didn't make me want to break my keyboard. Thief: Gold and Thief 2 are older than this game yet hold up far better in pretty much every sense (minus graphics, although Thief graphics patches can actually give this game a run for its money, funnily enough). Dishonored might be too action-oriented for your tastes, but its far better and far easier to play a nice, challenging "ghost" playthrough rather than a ghost playthrough involving antidepressants and a bottle of hard liquor to soothe the pain Losing a ghost run in the previously mentioned games were because you messed up. In this game, its sometimes the opposite.
So no, I can't recommend this game. It's broken in too many ways, and can't hold up through the ages.
And no, the "dont hate because age" argument doesn't work. Thief: Deadly Shadows came out essentially around the same time, and it is less broken, less linear, and less rage-inducing. The controls are clunky, sure, but at least they don't cause me to die in stupid ways. If you wanted to play a stealthy modern game though, there's always Rainbow 6. The old ones are more hardcore than eating a brick, but at least if you fail them, it's your own fault rather than the game's. The newer Vegas games are a little too action-y and not enough stealth but could be up your alley.
tl;dr Please don't. Some old games just don't hold up through the ages. If you do still like it okay. It's your cup of tea and you can handle it. I on the other hand, couldn't. And I don't think some others might either. There's other 10 dollar stealth games out there. Better ones.

Most games have stealth as an option but I never see it as the only way to progress.  Options are nice but I love it when the game punishes you for being spotted.  Forget about shooting your way through.  Guns are literally only used to take out lights.  Anything else is a travesty.  Hardcore stealth like this is very few and fare between.  Which is why Splinter Cell is one of my favorite game series.  So much nostalgia sneaking past guards in very dark places.  Using your wits and the shadows to sneak by.  Hell some missions flat out failed you if your spotted and why the ♥♥♥♥ not when the entire premise is that you weren't supposed to be there.  Taking out a single guard requires timing and strategy as just taking him out isn't enough.  Finding a good place to hide his body is critical. Singleplayer: Good.
Multiplayer: "Okay" (12/12/2014), but your mileage may vary.
Worth the cost?  Maybe (read on).
Campaign:
I found the campaign to be great fun.  I played the whole thing with friends watching via Steam's beta broadcasting feature.  The storyline was your typical Call of Duty fare—that is to say, it's the kind of action movie plot you'd feel comfortable seeing as a half-price matinee at the theatre.  In other words, don't take the inclusion of Kevin Spacey as an actor in the game to mean that the storyline is anything but what you've come to expect from Call of Duty.  Knowing that this was likely the case before I jumped in, I enjoyed the campaign as it was.
The gameplay of the campaign was simply great fun.  There's a lot of stuff to nitpick—like the fact that some of the quicktime events feel a bit "off" in their timing; and that some key functions of the game need to be remapped (or even mapped!)—but that's really all they are: nitpicks.  Overall, the campaign was a fun jaunt and the combat felt tactical with plenty of opportunities to use your equipment and myriad new abilities.
Multiplayer:
I haven't played much of multiplayer, but already my feelings about it are mixed.  What I have played has been "okay."  Just as in the campaign, the exosuit makes the gameplay incredibly fun.  Unfortunately, matchmaking seems slow for any mode except Team Deathmatch, which means that's probably what you'll end up playing if you just want to play, and team balance is a serious issue.  I've been placed on an outnumbered team more than once, and just in my previous play session I was on a team of 2 versus a team of 5.  (Side note: We lost, but only barely.  Score was really close!)
The maps feel cramped.  I haven't played a map yet that seemed like a good fit for a sniper rifle.  I've read other reviews here that say the game is mostly played with Assault Rifles and SMGs, and, currently, I can't disagree.  Fortunately for me, the run-and-gun nature of this is acceptable—that's my preferred playstyle.  However, I am experienced with many other playstyles thanks to Planetside 2 and other games, and I'm somewhat concerned with how viable switching up classes and roles will be as I gain ranks.
It's easy to see why afficionados of past Call of Duty games could feel so slighted by this installment.  Though, I feel at this point I should reiterate that I *am* still having a lot of fun in the multiplayer, despite these rather significant flaws.  The gameplay is tight and very responsive (when lag isn't an issue, and thus far, for me, lag hasn't been a big problem).  And though the maps I've played feel cramped, they do quite well in facilitating fast-paced gameplay.
I'd love to see dedicated servers for this game.  I still want to play some more with matchmaking as it currently stands, but I really feel like dedicated servers would extend the longevity of the multiplayer experience.  I do think monitored, dedicated servers would reduce the complaints about lag and hackers.
I don't think I've run into any hackers yet, by the way.  Maybe that will change as I play more, but thus far, it hasn't been an issue.
Overall:
Overall, I feel I can recommend this game based on the enjoyable campaign and the solid gameplay both in singleplayer and in multiplayer.  However, for all the reasons mentioned above, I'd suggest any potential buyer (if you're reading this, that's probably you) weigh the game's drawbacks on his or her own personal scale to determine whether the game is worth the investment.  For me, the game's flaws aren't game-breaking and I very much enjoy playing, and get excited at the prospect of playing.  For this simple reason—that I find the game fun—I'll give the game a thumbs up.
If you like bad games this game is not for you, because it's good.

Edit: Ok, actual review (may contain spoilers, read it at your own risk):
You are Amanda Ripley, an engineer (obviously, otherwise there would be no crafting!), aboard the ship Torrens in its way to Sevastopol station where they are in possession of the Nostromos' flight recorder.
Let's start with the good. The game starts out oozing atmosphere from the Alien universe. From the art design, to the soundtrack, to every detail. The game screams '1979 Alien'.
Like every good horror movie (or game) things get bad very quickly and, after that, the game begins to really shine.
As you explore the (for the most part) dark station, you can't shake the feeling of dread. Every noise makes you nervous, every shadow makes you tense. It's terror at its finnest.
That level of quality is mantained until the Alien decides to show up. Then, instead of raising the bar even more, for me, the game starts spiriling down. After playing hide and seek for the nth time, you become comfortable with the Alien. Fear and terror trade places with tedium and frustration. Your only real fear is of not being able to get to the next save station and have to repeat ten to twenty minutes of the game again.
Speaking of that, let's talk difficulty. The game recommends to you playing on hard (so that's what I did). I didn't notice it being hard, really. Frustrating, yes, hard, no. Once you come in contact with the Alien for the first time, then it's a hide and seek game until the end. The frustration comes from repetition. And I don't mean repeating the same section over and over because you died (I didn't die that often), but from the fact that, sometimes, the Alien doesn't go away. So you are either forced to wait until it does (minutes for me) or risk being in the open and killed. I chose a more conservative approach and only moved when he wasn't around. That didn't help much. Sometimes I had to retreat several times to the same hiding spot because that thing kept "spawning" ahead of me and cutting me off from where I needed to go.
Which brings me to the AI of the game. Is it good? Well, not quite. If I knew before hand that it wasn't that good, I wouldn't be so conservative in the first place. The AI doesn't notice the opening and closing of doors (even if that happens inside its line of sight. If it doesn't see YOU, it doesn't bother that things close and open), it doesn't hear your ridiculously loud animation of going in and out of lockers to hide and it doesn't have a very good sight either, even on hard. What it does perfectly is its randomness. You can't predict what it's going to do next. That is amazing and it got me a few times by being unpredictable.
I also mentioned crafting. You can craft a number of devices to help you cope with various threats on your journey to surviving the nightmare. The fact that you can craft anywhere (no need for tools or a workbench) is funny to me, but I digress. Those devices are little more than gimmicks. You have: Noisemakers, pipe bombs, emp bombs, molotovs, smoke grenades, flashbangs and medkits. All, except the medkits, are so situational that you may play the entire game without using one. For example, the noisemaker. Sounds good on paper but if you throw them too far, the Alien does not hear it (odd since if you run, he hears you from ridiculous distances). If you throw it too close, it's next to useless. The EMP grenade is good for when you have a bunch of androids together. That only happens once in the game. It doesn't help that you come accross EMP resistant enemies later in the game either. For 'lone androids' you have a much better tool: the Stun Baton (or even better: avoid them entirely. You can outrun them and outsmart them pretty easily).
Bottom line:
It seems I'm bashing the game quite a lot but I certainly enjoyed it. It felt a bit too long as it overstays its welcome after a certain point when you start to notice the game getting repetitive, but I would still recommend it for Alien and horror fans.

I got this game back in 2016 when the game first game out. Me and my friend both got it for Christmas and we finished up the entire tree in just a few days. We loved the game but started to find it boring. A few months later, the creators of astroneer made the game a lot better, more interesting, harder, and just a lot better in general. Now, after only 2 years of being in early access, the game has progressed tremendously. There is now research points, better exploring, less and less bugs, starts on modularity, and much more! I would HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone who likes to just casualy play and explorer by them selves or with a friend!

Even for an Alpha, this game is very enjoyable and interesting to play, and even more interesting if, like me, you weren't told how to do anything beforehand (figuring things out feels like an aspect of the game itself). I love the sound cues (for research, oxygen and sandstorms for example), the different dangers and ways to deal with them, and how you get your research currency. I also love how you can slide down hills like you're using a snowboard, though at one point that nearly killed me, hehe. Sandstorms, though dangerous and annoying, are an interesting and nice detail which to me makes the game the tiniest bit more special.
The only thing that has annoyed me so far is how tricky it is with making slopes, like to go to a lower part of a cave or from the banks of a river to the bed.
Seeing as I've played 2 and a half hours so far and have barely moved from the area around my pod, I think I'm going to play this game for a while.

I love how early the game stage is in, and how well it is in, yet there are some bugs that usually end out as a 10 minute laughing session.
Astroneer is a low-poly sandbox survival game where you are in a different solar system (what in the actual fook are you there for?) and pretty much making a life there, you can explore caves, shipiwrecks, and even fly to different planets, and even solar systems!
There is also a multiplayer feature in the game, but it is only really meant for friends, there isn't in game chat, but assuming you're friends, you can use steam chat, or discord to talk. Multiplayer is also a little bit unbalanced in a way that the server host cannot kick, nor invite friends, it is up to the friend to join the game via steam chat. I don't quite like this feature because if you have lots of friends, and one happens to be a troll, well, you're boned.
But before you buy this game, make sure your system can handle it, even though the min. specs were quite low, I found myself running through a few lagspikes during the game playing on my laptop while traveling.

I will start by saying I never played these games on the original Xbox as I never owned one, but I love stealth games and will often take the stealthy approach in non-stealth games like Skyrim. With that being said, I HATE this game on PC. It's not the hardcore stealth aspects (I love that and did just fine), but the controls are EXTREMELY unintuitive and clunky. I changed them around a bit, but I can't do anything about some things. For example, you basically have to get close enough to smell a guard's♥♥♥♥♥just to get the option to grab him. By the time the notice pops up, the guard turns around and you're caught. Jumping is a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ too.
I ran into a few glitches as well that required me to restart the entire mission like the oil refinery level. A door that was previously locked until near the end when the guy you're after goes through and leaves it open for you was still shut when I got there. I got to maybe halfway through the CIA level on my way to get my gun and I could not get past a maintenance worker in an inventory room. I was in complete darkness and he'd see me everytime from several feet away, but there was no other way through. I said Eff it and deleted the game.
That being said, I like a lot of things they did with the game. The stealth aspects are quite detail-oriented for its age. Guards react to the sound of your footsteps based on how fast you move, they will turn the lights back on in a room if you turned them off, and they do a decent job investigating any disturbances.
I played Blacklist before this one and I loved it. The controls were far more intuitive (except for when you're trying to get away from a grenade) and you can play it however you want. But I don't have time to play a 12 year old game with controls this bad.

The controls for this game are incredibly clunky, which makes what would be simply tasks quite frustrating when Sam Fisher refuses to climb a pipe or move along because you aren't facing in exactly the right direction.
Dying or failing a mission becomes irritating with the unnecessarily long 'Mission Failed' screen which, along with the instructions in your headset, are the only parts of the game you can't skip, and have to watch/listen to all over again. Dying and then redoing one part of the game very quickly because you now know what to do results in then having to wait for half a minute while the instructions cycle through one after the other until they finally reach the part that you've arrived at.
I suppose this was a good game in 2004, but as it is, it's just too annoying for me to enjoy.

Let me put this out there, I have played a LOT of MMOs, some were good and some were really bad. ESO started off bad back when I played it in beta and has slowly grown into something that I have found VERY enjoyable and addictively fun.
But to enjoy this game you have to enter with the mindset of it being an MMO game set in the universe of the elder scrolls and NOT an elder scrolls game with a multiplayer feature or you WILL be disappointed (hence a lot of the bad reviews).
The Good:
Unlike most MMO's the combat here is really fun, swing your word block with your shield and then switch to ur bow or staff and get those far away targets, aggro them and pull them in then turn into a tank. it is FUN. also it feels more like a regular game than an MMO.
The graphics are really nice, not skyrim nice but really good none the less.
Huge open world that we all know and love, getting to visit the Ashlands again brought back so many memories of endless nights on my xbox playing morrowind so many years ago.
Nice voice acting (not perfect but nice, especially that all NPC have their lines read by voice actors)
I love the new justice system, being a lawman or thief are both a lot of fun.
So far it seems to be a good story, not as good as previous titles but it stands up well :)
The Bad:
No auction house.... I mean seriously? no Auction house?... NO AUCTION HOUSE??? sure there is guild stores but they suck big time. auction houses have been THE best way to make an income for me and to find cool items and needed resources in almost all MMOs I played, to be honest I feel a bit aimless without it.
The cheapest horse is 10,000 gold, next in line is 40,000... I am level 10 now and I barely have 3000, and this is from a person who searches every thing he comes across, does all the side quest and never bought a single peice of equipment (stole or found them all) and I sell everything I can to merchants (again exactly why we need an auction house!!)
Other than the side quests and quests, and the usual exploring and crafting, I find it limited in what to do... I mean I want to sail my own  boat, fly in the air, farm a land... give me a sense of being a part of that world, don't limit me.
No player housing, now sure not all MMOs have this, but this is an elder scrolls game for the love of everything good. having your own house that you stuff with your trophies and junk has been a traditions for ages with elder scrolls games lol.
Final words:
All in all this has been a really nice game so far, I have truly enjoyed ESO more so than many MMO's I have tried save for maybe 1 or 2 other games. I would strongly recommend it to any fan of the MMO genre and the ES series.

Where to start..?
First off, during my time playing Dishonored 2 I didn't experience any frame drops, crashes or game breaking bugs that ruined my time with the game. However, even with my somewhat beefy computer, the games settings were auto set to medium and I ran 35-50 frames throughout the entire playthrough.
Next, the game itself. I am a massive fan of Dishonored 1 and all 3 of the DLC's that came out for the first game. I was hyped from the first day Dishonored 2 was announced. Dishonored 2 was worth the wait as it is a real masterpiece to play. My first playthrough of the game I played as Emily and did a stealth/ no kill run. The stealth in this game at times is really challenging and enemies AI has been improved to make it somewhat harder for you to sneak up and choke out. Enemies are more aware and react more when they notice someone went missing or when they see a body. Unlike in the original game, this time I feel like you need to play a little more careful when sneaking around.
The level designs in the game are some of the best yet in the series. Each mission you are in you can see the detail and beauty of each level. From starting out in Dunwall, to first arriving in Karnaca and exploring the capital of Serkonos, each area is packed full of style. Some of my favourite missions to play include The Clockwork Mansion and The Dust District. Both of these missions show the beauty and intricacy that Dishonored 2 offers.
The choices you make in the game do affect how the story unfolds later in the game. I won't go into detail on this section of the review, as I have on played the game once as Emily. I will reserve a more detailed section once I play as Corvo and play the game completely different. However, the choices you make in this game changes up how the story plays out. Compared to the first game, Dishonored 2 expands greatly on choices the player can make.
The powers in the game are awesome as always. I played as Emily for my first playthrough and after fooling around with her powers that she gets from the Outsider, I can say that her powers are more fun to play with than Corvo's powers from the first game. Dishonored 2 also focuses more on customizing your powers in the sense that you can change up how you power acts and what it does. I focuses mainly on using Far Reach, Dark Vision and Domino.
Lastly, I will talk about any bugs or glitches in the game. As I said previously, I hadn't come across any game breaking bugs. However, I have come across a few things that left my scratching my head. First glitch I came across, was when I'd use Far Reach. Rarely, I would get stuck in the air and wouldn't be able to get down. Reloading fixes that glitch. Next glitch I came across would be that if you quick save on top of a Watchtower, quick loading would kill me instantly until I would go back to another save. The last glitch I came across was during The Clockwork Mansion mission. I found myself not being able to quick save or save save for a good part of that mission when I was in Jin Dosh's mansion. Reloading wouldn't fix the issue. After a little bit, that game fixed itself and I could save again.
My final thoughts on Dishonored 2 are that I believe this to be the game of the year as it was a fresh, fun and challenging game. The style and sound of Dishonored 2 is wonderful and tasteful and the gameplay in engaging and fun. Despite the glitches and framerate problems people are having, which can easily be patched, I still give this game an easy 10/10.

No More Room in Hell in my opinion, is one of the best mods ever made. It's truly free to play, there is no such thing as pay to win in this game.
When it first came out (even still), there was (and is) nothing like it. The idea of being able to get infected with no possible way to escape it but inevitable death is one of the most horrific things in gaming.
There is nothing more heartdropping then when you are 2 minutes away from beating a level and suddenly you get bit, with only you and your comprade left at your side. The best route is to wait for your near death then have your friend execute you, because when you come back as a zombie, you come back in full force. The idea of that is just so awesome, and with the games random seeds, you never really know what path to expect.
The best map for objective is broadway, in fact, it's probably my favorite map in multiplayer zombie games, the level is very well crafted while still remaining realistic, same with the rest of the maps, the environment is just perfect, and everything is really well balanced.
Don't forget the difficulty of this game though, I really love how it doesn't let up at all, it's not easy for sure, the melee system is more functional than contagion even, so you can't really complain about it. The players walk at just the right speed and the fact that you can only carry so much works very well with the gameplay, some games having a stock limit doesn't work at all, but in this game, you will have to choose carefully what to take into battle and how to manage your supplies.
The only other game to suck you this dry of ammo is probably Resident Evil 4, so I don't know if that says anything, but the fact you are limited on ammo adds a ton more suspense to the game, it's very thrilling knowing at any time you can run out of ammo, and if you are being chased by a horde, most likely, you are ****ed.
