Ive just recently finished my 3rd playthrough, and overall the game felt a lot more streamlined than dark souls 1. This is a good thing despite what a lot of people complain about, which i will go into further later. Lets start with the upgrade system, instead of upgrading your weapon to max, then finding a specific blacksmith which "ascends" the weapon, then upgrading again, then finding another specific blacksmith to "ascend" it again, and then finally upgrading it to max... it has been simplified to just upgrading it and then infusion it, and if you dont like the infusion you can just swap it out(as opposed to downgrading your weapon and then going through a different upgrade path). Boss soul weapons are now just purchased with boss souls instead of upgrading a particular weapon to max and then combining it with the boss soul. Next the bosses, which were a bit less memorable than in dark souls 1, but still were challenging. Every boss has a part to tell in the story, which is a step up from dark souls 1. The story is layed out more straight forward in dark souls 2 as npc's actually tell you about the world, its history, and about other npcs instead of just babbling on about thier own problems and then cackle crazily until they inevitably try to kill you. This leads to summoning, both allies and pvp, the system has changed a little. In dark souls 1 your level was what was factored into how summoning worked(generally 10+-10% of your level). In dark souls 2 your accumulated souls are what are taken into account instead of the levels(but now the formula is +-25%). This is great news for people soloing the game as pvpers will not invade as often(it still happens luckily), however this is bad news for playing with friends and pvpers. To play with friends you now need to be within 25% of your friends characters soul memory(accumulated souls) which generally means you are your friend have to stay at pretty much the same spot. Pvping at low levels is nearly impossible to maintain as your soul memory goes up everytime you kill someone(if you kill someone super high level you might increase your soul memory to where you need to progress the game to start finding people to invade again). The good news to this is that there is a ring you can get even before the first boss that makes it easier to find friend in range(tried it and it works like a charm, it a ring though). The other good news is that soul memory only works in your first playthrough, which is to say on NG+ you can be summoned, summon, or invade anyone(which makes that ring for finding your friends even better). The zones are a bit more linier now, which is both good and bad, but what this also says is that you wont just wander into an area and not be able to kill things(it can still be really challening, but the enemies shouldnt just kill you outright). Lastly Dark Souls 2 doesnt suffer from any of the porting issues that Dark Souls 1 had, which is to say that the graphics are customizable without a 3rd party addon, the fps is solid and i didnt notice any frame rate issues on any of my playthroughs, and lastly you dont need a mod to connect consistantly with friends. Overall the game was enjoyable with lots of replay value, they made NG+ different than your first playthrough by adding in additonal lore elements and enemies, which just adds the to replay value.
In short while they did fix most of the annoying issues with Dark Souls 1, the gameplay is still the same at its core, which is a good thing for most people. I would highly recommend this game for anyone like liked the previous game, that said this kind of game is not for everyone, if you didnt enjoy the first game then you wont enjoy this one.

Dishonored 2 is a masterpiece of modern game design, and a true sequel.
The first game showed us how artistic vision can overcome the idea of graphic resolution by presenting us with beautiful environments and an immersive dark atmosphere. The characters were memorable, and the story always seemed much larger than the game let on, as notes and other dialogue often hinted at places far away from Dunwall.
The sequel, which takes us to Karnaca - another small part of the world Arkane has built, while going for a more colorful atmosphere manages to maintain the Dishonored feel, and builds on the already amazingly simple yet deep and unpredictable gameplay. The game, while short adapts to the player’s preferred playstyle, allowing them to feel the consequences of their actions. The experience largely depends on the player placing certain limitations on themselves like not killing anyone, or doing things a certain way, for the sake of challenge or morality, which in turn allows for replayability further amplified by the choice between two different characters with different points of view on the story. Even though all actions eventually boil down to a binary chaos system, Dishonored manages to make a spectrum of small choices to feel significant and memorable.
This is the Dishonored we know, but better, with larger maps to explore and discover small bits of story, new powers to play around with, and more of this great world to immerse ourselves in.

This game has the gates of Oblivion with the Sigil Stones ans Scamps that follows with it, Ayleid Ruins with traps and Welkynd Stones and the Shivering Isles with Haskill and Sheogorath. I couldn't stop laughing when I fist saw Haskill, all I could think about was the Summon Haskill spell you get from the Shivering Isles quest line in The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion.
This game also contains the Dwemer Ruins with the Dwarven Spiders and the Dwarven Spheres, the old dragon burial mounds and the Nordic Ruins with Draugrs and puzzles. Almost everything you can do in The Elders Scrolls V: Skyrim, you can do in this game. And you can do a whole lot that you can't do in Skyrim.
This game has content from all of the Elder Scrolls games, but I have only played Oblivion and Skyrim so that's all I know :P
If you are looking for Skyrim online, you're not going to find it here. But if you are looking for a unique MMO, with content from all the Elder Scrolls games and endless possibilities in character builds and playing styles, this is the game for you!

The game is a simple city builder based on short timed campaign mode with primary and secondary objectives, earning stars and trophies based on how well you did. The game also has a sandbox mode where you can set your own win conditions, or none at all and just play for fun. In the sandbox it will take you under an hour to max out and try everything the game has to offer in terms of building mechanics, but for the cheap price of €4, it’s a rather enjoyable experience.
The only flaw I could find is not being able to continue a campaign scenario once you meet the main objectives to also complete the side objectives without having to replay the whole scenario again being careful not to satisfy the main objectives before the side objectives are done first.
Overall it’s a fun little city builder. If you are after a very casual, easy to learn city builder game that you can pick up any time just for a few minutes this is definitely a good one to try.

Things to keep in mind about this game
1. It's a $10 game so have the right expectations to start with

5. Take advantage of NPC's from your base to do supply runs but always make sure they have an escort.
6. There are difficulty settings: A. Keep the diabetic alive or B. Let her die.  A is extremely hard and B is a cakewalk.
7. Explore the map and choose a base carefully because resources are VERY limited and the wrong spot is very aggravating to defend, where as, a good spot is very easy to defend. Some very good spots only have one entrance to defend.
8. Concrete towers on top of cliffs to defend your main gate with snipers inside makes all the pain go away =)
9. It's worth the effort to recruit anyone and everyone except the Cult people who are nuts.
10. If 7 Days to Die had this NPC system my soul would become lost because the perfect game would be a blend of that game with this one on single player mode.

Ive just recently finished my 3rd playthrough, and overall the game felt a lot more streamlined than dark souls 1. This is a good thing despite what a lot of people complain about, which i will go into further later. Lets start with the upgrade system, instead of upgrading your weapon to max, then finding a specific blacksmith which "ascends" the weapon, then upgrading again, then finding another specific blacksmith to "ascend" it again, and then finally upgrading it to max... it has been simplified to just upgrading it and then infusion it, and if you dont like the infusion you can just swap it out(as opposed to downgrading your weapon and then going through a different upgrade path). Boss soul weapons are now just purchased with boss souls instead of upgrading a particular weapon to max and then combining it with the boss soul. Next the bosses, which were a bit less memorable than in dark souls 1, but still were challenging. Every boss has a part to tell in the story, which is a step up from dark souls 1. The story is layed out more straight forward in dark souls 2 as npc's actually tell you about the world, its history, and about other npcs instead of just babbling on about thier own problems and then cackle crazily until they inevitably try to kill you. This leads to summoning, both allies and pvp, the system has changed a little. In dark souls 1 your level was what was factored into how summoning worked(generally 10+-10% of your level). In dark souls 2 your accumulated souls are what are taken into account instead of the levels(but now the formula is +-25%). This is great news for people soloing the game as pvpers will not invade as often(it still happens luckily), however this is bad news for playing with friends and pvpers. To play with friends you now need to be within 25% of your friends characters soul memory(accumulated souls) which generally means you are your friend have to stay at pretty much the same spot. Pvping at low levels is nearly impossible to maintain as your soul memory goes up everytime you kill someone(if you kill someone super high level you might increase your soul memory to where you need to progress the game to start finding people to invade again). The good news to this is that there is a ring you can get even before the first boss that makes it easier to find friend in range(tried it and it works like a charm, it a ring though). The other good news is that soul memory only works in your first playthrough, which is to say on NG+ you can be summoned, summon, or invade anyone(which makes that ring for finding your friends even better). The zones are a bit more linier now, which is both good and bad, but what this also says is that you wont just wander into an area and not be able to kill things(it can still be really challening, but the enemies shouldnt just kill you outright). Lastly Dark Souls 2 doesnt suffer from any of the porting issues that Dark Souls 1 had, which is to say that the graphics are customizable without a 3rd party addon, the fps is solid and i didnt notice any frame rate issues on any of my playthroughs, and lastly you dont need a mod to connect consistantly with friends. Overall the game was enjoyable with lots of replay value, they made NG+ different than your first playthrough by adding in additonal lore elements and enemies, which just adds the to replay value.
In short while they did fix most of the annoying issues with Dark Souls 1, the gameplay is still the same at its core, which is a good thing for most people. I would highly recommend this game for anyone like liked the previous game, that said this kind of game is not for everyone, if you didnt enjoy the first game then you wont enjoy this one.

**UPDATED REVIEW 14 DECEMBER 2014**
Okay, so after finally figuring out how to fix the low texture resolution problem and finally being able to connect to multiplayer... I figured I'd update my review.
First, after getting the graphical issues figured out, I decided to give the campaign a run through. Not bad actually. I have to admit, the campiagn is pretty interested. Of course it's your typical Call of Duty storyline, but I think they actually managed to pull a gem out of their asses (Activision, I mean).
The gameplay is fairly smooth. The sound could use some improvements... They're really not focusing on improving their work in the sound department. Just recycled sounds from previous CoD games. Graphics, once everything was sorted, are actually really good. The facial expressions are very captivating. It almost appears they've super imposed actual actors' faces onto the characters' bodies. I'm impressed. We're talking some Heavy Rain quality sh*t here people, lol.
Anyways, after drudging through the campaign, I found myself actually having fun (for once in a post CoD:MW). Now onto the multiplayer.
Let's get the bad stuff outta the way now. As I'm sure you're well aware, there are no dedicated servers... Which means cheaters everywhere. My God are cheaters everywhere. Every single game I joined had about one to two cheaters every round. Also, barely anyone online. Took me 20 minutes to get into a game... Mosh pit, mind you. A culmination of different modes. 20 minutes. That was pretty much it for the negatives, though.
As for the positives. I'm really enjoying the character customization. Call me old fashioned, but I love creating my character and really making them my own. You can do that here. One thing that bugs me though is the timed (rented) equipment. Never been a huge fan, but this doesn't really bother me too much. Once I got into a game, it was actually pretty fun. The use of the exo with the fast paced, claustrophobic, in your face tea bagging, all made a pretty good experience. I managed to level myself from 1 to 13 in about an hour. So, every round you're bound to get something, whether that be a promotion or a badge. It definitely keeps you coming back. Well done Sledgehammer.
So, after giving the game a go after fixing the issues mentioned in the previous (below) review. I can recommend this game... At a massive discount (Maybe get it during the Holiday sale.. If it goes up on sale). I'm still pretty butt-hurt about Activision's lack of communication and much needed TLC for us PC Gamers. We were, after all, Call of Duty's original demographic of choice.
For anyone having issues with low textures and not being able to connect with the Advanced Warfare Servers, shoot me a message and I can walk through the process I took to resolve the issues.

Although an ardent fan I can only give the original Splinter Cell a 9/10, simply because Chaos Theory was by and far the best entry in the original stealth trilogy. While a game this old may not entice new fans it will certainly delight old fans and stealth/action games enthusiasts in general. During the sales it can be snapped up for less than 2.00 but still, for a game this playable and gripping 4.99 is a steal.

Broforce has got more testosterone in each pixel than Arnold Schwarzenegger has in his whole body.
Broforce is an excellent couch coop game. ridiculously chaotic. My only problems with it is the campaign is short, and there is a lack of challenge to alot of the gameplay.

Broforce is a game where you have to learn to improvise. Sure, you start out with the one Bro who has guns, but soon, you're unlocking melee-only bros, bros that only have flamethrowers and bombs, bros with certain perks that dramatically affect the way you play the game. You don't get to choose your Bro, the Bro chooses you, and like any good action hero, you gotta
liberate them all with the cards you've been dealt. That's Bro life.
I would like Broforce more if the difficulty curve didn't spike like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, however. Most levels are pretty much you getting the hang of Bros and creating cool explosions that fill the screen and liberate everyone in view! However this kind of thing doesn't really mesh all that well with the bosses, which are more of your Contra-sidescroller fare. One moment, you're improvising with explosives and bullets on very squishy goons, the next you've gotta figure out how the hell you're going to
liberate this giant tank with eight sections or
force-feed hot dogs to a Bro in a mech suit off the cliff. It's two different kinds of gameplay styles that don't mesh all that well together.
But god dammit, when it works, it works. It's one of the smartest dumb action games I've played in a while, and I can't wait to see what the final version is going to look like.

TL;DR
------------------------
CONS:
-Mouse acceleration/smoothing ~ easily FIXED by enabling V-Sync,
-Bounce off the surface when using Far Reach while falling ~ (Emily),
-Performance drop when alt-tabbing/minimizing the game.
PROS:
-EVERYTHING ELSE!!!
------------------------
I bought Dishonored 2 ignoring all these negative reviews because most were about bad optimization and whatnot.
To set the record straight -- the game IS NOT poorly optimized, you're just too big of a mongloid to adjust the settings properly or simply think you can run the game maxed out with a 2010 computer/components.
The only problem is the mouse smoothing/acceleration, which is EASILY FIXED by enabling V-Sync. Yes, you will limit your FPS but who cares? Those 60 locked frames are just perfect for this game because it's not a game about admiring the graphics or the scenery, but sneaking around and carefully getting past (or getting rid of) the enemies and of course it's gameplay aka combat system.
That being said, it's the only CON in my eyes (and also a HUGE drop in performance when alt-tabbing/minimizing out of the game + maybe falling and then using Far Reach which weridly bounces you randomly and you don't always end up where you wanted to).
Putting that aside, I run the game on preset (Very High mostly everything (shadows and water quality being on High and lens flare + all that disabled) and I get 100 FPS minimum if I disable V-Sync. I have a GTX 1070 G1, 16GB RAM, i7 3770 and W7.
The story is fine, the visuals and gameplay are smooth and fun and it's a big upgrade from the 1st. Considering you can choose from 2 characters and with that the play style, it's damn awesome. A lot of replay value and the amount of different approaches you can take to complete your mission just makes you coming back for more. Of course the achievements are also something you shouldn't ignore and just add up to all the fun you can have from the game.
I definitely recommend the game, however, keep in mind it's a demanding so I wouldn't really recommend buying it if you don't have the newest graphics card or a somewhat powerful PC (even with the older GPU). That aside, I personally don't think the game is worth it's original price and I never would have paid it. In my opinion, it's worth around 40€ but not 60€.

I really really wanted to like this game, and have tried a few times to get into it over several hours. It has everything I want in a game; base building survivalism & zombies.
What it doesn't have that I need is a user interface that isn't like arm wrestling several octopii, and a view that doesn't feel like you're stuck in extreme close up.
I understand it's a one dev game, so I don't regret buying it at all.
The camera view and control system is barebones functional but annoying as. You simply cant see anything coming before it attacks you, fundamentally at odds with the survivallist nature of the game, the idea that you can't carefully sneak around and choose when to engage.  A screaming slobbering zombie apparently can't be noticed before they see you.
The zombies appear already charging/attacking at the edge of your FOV, you cannot avoid them say when you have run out of ammo, or are simply wanting to progress rather than fight every posssible battle.
This gets mind numbingly boring, and combined with the extremely limited camera view completely washed out the other aspects of the game that would otherwise be awesome. For me anyway.
If you don't mind overlooking really clunky interfaces, there is a lot of cool stuff in this game, I just got sick of the view and interface.
For the dev; love the idea and most of the gameplay mechanics hidden behind the GUI; have never been more annoyed with a camera view and menu/control system. I say that having never designed and built one ;), but having played a few at both ends of the budget spectrum.
Interested to see your next game, this is a close miss for me. I want to play this game more, just not with the current GUI/menu systems and camera control.
Prospective buyers - Play the demo first!  plenty of content for the price if you can get past the view and GUI.
Not recomended as I think its a very niche market that will forgive its weaknesses.

This game really tries to be a Build-a-Lot type casual builder/resource manager, but the dreadful scaling and balance ruins most of its mechanics.
Whenever a new successful formula emerges in the world of casual games, there will be myriads of copycats trying to cash in on it. Townopolis is such a clone, this time trying to imitate Build-a-Lot, a popular time manager/city builder from 2007.
The goal of each of the 24 levels is mostly the same, despite the seemingly different objectives: build houses (ranging from small homes to apartment complexes), collect the rent from them, and use that money to unlock better houses, upgrades, and support buildings. Each of these increases the rent money in some way, so the more you invest, the faster the money flows.
This is the theory. In reality, the balance is ungodly atrocious. The smaller buildings generate income so slow that some levels are designed with 5-10 minutes of pointless waiting in mind. On the other end of the spectrum, the large apartments make more money you can spend, rendering cash a meaningless resource; at this point, the slow speed of how ordered building materials arrive becomes the biggest limiting factor.
Sadly, the middle ground between these two is slim, so there is just too little fun in playing Townopolis to recommend it to anyone but the most desperate Build-a-Lot fans.
Just ... don't even ...

Oh, Dark Souls 2 where do I begin. Having spend more than 1000 hours from earlier titles by FromSoftware such as the Tenchu series, Demon souls, Dark souls and now Dark souls 2. I am happy to annouce that Dark souls 2 definitely lives up to the hype shown in last year's E3 as well as all the trailers lurking around the internet and our anticipation buidling up for the april pc release.
One of the biggest difference between the console version and the Pc version is that this time around, FromSoft constructed the PC version from ground up instead of porting it over which means that the graphics can be adjusted depending on the computer spec and that the experience is further enhanced by 60fps running constantly on most pcs. Textures is also much more detailed than dark souls 1 thanks for the improved game engine. Furthermore, the features provided by convenants and items all work well and match making seem to work constantly without the need to idle in the same location just to wait for an opponent.
The unique match making mechanic found in dark souls 2 is also different to the first game and instead of using soul levels as a measure of player strength, the game uses soul memory (SM) so that this way it can be more balanced in both pve and pvp.
The Story
Once again, player takes on the role of a nameless hero who became the bearer of curse and arrived in the plagued and dying land of Drangleic. Only by acquiring powerful souls of the ancient, the player will be able to confront the King and the Queen which will inturn free the hero from said curse. On the surface, dark souls 2 does not provide you with 'up your face' insight in what is going on around you as well as the lore and the background. However, smart players will soon find that all the information you seek will be found by talking to npcs scattered around the world as well as reading the description of every items found in the game. This provide enough solid fact to construct an excellent rpg and enough myths left for players to interpret.
Gameplay
First of all, I recommend players to have a game pad in order to play this game because keyboard and mouse control is awkward and often involve pressing keys located faraway from each other or unusual for video games. In terms of control I would say that the core mechanics is still solid and similar to the first game with minor improvements made but that is actually a good thing for veteran players and new players alike because it is intuitive in ways of switching weapons/shields and tools or spells. You only need to press the matched direction button on D-pad to allow switch of equipments. Dark souls 2 also introduced a equipment durability bar even thought it also existed in the first game. In dark souls 2 banging equipments against the wall will repel you and at the same time it will damage your equipment getting it low will be risky and lower its efficiency, breaking it will rendering it useless and require souls to be repaired by a black smith. Similarly, using heavy attack has also proven to degrade equipment at a fast pace.
Graphics
Before you go on and say anything, I know that buying a souls game for its graphics is not what the developer wanted us to do and im not saying dark souls 2 graphics is bad. In fact, it is great. Dark souls 2 features some of the most amazing visuals I have seen in recent years. From the mountain peak of Dragon Aerie to the land scape of Drangleic Castle and to the decaying undead crypt, it shows historical traits of traditional medieval fantasy perfectly and authentically portrayed in a video game. In addition to the graphic, the music is also really well composed from the intense and dangerous boss fight sound track to the grand, majestical and beautifully orchestrated music of a royal palace, the game really mixed and blended two features really well which will often get you pump and feel the sense of achievement after defeating the seemingly unbeatable bosses. Moreover, Dark souls 2 also features original voices given to the npcs of the game from the honorable knight of Mirrah to the traveller of Jugo as well as the lowly merchant of Volgen the game is really trying to create one hell of a unique and immersive experience for the player at every turn.
Difficulty
FromSoftware is notorious for creating difficult games that torment players and punishing them for little mistakes at the most important moment. There has also been rumours that Dark souls 2 is easier than Dark souls 1 and many features were dumbed down to make it more accessible to new players. In some way it is. However, what dark souls 2 provide with players is more freedom in what they want to do. For example if someone finds the game too easy or not challenging enough, they can use an item called 'Bonfire Ascetic' to increase the damage and the health of the enemies at the same time it reduces the amount of damage dealt by the player and if that is not enough, you can burn Bonfire Ascetics 8 times to cap the difficulty. If you wanna be even more hardcore you can also join the convenant of champions which will add another layer of difficulty and disable the co-op function to make the game solo only.
Verdict
Overall, I think that darksouls 2 is the best game of 2014 with amazing production value, replayability and accessbility. However, it could also be one of those game that only caters to a certain crowd of gamers.
Finally, If you enjoyed the first game, you will enjoy this game even more and if you enjoy S&M you will love this game

I was gonna write out a long and in-depth review but I realized there were enough of those already. If you're like me and think that well-designed and interesting boss fights and levels are the best part of the Souls series... well, this is not the game for you.
Demon's Souls was a literal masterpiece, and it's spiritual sequel Dark Souls was quite a game in its own right. While it never reached the peaks of quality boss design like Maneaters or False King; the interesting fights like Old Hero or Fool's Idol; the all-important educational fights like Phalanx or Tower Knight; or the emotionally charged encounter with Maiden Astraea... it still blows Dark Souls 2 out of the water.
I can count the well-crafted/interesting/emotional/memorable fights on one hand (it's 2, and both are ONLY interesting). Level design is acceptable but lacks consitency, the world is a scattered and poorly connected mess (Majula->Tower of Flame->No Man's Wharf/Earthen Peak->Iron Keep), enemy variety is lacking and their placement is haphazard at best, and the game is much easier than the predecessors.
It lacks the interesting lore of Demon's Souls (and Dark Souls) and the in-depth character stories of Dark Souls. The lore is... alright. There are some neat little tidbits but it relies too much on "mysterious" (The true nature of this sword is unknown, even to the
herself.) descriptions and references to Dark Souls to actually stand out. The characters, while at least somewhat engaging have no closure in their storylines whatsoever. All vendor-style NPCs end up in Majula and then just... stay there, never changing. The summonable NPCs just... stop being summonable with no real culmination of their story arc and the only character story with a real ending
is kind of a letdown, and a clear reference to the previous games.
HOWEVER! It is still a Souls game. Discovering each new area, beating the bosses, no matter how lame they may be, and admiring the cool environments is still a lot of fun. No matter how much I wish it were more like Demon's Souls and Dark Souls and no matter how much I complain about how bad it is... it's still a a pretty sweet ride and a wicked adventure.
So take this as you will. I was let down and underwhelmed when I looked back at the game, but still had a pretty good time (despite a few glaring issues with the bosses) during my first playthrough.
7.5/10

It's hard to describe what I like so much about this game and a few years ago I probably would have scoffed at the idea of even playing a game like this. I started playing ETS2 at a time in my life when I was having a lot of trouble with stress and anxiety and I found that listening to podcasts or audiobooks really helped, but I had to be doing something else like walking, driving, cleaning or doing the dishes in order to really get out of my head.
I finally decided to check out this game because of how often I heard it coming up as being one of the most relaxing games ever. I love long distance driving and since I work from home I barely drive anymore and I found that this game combined with a good podcast or audio book really was the most relaxing video game experience I had ever encountered. Driving through the different countries, checking out the sights, and completing a delivery just puts me in a better mood.
Even now when my stress level has evened out a good bit I still love completing a delivery or two and expanding my slowly growing trucking empire. The sim aspects of buying garages, trucks, hiring drivers, and training them really adds to the overall experience if it's something you even want to engage with (since you really don't have to do this part at all and can just complete random deliveries). You start to become attached to your truck and slowly add to it as you make more money.
It's also really refreshing to see the dev here constantly releasing new DLC in the form of whole new countries to drive in and smaller fun DLC like heavy cargo. They work closely with the community both here and with American Truck Simulator to release beta updates that can include large free updates to the game like random encounters or better GPS. This is a game I will contiue to play for years to come.
This is my medication. Let it be yours.

Truck game? I don't even like truck in real life and I always hate it when i got stuck behind one in a one lane road. So I tried the demo of this game to see whats all the hubbub is about. And from being annoyed by truck, this game helps me to form respect and appreciation toward truck driver and somehow annoyed at myself as i see myself in the AI behaviour in game. Like "WHY THE HECK ARE YOU SLOWING DOWN IN THE MIDDLE OF THE ROAD NOW I NEED TO GEAR DOWN AND BUILD UP AGAIN ALL THOSE LOST MOMENTUM YOU PIECE OF..." now i drive my car and react properly with trucks on the road. So i bought the game and the journey begins...
It is a very relaxing game that I always fired up during weekend nights. But it also can be challenging at times like hauling the oversize cargo with steerable axle and then trying to reverse park it in one go. Some of the good points about the game that I can think of:-
-The map is huge and it's getting bigger every year.
-New trucks and tuning packs are introduced every now and then.
-New trailer and challenges are introduced as well (heavy cargo, high power cargo, double trailer, and soon to come special cargo)
-Mods:-
+Huge list of mods with multiplayer mod stands out at the top (TruckersMP). You get to have a delivery convoy with your friends or stranger and witness some funny stuff on the road. And it's fun to chat using the CB radio or using other 3rd party voice chat app like ts or discord. I've also joined virtual trucking company and make deliveries based on requirement of a virtual company. If you like role-playing, TruckersMP mod really offer that part in this area.
+Map mods is just unbelievable and the attention to details in some of the map mods is just astonishing (ProMods, RusMap, TSM, Eldorado... to name a few).  I've driven in snowy region of Iceland and desert of North Africa.
+Truck Mod and trailer Mod. The truck that you want to drive isn't in vanilla game? chances are there is a mod that allow you to use that model of truck out there. My fave is Volvo VNL with Baobab tree trailer climbing mountain of Eldorado Map mod.
+Truck skin and trailer skin, company name and skin, gas station brand name and fuel price. All these are mod-able that it helps in immersion.
-Constant update and development of the game. You can tell that they really love the game and that's all I need from a developer.
And that's only what i can think on top of my head. I'm sure there are a lot more points that I haven't mentioned.
But like any other game, there are things that can be improved such as:- (in my opinion)
- the graphic. The graphic is still limited to what DirectX 9 can offer. I'd imagine that having this upgraded will tremendously improve the quality of the game in term of graphic and performance.
- the ability to own your own trailer and pick up cargo from factory and deliver it. There is still no option for this yet.
- damage system and physics. The damage system is still pretty basic, like if i get into an accident, when i go to service station i can see what the percentage of damage for different part of the truck. I completely fixed the engine and transmission. I ignored the cabin and wheel damage. After leaving the service station, my truck engine died with message "engine malfunction" when i know it's completely fixed. It's just the tire and cabin that is still damaged. So it kinda defeat the purpose of having option on what to repair at the service station... oh and it would be nice to have visual effect of a damaged truck. Like my cabin is 100% damaged but in game, it looks brand new and shiny all the time.
- attention to detail. For example it would be nice if we can interact with the interior of the truck like pushing button on the GPS nav, radio, roll down the window, go out of the truck to attach/detach the trailer. And also, there is still no cable connection between the trailer and truck even though the wires and cable is hanging behind the truck, I guess they are connected via wifi?...
well these are just my opinion. Whatever it is I'm still enjoying the game with my friends. :)

I played(and completed)this game on PS2 before,and I can say that this is an amazing game ^_^
I remember how this game just captivated me when I first played it on PS2,because of the amazing music,characters,etc in it
The plot(in a summary): The President of Georgia is assasinated,allowing billionaire Kombayn Nikoladze(main antagonist)to seize power by bloodless coup d'etat. Sam FIsher(the character you play as),former Navy SEAL officer and Persian Gulf War,is recruited by the NSA to work with it's new division,Third Echelon. He is dispatched to Tbilisi to investigate the disappearence of 2 CIA officers. He finds out that a man named Vyacheslav Grinko(another antagonist)removed their subdermal tracking devices and tracks him down to the defense ministry,finding out that Nikoladze is doing an illegal operation in Azerbaijan. Sam goes to an oil rig and finds that NATO forces are sending fighter jets to bomb the rig,he finds Piotr Lejava and gets his suitcase,which has a laptop containing an encryption key to"The Ark". The information is revealed to have come from a mole in the CIA,so Sam goes to the CIA HQ to investigate,and interrogates Mitchell Dougherty,finding that his OCD caused him to backup data on an insecure laptop,which was exploited by a network owned by Kalinatek. He goes to Kalinatek and finds Ivan,and gets his encryption key. He goes to the Chinese Embassy in Myanmar and finds that the Chinese general Feirong is working with Nikoladze,and that American soldiers are going to be executed on live TV. He rescues the soldiers,and kills Grinko in a firefight. He goes back to the Chinese Embassy and forces Feirong to shre information stored on his computer,which reveals that Nikoladze fled back to Georgia. Sam goes back to Georgia and finds Nikoladze in the Presidential Palace,where he narrowly escapes being killed,with Lambert's arranged blackout saving him. He then assassinates Nikoladze after learning that he is disclosing The Ark's location.
The music is amazing.
The characters are amazing,especially Lambert and Grimsdottir.
The stealth mechanics are pretty good too(even if the AI can be wonky at times)
Anyways,overall this is an amazing game that I recommend to everyone.

SMITE carries out a new perspective on familiar game design which makes everything feel fresh again. For example, the way SMITE has the camera behind your character instead of viewing from a birds eye view drastically transforms familiar MOBA mechanics, creating an interesting and challenging take on a genre that rarely strays from common guidelines. Beyond the new angle, SMITE has a range of features to help ease new players in, along with its entertaining different game modes that all present special rewards for those who stick around.
Smite can often end up feeling more like a third-person action RPG than a MOBA, and that’s the greatest change in gameplay. Using W, A, S, and D to move feels natural, and it’s engaging and very tense to get up close and personal in an enemy’s face. Combat is much more complex in a different way than in other MOBAs – your position and the direction you’re looking feels so important when playing as a melee character, and every ranged ability in Smite is an aimed skill shot, INCLUDING YOUR AUTO ATTACKS.
Minions in Smite act a little different to other MOBAs, as they still defend their Gods with very hard-hitting attacks early on, but what is different is when they're killed everyone in the area earns experience and gold – not just the person who scored the last hit. While last-hitting is a test of skill in other MOBAs, not having to worry about it in Smite encourages more team fights against Gods rather than constant item farming. That being said a slight gold increase is rewarded for players who last hit minions among the minion wave.
The god selection and lore is what really attracted me to SMITE as they are all borrowed from seven different ancient religions. Personally I feel the developers at Hi-Rez did a wonderful job incorporating their familiar mythological backgrounds straight into tactical MOBA roles – the Greek demigod Hercules is a burly, boxing style melee character, while Zeus hurls lightning at his enemies. I was pleased with the huge variety between the now 69 available Gods(at the time of writing this), and their impressively detailed models. Some flashier abilities, like Norse god Thor’s Ultimate, Anvil of Dawn, work especially well with the third-person camera because they launch you up into the sky. They’re thrilling to execute, and it’s neat to see the map from another perspective.
The developers also go into great detail when designing skins, wether it will be a funny skin or a serious/bad♥♥♥♥♥skin. The developers really do make a lot of effort with them. You'll find the more expensive skins have some very cool effects which can change the way you use the ability. Although the gems can seem at little pricey if you get attached to the game its a worthy investment.
In my experience the game is one of the more fun and enjoyable MOBAs with the ability to certainly outplay your oponent. I feel the ranked or even pro scene never kicked off as competetively as they intended, but its a great way to spend a few hours with your friends.

What is Townopolis?
Townopolis is a casual sandbox/scenario based neighborhood planning game. It follows the traditions of the sub-genre of casual games, adding nothing new but doing well what it does. Mostly.
The sub-genre has you as planner on a map of a small neighborhood where you build houses, upgrade them, add features to them etc.
The houses generate income which is used to generate more income by building more houses. All the while you have a small resource management aspect with one or few resources (in this case one, named "materials") and builders. Each level has a time limit in which a certain goal must be fulfilled, for example in the first non-tutorial scenario you have 10 minutes to build a supermarket and have 6,500 dollars income per month (in reality: every few seconds) and ten upgraded houses (as optional goal). So you need 12 workers, lots of material, a supermarket building blueprint/license and you must make enough space for your building project. Things are made harder by the fact that there are two sawmills and some forests that can't be removed. The sawmills produce unhappiness to everyone living nearby, as does the supermarket. Houses grouped together are more happy because people like to live with other people. Which technically is true for not everyone, but in the game it is that way.
Controls:
The entire game is controlled with the mouse. The controls are explained ingame, but pretty much everything is done through a contextual menu on the main screen or the license/blueprint menu where time is paused. Alternatively you have a visible pause button as well.
Graphics:
The graphics are isometric, so you see everything and can act quickly. The UI fits with the isometric theme, but at the beginning can be overwhelming. However, since things unlock one by one you can learn the buttons all without complications.
Sound:
The sound is standard. There is nothing special, it just is forgettable music that runs in the background which doesn't become annoying but will also not stick with you after exiting the game.
Gameplay:
The gameplay was described above in the sub-genre description. There are additionally some trophies to be earned that are also unlocking Steam Achievements. Apart from the usual ones that can just be grinded or naturally earned while playing, there is also one for completing the campaign and getting all gold stars (for par times). The campaign has 24 levels, which are enough for a few hours of gameplay. There is also a sandbox mode, which has an achievement to finish 12 missions or scenarios in it.
Overall the game can be recommended for fans of the genre. The sale price of 1 Euro or your local equivalent is good enough to pick it up and have some fun. You just should expect a rather casual game, if you don't know the sub-genre already.
Recommended: For genre fans

This is a simple, goal orientated town management sim. Well worth the 3.99 USD (you can also find it cheaper in the Indie Gala bundle)
I wrote something about it on my blog:

Once again, I wish there was a "maybe" option. The reason I gave it a thumbs down is the way the game is marketed.
"Build your own town and make heaps of money in this addictive strategy game. Construct an idyllic neighborhood with plenty of houses and keep your residents happy by providing all services they need, and they will reward you with a tidy profit."
While that statement is completely true, it gives the impression the game is a city builder and a lot of the reviews below are calling it a city builder, but it's not.
Townopolis is a cross between a puzzle game and a time management game. The theme might be construction, but the game is about figuring out the optimal arrangement of your buildings to achieve the goals each level sets you. There is no sprawling map or freedom to build. You are provided with a small map consisting of tiles. Some you can build on, some you can clear and then build on, others can't be built on (factories etc.) and/or cause negative happiness to the neighbouring tiles. You want to keep the residents happy, and every building type has positive or negative effects to those in the neighbouring tiles.
Now that is out of the way. I bought the game because it was cheap and I love city builders. To that end, I was disappointed. The game, however, is simple to learn, isn't very complex, there is no resource gathering other than waiting for rent to arrive, and if you like puzzle games and approach it as such, it's very casual but worth checking out.
The only real negative I had was the frequency buildings broke down. As soon as you get to 8 or more buildings, it seems one or two of them start breaking down at random every few seconds, so you have to frantically repair each of them manually and the game just becomes about time management at that point. Not to mention how annoying the break down sound effect is, when you are hearing it every 3 or 4 seconds.
It's cheap, it's casual, it can be fun, but buy it because it's a puzzle game, not a city builder, and you'll avoid disappointment.

Genre of casual games has long enjoyed popularity, but until recently avoided Steam. Now its number constantly raises and being relatively popular, distributors do not hesitate to re-release older titles too. Townopolis, originally from 2008, by Slovak team Lonely Troops is a good example, how to do it right.
Townopolis is a casual strategy game that does not set any high goals in terms of sophisticated strategic options, but only for basic entertainment. If you are one of those people who like to build & build, modernise or even demolish, then this game is for you. This game will take you on activities in all mentioned directions. Everything revolves constantly around buildings. Games starts with just the basic types of buildings and then gradually add other options of structures and stuff.
In each of the 24 levels in total you have to focus on different aspects of building. Sometimes you have to pay attention to high number of inhabitants, sometimes their satisfaction or high earnings of your developer. During construction you need to improve buildings and equipment, purchase of materials and licenses for building features and of course hire workers.
Initially, it is possible to build on already cleared area, but soon you’ll need to find a place for yourself, cutting down forests first, clear old abandoned houses and useless buildings etc. Each advanced structures, like the post office or supermarket requires a license. They tend to be quite expensive and you need to have built many high earning houses to afford it. Each building can be upgraded by star rating. The more stars, the more money. Satisfaction of your inhabitants is expressed by yellow smiley and angry ones by red smiley. Dissatisfaction can be reversed by building up structures in the vicinity or by fulfilling people’s needs.
The first few levels are just a tutorial where you learn the basic principles and mechanisms of game and you’re told what to do. Then you have to decide for yourself what will be the development strategy to accomplish all objectives in the desired limit to get gold star and trophy for each level. I needed to replay a few levels to get all achievements.
Graphics corresponds to the genre and its time, but it’s still enjoyable in comparison to some newer games. The game can be played comfortably in the window and the background music is nicely flowing during play. It’s nice to see Steam Cloud feature too.
Overall, the game can be recommended to every fan of casual strategies and casual players in general.

I was gifted the first game about a year ago and it quickly went from completely unknown to me to being one of the best games I've ever played.
This game contains all the things that made the last one great, along with an entirely new set of areas, hundreds of new weapons, armor, and spells, and nine new covenants (which are most usually a sort of player faction in pvp).
There are also ~30 bosses, each with a different kind of design and backstory. Speaking of the story: it is one of the most interesting ways to present one. Most of the story is uncovered through such simple things as loot placement, area design, and item descriptions. NPC dialogue shouldn't be glossed over either: it can be easily skipped over or ignored, but it usually contains important (or sometimes blatant) hints towards your next objective or to the lore itself.
The level design is still incredibly well done. You are almost always capable of choosing between 2-4 choices at a time when deciding where to go next. This non-linear model is contrasted against the more linear design of the individual levels, which allows them to fine tune the path through the area for the best gameplay experience.
The combat itself is quite good as well. All actions deduct from a regenerative stamina bar, which means you must be strategic in order to plan out your actions. This usually means that the PvP involves exploiting mistakes that your opponent makes. The wide variety of weapons (anything from a katana to a scythe is available, with multiple weapons usually taking up each type of weapon moveset) allows for some specialization in a fight, as well as the four different branches of magic.
Online play involves PvP or co-op, where you are capable of either helping someone else along through their game as a phantom, or invading their world as a dark spirit in order to fight them. Covanants alter these two main components of multiplayer into many different forms.
Many of these features I've described may seem like it should be a standard feature of a game, but I've found that at least some of these can be done away with or poorly executed in many games.
Features like NG+, multiplayer, and completionism can make this game's replayability last fo days yo.

It's been more than a decade since the original release of Splinter Cell. Does the game still hold up as one of the pioneer hardcore stealth games to this day? ...Yes, yes it does.
You play as Sam Fisher, a Splinter Cell in the secretive OPs agency known as 3rd Echelon. You are shadow, invisible, a ghost...and an excellent infiltrator. Should you be captured, you would cease to exist to the general public. With the credo realized, you must play this game as if the light will burn you alive. You will slowly creep through various locales finding ways to circumvent guards or silently take them out. You are provided a generous amount of tools and gadgets to help you in this cause. Be it sticky cameras, wall mines, to snake cameras...you will always find a use for the tinkets possessed by Sam.
The game is pretty unforgiving in terms of stealth. There are 5 ratings of exposure to light you can be in at once and depending on your current position will determine how fast a guard realizes it is a bionic commando versus a mosquito buzzing around. There is also an invisible noise detection level which varies depending on the surface you creep upon. You can flatten yourself against a wall to be even more hidden and use distractions such as light switches to pull unexpecting guards to their sleepy fate.
One aspect that still amazes me is that you can sneak through most levels without ever touching a guard or being detected. Granted, since this game needs to have a little bit of variation from the normal stealth routine...you'll find yourself in a couple of mandatory shootouts. These occurances are few and far between and help break the typical slow creep and crawl you'll be doing through most of the game. Music and sound play a big part with music dynamically ramping up in intensity when guards are becoming alerted to your prescence to heavy rock when a battle is unavoidable. Ambience of halogen lights and crickets chirping as well as cars passing by will be your typical tune when you are a ghost.
Techincally speaking, the game looks great if you do a few simple tweaks in the game's .ini files. I personally could not see the CG cutscenes without sacrificing my graphical tweaks but just watch them on YouTube and you'll still get the full effect. A small price to pay for 1080p and anti-alising. The game runs stable at 60fps and looks fairly decent for its time. Volumetric lighting and partial physics exist here.
I can fully recommend Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell for anyone looking for an actual stealth game where slow and steady certainly and almost always wins the race.

SMITE carries out a new perspective on familiar game design which makes everything feel fresh again. For example, the way SMITE has the camera behind your character instead of viewing from a birds eye view drastically transforms familiar MOBA mechanics, creating an interesting and challenging take on a genre that rarely strays from common guidelines. Beyond the new angle, SMITE has a range of features to help ease new players in, along with its entertaining different game modes that all present special rewards for those who stick around.
Smite can often end up feeling more like a third-person action RPG than a MOBA, and that’s the greatest change in gameplay. Using W, A, S, and D to move feels natural, and it’s engaging and very tense to get up close and personal in an enemy’s face. Combat is much more complex in a different way than in other MOBAs – your position and the direction you’re looking feels so important when playing as a melee character, and every ranged ability in Smite is an aimed skill shot, INCLUDING YOUR AUTO ATTACKS.
Minions in Smite act a little different to other MOBAs, as they still defend their Gods with very hard-hitting attacks early on, but what is different is when they're killed everyone in the area earns experience and gold – not just the person who scored the last hit. While last-hitting is a test of skill in other MOBAs, not having to worry about it in Smite encourages more team fights against Gods rather than constant item farming. That being said a slight gold increase is rewarded for players who last hit minions among the minion wave.
The god selection and lore is what really attracted me to SMITE as they are all borrowed from seven different ancient religions. Personally I feel the developers at Hi-Rez did a wonderful job incorporating their familiar mythological backgrounds straight into tactical MOBA roles – the Greek demigod Hercules is a burly, boxing style melee character, while Zeus hurls lightning at his enemies. I was pleased with the huge variety between the now 69 available Gods(at the time of writing this), and their impressively detailed models. Some flashier abilities, like Norse god Thor’s Ultimate, Anvil of Dawn, work especially well with the third-person camera because they launch you up into the sky. They’re thrilling to execute, and it’s neat to see the map from another perspective.
The developers also go into great detail when designing skins, wether it will be a funny skin or a serious/bad♥♥♥♥♥skin. The developers really do make a lot of effort with them. You'll find the more expensive skins have some very cool effects which can change the way you use the ability. Although the gems can seem at little pricey if you get attached to the game its a worthy investment.
In my experience the game is one of the more fun and enjoyable MOBAs with the ability to certainly outplay your oponent. I feel the ranked or even pro scene never kicked off as competetively as they intended, but its a great way to spend a few hours with your friends.

The biggest draw of ESO is undoubtedly its combat system which blends your typical MMO combat with more involved combat like the Elder Scrolls (ES) series is known for. .

The "Tamriel Unlimited" update really brought the game to where it needed to be to be called an Elder Scrolls game.  This update added a justice system like you would see in any other ES game.  The "Guild Shop" feature replaces the auction house system that has become standard fare in most MMOs. Guild shops are set up in market stalls in every major city and allow members of that guild to sell their items from that stall, it results in players actively going to the market rather than standing around the same auctioneer all day and really makes the cities feel more alive with player activity.  This update also added the dye system in which armor dyes are unlocked based on achievements, for example fighters guild red can be unlocked for ranking up in the fighters guild.
Also you can launch the game without being signed into steam which is nice.

This game went from being god awful to being shockingly good.
The Crime and Justice system is the first of its kind I've seen in an MMO. The crafting system is something I think all MMO's could learn from.
For those expecting Skyrim with friends... Its not that. As a matter of fact I would say that, besides the setting, this game has more in common with Fable than Elder Scrolls. There's even a quest which features the voice actor of the Fable Guildmaster that has a jab at how he was handled in Fable. Thar archery system in this is handled nearly identically to the bows in Fable as well.
On its own its a decent MMO with an incredible player driven PVP battlefield. Players can erect siege engines, destroy towers and buildings. I havent spent enough time in the PVP yet but what I did spend was mindblowing. We tried to take over a farm from the aldmeri dominion with a small strike force and one catapult. We nearly succeeded too, but the enemy got reinforced and we had to pull out. Its a weird cross between planetside and a typical MMO in the PVP.
So far, beyond a couple outliers, the fetch quests have been well explained and voiced, making it feel like I'm not just grabbing 8 macguffins for my next level. The combat is very active and I have found I cannot dual screen like I can in Quickbar based MMOs. I need to be focused in combat or else I will die, which is a refreshing change.
The quick travel in this is just explained by "MAGIC" and you can either use a wayshrine to travel for free or use a small amount of gold if you cant reach a shrine safely. I find the teleport much nicer than watching my character go all across the terrain like in other MMOs.
With the advent of Buy to Play instead of a subscription I imagined they would end up with a SWTOR like second and third class citizen model, where XP is reduced for non subs and you cant do things like dye your armor. THIS IS NOT THE CASE. THERE IS NO SECOND CLASS CITIZENSHIP MODEL IN THIS GAME. If you buy it, you own all of it. No Subscriber only areas, no VIP lounges, just the whole ham MMO. Subscribers will have access to any DLC that drops (That nonsubs can buy), but in my opinion that is absolutely fair.
So far, I am extremely impressed with this turnaround and hope many of you will play this with me.

The Elder Scrolls Online: Tamriel Unlimited is a fantastic game with a lot of content, a good community (from what I've experience), and good customization. It is definately a lot more improved that when initally reviewed, and thus I believe it does not deserve the hate it receives.
Firstly, I have played the game since beta. While I did not play a huge chunk of the game, I played enough to be able to say it was somewhat lacking, and while fun, it did bore me out fairly quickly. When the game launched, I didn't not get the game, and had only heard bad things about the game. It was only after a few months later did I eventually decide to dive back into the world of Tamriel, after hundreds of hours of playing Skyrim. The game had improved drastically since beta, and I truely recommend anyone who has not played the game to give it a try, especially now that the game has gotten rid of the Monthly Subscriptions.
On that topic, no the game is not "pay-to-win" due to the reduction of the monthly subscritpions. As of now, the only things you can buy are Mounts, Pets and cosmetics with no plans to add a pay-to-win element into the Crown Store.
The biggest thing you must remember when looking at this game is that it is NOT Skyrim Online. The faster you get that notion out of your head, the better the game becomes. And while it is not Skyrim Online, it is still a really fun game, and probably the closest you'd get to such a game. The game is heavily quest based in the leveling process, but they're relatively fun quests and everyone is fully voiced.
The customization in this game is really enjoyable with the way you are able to pick any weapon, take various skills, pick morphs, wear any armour, it's extremely fun to experiement with different armour sets and weapons, trying to find that perfect build for your playstyle (though looking online for builds isn't a bad thing, either). I have had a ton of fun over multiple characters with different classes just waiting to get new skill points in order to try new things.
While this may not apply to everyone, I have found the community to generally be really good. There are probably going to be trolls, or generally dislikable people along the way, but for the most part I have found the chats to be nice, and the guilds to be pleasant. Speaking about the chats, they are not filled with spam on buying gold online that I find in a lot of other MMO's, and they're actually filled with people actively talking (for however long that may last).
All in all, I believe this game is well worth the price and is definately a fun experience. It is different to other MMO's and I enjoy both playing in first person and third person, though I had to change the FOV to 130 in first person (and even then I would have prefered a bit more). I'd recommend this to anyone looking for some entertainment, and definately to someone who was put off from getting it due to the negativity that it once had.

This is what I liked and would like to see more of ( Reviews for me come in final products ).  I will update this post with more information as I play through Campaign and Multiplayer. I also hope to screen shot the game as I go so I can show some of the great improvements and updates over the mod version. Which are easily found on the fun and always exciting railway ride into Black Mesa.
What I liked that wasn't in the mod :
+ That it's finally on steam
+ Multiplayer is fast paced and tons of fun ( reminds me of the old shooters, Quake, Time Splitters etc...)
+ Can customize the looks for your character in multiplayer ( I am sure the community is already modding the Teletubbie skin into the game. Wouldn't mind seeing one with a headcrap in a MP match  lol )
+ The graphics are a lot better than the mod with new textures, models, and particle effects
+ Game seems to run better under the newly forked game engine ( must have taken them a while to make the changes )
+ Day 1 mod support ( maps from original half life and other poppular source engine games already being ported over by the community
+ MP maps so far feel very well done
+ The new voices added to the game are very nicely done
+ Controller Support
+ Devs seem very committed to the community ( Oftenly they play in the matches themselves, taking feedback from players )
+ Fast patches to the game from devs, already seen a decent size one today on bug fixes.
+ Mod tools with steam workshop
+ Completely new AI for the marines ( Miles better than the mod )
+ The music is done well and placed in situations where it actually adds to the feeling and atomsphere.
+ The vast detail on almost every non imprtant object in the game ( there was times I found my self looking at non animate objects. For example in the begining of the game I found a motherboard on the floor fully decked out with Ram, Cpu Fan, and all the other stuff you would find on a real one. Even the fire extingusihers have everything down to the small fine print you find in real life. Extreme care went into almost every single object the team has added in the game )
+ Flow of the game never feels too dull or to repetitive much like the original game they caught the atomosphere
+ Animations on some things in the mod no longer look weird and clunky
+ Crouch jumping feels way better in this version
+ Weapon models and
+ Very funny and well though out homages to the original game
Overall I think there is quite a big difference from the mod ( with the limited 15 hours I have had playing it ) and I am happy to be an Early Access owner ( much like backing a dev on kickstarter ) of Black Mesa. I played the mod so many times through, because I loved the take back feeling it provided faithfully to the original.
Things I would like to see in the future and improvementso on current features:
Co-op campaign ( Like in the HL version on PS2. I do think that it will be modded in by the community very fast )
/Voice chat with mute and other various options
/More MP maps that offer more game styles ( Currently on the official servers Death Match and Team Death Match only )
/More language versions for other countries ( For non speaking english people )
/Cloud Saves to the steam cloud ( was hoping for this on launch, not a big deal though since around 30% of my 270+ steam games use it )
/A better improved close captioning or subtitles option. I think the current version is really ugly with the grey box the text sits on.
/ Obviously Xen
/ Some area's where lighting could be improved a little
/ Changes when you pick up a weapon in MP it auto changes to it ( Not sure if this is a bug or a design decision )
/ More voiced announcements in multiplayer ( the current ones are awesome btw )
Honestly I could nick pick for days both good and things I would like improved on. This is what I have come up with for now, and think even in it's Early Access it's worth the asking price. I highly suggest this to people who want to relive one of the best remakes of a game in recent years. Those who never played the mod this version will suit you the best. Those who have and wondered " Is this really worth it ?" That's up to you! I did and this is what I thought! I spent 13 hours trying to kill the damn horse. There are no consequences in this game. This warped reality will have you staring at your screen like some sort of zombie waiting for that glorious, "You horse has died, you lose. You are also a horrible monster." However, that moment will never arrive.

For real though, this is one of the best horse games I have ever played. Don't let the title fool you, this game is legit. This is not your ordinary, boring af, 3-day event competition with no story horse game. This game has a real story with a cast of very interesting, well rounded characters, each with in-depth backstories you can discover. Yeah, you heard me. A horse game with actual characters that talk about actual things with an actual plot. This is the real deal. Real talk.
The plot has got some cool mystery elements, lots of scandal, social commentary, romance if you choose, and it adapts to how you play the game. There are multiple paths and multiple endings. Do you mostly care about eventing and breeding horses? You can choose not to concern yourself with solving the mystery and the focus of the plot will shift.  The interesting side character backstories? You only discover them if you chose to interact with them. Very adaptive. Yes. Good. Encourages the player to interact with the in-game world. Yes. Good!
Since the the story is a mystery it can get a little intense at points and might get a little bit scary for some younger players.
This game is pretty gosh darn ugly, but fortunately, it is very easily modded. The textures, text, sounds, meshes/models, and animations are all there for you to fiddle around with. Unfortunately, if you can't mod the files yourself, you gotta deal with the ugliness because there are no mods out there for this game. It was 2007. A more innocent time. A simpler time. An uglier time. Much uglier. Very ugly. Bad. Mouths do not move, some people don't blink, the saddle clips through the horse, the girl clips through the saddle AND the horse, the chestnut horses are not chestnut and the cream horses are NOT cream. Currently trying to find a way to upload some of my mods to the steam workshop for other people that are bothered by these things.
There's lots of neat stuff in this game. You got all sorts of collectibles, sidequests, and secrets. It's got a stat system, a training system, a breeding system, a rider skill system,  an affection/morale system and each of these systems effects your game in tiny ways. Very fun. Yes. good.
On foot, the controls can feel very clunky. On horseback, things are easy-peasy. You can configure the keys to your taste, but not all of them. Gotta go to the config.ini to change them if you can't handle the good ol' 2007 clunk controls. They are very bad.
Like most horse games, this has a ridiculously long grooming sequence. Unlike most horse games from the time, you can actually rotate the camera and brush the ENTIRE horse instead of just one side. The shower option was actually developed in hell itself by the devil. I have proof. I can confirm this. There is also a hoof-picking sequence in which you have to avoid hitting the frog or else the horse will scream VERY LOUDLY. AMAZING! REVOLUTIONARY! Yes. Good! Oh, and get this, GET THIS: you get emmerse yourself in an AMAZING FIRST PERSON STALL MUCKING EXPERIENCE! YES!
There is a training and trust bar you can fill up. The activities you need to do to fill them up are awful. The lunging minigame is very confusing and very difficult. Actually had to look up a tutorial. Very hard. You need a good mouse. The other minigame is just memorization based but there is a very loud buzzer noise that plays if you answer incorrectly. Very scary. Mute your volume for that. You will pee yourself. I know this.
Ugly yes, but a quality horse game with a lot of depth and character, which is saying a lot because horse games are notoriously bad. The stat system is well made, but simple and won't confuse younger players. More realistic than most horse games targeted at a younger audience, but realism fans will likely not rejoice. This game has something for every age group. Good enough that you can genuinely enjoy it, and bad enough that you can still make fun of it the whole time. Very poorly made, but that's part of what I like about it.

Ok, so first let me say that all of the past reviews are just biased and people whining about no dedicated servers.  People have been saying that it is 2014 and we need dedicated servers.  No, we don't NEED them because the game functions fine without them.  Yes, we should have them but does not having them hurt us in any way?  A lot of players whine about the lag but I rarely have a low ping.  I don't know why everyone else lags so much.  Ok, so now onto the game
Sledgehammer claims that the new exo-suits "revolutionize" the game, the added verticality is nice but the exo-suits are merely a refreshing twist to the Call of Duty franchise.  Sledgehammer brings back a few old weapons like the AK-12 and they also plan on re-modeling and reconstructing some old maps that we loved from the past installments.  They also didn't just copy and paste the killstreaks and I feel that there is actually some variation in this new game.
The weapons are pretty balanced, the assault rifle nerf has made the BAL-27 less dominant and gives other weapon types like the weak SMGs a chance in close quarters gunfights.  The new loot and character customization system is great.  It isn't like Borderlands 2 loot but it adds some variation between weapons.  There are different types of loot, Enlisted being the most common and Elite being the rarest.  You earn loot from supply drops that can be earned ingame.  Weapon variants buff and weaken the weapon in certain aspects but if combined with the right attachments, can be devastating.  This brings me to the attachments, once again Sledgehammer has put effort into making there be LOTS of variation between the different types of grips, sights etc.  The character customization allows you to personalize your character, there are many different "outfits" that you can unlock and all of them look BADASS.
The biggest failure of gaming history (Ghosts) has made me lose ALL FAITH WHATSOEVER in the Call of Duty franchise itself.  I am glad that I gave it ONE last chance.  In the end, this game is a refreshing twist to the Call of Duty franchise that still has room for improvement.  I imagine within the next few months that this game will be great and balanced.  I am happy to be able to reccomend a Call of Duty title again.
Even though there is room for improvement, this game adds a refreshing twist to CoD

SMITE carries out a new perspective on familiar game design which makes everything feel fresh again. For example, the way SMITE has the camera behind your character instead of viewing from a birds eye view drastically transforms familiar MOBA mechanics, creating an interesting and challenging take on a genre that rarely strays from common guidelines. Beyond the new angle, SMITE has a range of features to help ease new players in, along with its entertaining different game modes that all present special rewards for those who stick around.
Smite can often end up feeling more like a third-person action RPG than a MOBA, and that’s the greatest change in gameplay. Using W, A, S, and D to move feels natural, and it’s engaging and very tense to get up close and personal in an enemy’s face. Combat is much more complex in a different way than in other MOBAs – your position and the direction you’re looking feels so important when playing as a melee character, and every ranged ability in Smite is an aimed skill shot, INCLUDING YOUR AUTO ATTACKS.
Minions in Smite act a little different to other MOBAs, as they still defend their Gods with very hard-hitting attacks early on, but what is different is when they're killed everyone in the area earns experience and gold – not just the person who scored the last hit. While last-hitting is a test of skill in other MOBAs, not having to worry about it in Smite encourages more team fights against Gods rather than constant item farming. That being said a slight gold increase is rewarded for players who last hit minions among the minion wave.
The god selection and lore is what really attracted me to SMITE as they are all borrowed from seven different ancient religions. Personally I feel the developers at Hi-Rez did a wonderful job incorporating their familiar mythological backgrounds straight into tactical MOBA roles – the Greek demigod Hercules is a burly, boxing style melee character, while Zeus hurls lightning at his enemies. I was pleased with the huge variety between the now 69 available Gods(at the time of writing this), and their impressively detailed models. Some flashier abilities, like Norse god Thor’s Ultimate, Anvil of Dawn, work especially well with the third-person camera because they launch you up into the sky. They’re thrilling to execute, and it’s neat to see the map from another perspective.
The developers also go into great detail when designing skins, wether it will be a funny skin or a serious/bad♥♥♥♥♥skin. The developers really do make a lot of effort with them. You'll find the more expensive skins have some very cool effects which can change the way you use the ability. Although the gems can seem at little pricey if you get attached to the game its a worthy investment.
In my experience the game is one of the more fun and enjoyable MOBAs with the ability to certainly outplay your oponent. I feel the ranked or even pro scene never kicked off as competetively as they intended, but its a great way to spend a few hours with your friends.

TLDR; Much, MUCH better then at release. Give it a chance if you like MMORPG/RPG or the Elder scrolls!
-----------------
I played the beta and found it to be decent at best, it was definately not worth a subscription fee. Now however, with the subscription fee gone, it is worth it. If you're into elder scrolls or RPG/MMORPG's, then you should give this a shot! Especially now with the subscription gone.
The PvE questlines are really good, everything is voice acted. The main quest is good and immersive and the sidequests have a nice amount of lore and immersion put into them.
With the recently added crime system, playing as a sneaky thief is really fun. Stealing stuff, breaking into houses to steal their riches and even leveling within the thieves is much fun to be had. I really hope its just the top of the iceberg of whats to come!
The PvP is the most fun I've had in a while. I'm a huge PvP player, and while there is room for improvements and polish, the large scale PvP is still one of the best experiences so far. Setting up siege weapons on the walls, breaking down the gate or the enemy walls and capture their precious keeps! One of the best part is that you can level up by doing PvP, get gear and gold!
The character customization is awesome. You can basically become whatever character you want. Start as a mage and wear heavy armor, fight with a two handed axe to become a Battlemage for example. Any class can use and specialize in any armor/weapon, no matter which class you chose.
The Crown store which was added due to the removal of subscription fee, has *so far* not showed signs of becoming Pay 2 Win. Its mostly costumes and mount skins and stuff like that. I personally really hope for more cosmetic effects, especially for skills/spells!
There is probably more I'm forgetting right now, and while there is still room for improvements, as always, it is a much better game than it was at release. If you're in the "should I try it?" stage, then I would definately recommend it. Its in a much better stage than it was at release.
